articles.headline: Israeli strike kills Palestinian schoolboy in Deir el-Balah
articles.title: Education under fire: Gaza’s children face death on their way to school
articles.summary: Fourteen-year-old Mohammed Hamad was killed by an Israeli strike on October 17 while walking home from school in the al-Baraka neighbourhood of Deir el-Balah with his younger brother Abdullah. According to the Gaza Ministry of Health, escalating violence near the Yellow Line has resulted in numerous child casualties and school disruptions, leaving surviving students like injured fourth-grader Suad Abd Rabbo in urgent need of overseas medical treatment.
articles.description: Children have faced Israeli bombs and sniper fire since the academic year resumed in Gaza.

articles.headline: US approves possible sale of 500 Patriot missiles to Ukraine
articles.title: US greenlights $2.1bn Patriot missile sale to Ukraine
articles.summary: The United States State Department announced the approval of a potential 2.1 billion dollar sale of 500 Patriot PAC-3 missiles and related support to Ukraine. According to officials, the interceptors are not expected to be delivered until the early 2030s. Kyiv will fund the purchase using contributions from Canada, Germany, and Norway, alongside European Union loan funds, while Lockheed Martin serves as the principal contractor.
articles.description: Deal would be one of the most significant steps to supply defensive weapons to Kyiv since ​Trump took office in 2025.

articles.headline: Iran says four tankers on fire after striking mines in Hormuz
articles.title: Iran says four tankers on fire after striking mines in Hormuz
articles.description: Iran's Revolutionary Guard says four tankers have caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz.

articles.headline: World Bank reports rapid poverty reduction in India over the past decade
articles.title: India made ‘remarkable progress’ in reducing poverty: World Bank
articles.summary: According to an October 2026 report by the World Bank, India achieved rapid poverty reduction between 2011 and 2023, lifting approximately 496 million people out of poverty as extreme poverty rates declined. Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman attributed these improvements to strong consumption growth, rising employment among women, and expanded social welfare programs. However, the report also highlighted ongoing challenges, including wage disparities and a rise in youth unemployment.
articles.description: Report says the country saw one of the fastest reductions in poverty in the world; extreme poverty fell to 2.6% in 2023 from 27.1% in 2011, driven by government transfers and rising employment

articles.headline: India announces nationwide population census schedule for early 2027
articles.title: Population census to be conducted from January 25 to February 28 except in snow-bound and poll-bound States
articles.summary: The Indian government has announced that the nationwide population census will take place from January 25, 2027, to February 28, 2027. According to a Gazette notification issued by the Ministry of Home Affairs on October 30, 2026, the exercise will exclude specific snow-bound and poll-bound regions, while setting the official reference date as March 1, 2027, to determine demographic statistics accurately.
articles.description: Reference date for population census will be 00:00 hours of March 1, 2027; census will not be held in Manipur, Goa, Uttar Pradesh, Punjab and Uttarakhand, Ladakh, Himachal Pradesh and J&K

articles.headline: UN rights office warns of ongoing displacement and ethnic cleansing in Gaza
articles.title: Ethnic cleansing fears rise as Israel squeezes space in Gaza: UN
articles.summary: The United Nations Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights warned on Friday that Israeli military operations continue to displace Palestinians into a shrinking portion of the Gaza Strip, raising serious concerns of ethnic cleansing. The agency reported extensive destruction of civilian infrastructure and recent attacks on displacement camps, noting that ongoing conflict has caused significant casualties since October 2023.
articles.description: Israeli forces are treating the 'Yellow Line', which is encroaching westward, as 'a kill zone', the OHCHR says.

articles.headline: UN commission accuses Israel of ongoing war crimes and genocide in Gaza and West Bank
articles.title: Israeli forces committed war crimes, genocide even after Gaza ceasefire: UN Commission
articles.summary: The Independent International Commission of Inquiry on the Occupied Palestinian Territory reported that Israeli authorities continue committing severe human rights violations, including war crimes and genocide, despite the October 2025 ceasefire. Chaired by Justice Srinivasan Muralidhar, the United Nations body stated that over 75,000 Palestinians have died since October 7, 2023, while Israeli Permanent Representative Danny Danon strongly rejected the allegations as historical fiction.
articles.description: In Gaza, Israeli forces have continued expanding their territorial control, resulting in the killing and injuring of Palestinian civilians, including children, who approach or cross the Yellow Line, which separates Israel- military controlled Gaza from the Palestine-ruled parts of the enclave, Justice Srinivasan Muralidhar said.

articles.headline: Trump announces immediate Russian diesel supplies following talks with Putin
articles.title: Trump says Russia to immediately supply diesel to U.S. after talks with Putin
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump stated on October 9, 2026, that Russia will supply hundreds of thousands of tonnes of diesel fuel to the American market following a phone call with Russian President Vladimir Putin. The move aims to lower domestic fuel prices amid the ongoing conflict involving Iran. However, the agreement faced severe condemnation from Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and various American lawmakers who argued the policy supports Moscow's economy.
articles.description: The surprise announcement comes against the backdrop of a U.S. law seeking to impose steep tariffs against top purchasers of Russian oil and gas

articles.headline: Quad foreign ministers meet in Atlanta to review regional progress
articles.title: Quad delivering results for people in Indo-Pacific: Rubio
articles.summary: United States Secretary of State Marco Rubio met External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar, Japan's Foreign Minister Toshimitsu Motegi, and Australian Foreign Minister Penny Wong in Atlanta on October 31, 2026. According to Mr. Rubio, the officials reviewed Indo-Pacific cooperation and supply chains ahead of an upcoming summit in the Philippines. Mr. Jaishankar noted that the talks also focused on strengthening bilateral relations.
articles.description: The group reviewed progress in turning shared priorities into real benefits for the Indo-Pacific region

articles.headline: Andhra Pradesh chief minister orders high alert over cyclone threat
articles.title: Naidu calls for high alert as another cyclone threat looms over Andhra Pradesh
articles.summary: Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu directed officials to accelerate restoration works following Cyclone Arnab and prepare for a potential new cyclone on October 31, 2026. A depression in the Bay of Bengal threatens south coastal Andhra and Rayalaseema with heavy rainfall from November 2 to November 4. Authorities were instructed to monitor satellite data and provide compensation for agricultural losses.
articles.description: Depression over southeast Bay of Bengal likely to intensify into a cyclone by November 1; officials told to monitor its movement every six hours and expedite restoration works in cyclone-hit areas

articles.headline: Union government releases tax devolution instalment of 1.09 lakh crore rupees
articles.title: Centre releases additional instalment of tax devolution of ₹1.09 lakh crore to states
articles.summary: The Union government released an additional tax devolution instalment exceeding 1.09 lakh crore rupees to state governments on October 31, 2026. The Finance Ministry stated that the funds aim to support state development expenditure and accelerate capital spending ahead of the festive season. States regularly receive forty-one percent of centrally collected taxes across fourteen annual instalments.
articles.description: This is in addition to the regular monthly devolution and the second additional instalment this financial year

articles.headline: Quad ministers express grave concern over economic coercion and overproduction
articles.title: Quad ministers express ‘grave concerns’ over economic coercion
articles.summary: Foreign ministers from the United States, India, Japan, and Australia issued joint concerns regarding economic coercion and non-market policies during a meeting in Atlanta on October 31, 2026. Without naming countries, the alliance warned that arbitrary export restrictions and overcapacity disrupt global supply chains. The officials also emphasized the importance of preserving navigational rights and maritime security in critical global sea lanes.
articles.description: "The four ministers expressed grave concerns regarding economic coercion, including through arbitrary export restrictions," said a statement from the Quad alliance in Atlanta, Georgia.

articles.headline: Binance covers ninety percent of losses following massive cryptocurrency hack
articles.title: Crypto firm Binance covers 90% of losses after $6.3bn hack
articles.summary: Cryptocurrency exchange Binance announced on October 31, 2026, that it covered ninety percent of the 6.3 billion dollars stolen in a recent cyberattack. Co-chief executive officer Richard Teng stated that corporate treasury funds were used to protect users, while analytics firms suspect North Korean hackers. Law enforcement and the company are continuing investigations and freezing assets.
articles.description: Two analytics firms say they have robust intelligence pointing to a North Korean state-backed group as the likely culprit.

articles.headline: Evacuees from Russian-occupied Oleshky arrive in Belarus on route to Ukraine
articles.title: Ukrainian evacuees reunite with family after years trapped in Russia-occupied city
articles.summary: Civilians evacuated from the devastated city of Oleshky landed in Gomel, Belarus, following a local ceasefire brokered by United States First Lady Melania Trump. The residents endured severe conditions without food, water, or electricity, with some surviving on garden weeds. The humanitarian truce allowed mine-clearing operations along escape routes before buses transported citizens toward Ukrainian territory.
articles.description: Oleshky residents had been without food, water and electricity, with many resorting to cooking garden weeds to survive.

articles.headline: U.S. approves Patriot missiles sale to Ukraine as delivery timelines remain uncertain
articles.title: Trump admin approves potential Patriot missiles sale to Ukraine
articles.summary: The United States State Department green-lit the sale of 500 Patriot missiles to Ukraine following weeks of complaints regarding dwindling interceptor supplies. While the approval goes to Congress for review, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy warned that deliveries could take years. The weapons sale will be funded by donations from allies rather than United States funds.
articles.description: The approval, which goes to Congress for review, comes after weeks of complaints by Ukrainian authorities that its supplies of the interceptor missiles were dwindling

articles.headline: Beyond Cyclone Arnab: can India tackle the growing cost of natural disasters? | Insight India
articles.title: Beyond Cyclone Arnab: can India tackle the growing cost of natural disasters? | Insight India
articles.description: Cyclone Arnab hit the coast of Andhra Pradesh this week. In preparation, authorities evacuated people, halted transportation services and alerted disaster response forces. This is just the first cyclone of the northeast monsoon season. As climate change threatens to bring increasingly intense cyclones and other natural disasters, will India’s current disaster management programme be able to handle the social and economic costs I?n this episode, Sonikka Loganathan speaks to Safi Ahsan Rizvi, former Adviser to the National Disaster Management Authority, about what goes into disaster management, the costs to the economy and vulnerable populations, and how India has improved its strategy since 1999.

articles.headline: Wrestler Manisha Bhanwala secures historic World championship gold medal in Astana
articles.title: A dream come true moment for Manisha
articles.summary: Manisha Bhanwala became the first Indian woman wrestler to win a World championship gold by defeating the United States competitor Abigail Elizabeth Nette 8-6 in the final on October 31, 2026. Competing in the 59kg category in Astana, the 29-year-old athlete rebounded from a disappointing Asian Games performance. She dedicated the victory to her late father, helping propel the Indian women's team to a fifth-place finish.
articles.description: She becomes the first-ever Indian woman wrestler to land a World championship gold in Astana

articles.headline: Democratic Republic of Congo records over 5,000 deaths in deadliest Ebola outbreak
articles.title: More than 5,000 die from Ebola in DR Congo's deadliest outbreak
articles.summary: Government data shows that more than 5,000 people have died from an ongoing Ebola outbreak across eight provinces in the Democratic Republic of Congo. Public health officials reported over 10,300 confirmed cases with a fatality rate of 48.6%. The World Health Organization stated that greater access to affected areas and key control measures are needed to end the epidemic.
articles.description: Government data shows that more than 10,000 people have contracted the rare virus.

articles.headline: Central teams inspect cyclone Arnab damage in Andhra Pradesh as relief sought
articles.title: Central teams assess cyclone Arnab damage in East Godavari, Konaseema as Naidu seeks ₹4,600 crore in relief
articles.summary: Two Inter-Ministerial Central teams inspected cyclone Arnab-hit regions across East Godavari, West Godavari, and Dr. B.R. Ambedkar Konaseema districts on October 31, 2026, evaluating agricultural and infrastructural losses. Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu previously estimated total damages at ₹4,600 crore following the October 29 landfall. The assessment aims to verify extensive destruction to paddy fields, horticulture crops, and thousands of houses and fishing boats.
articles.description: Two Inter-Ministerial Central teams inspect damage to crops, houses, public infrastructure and fishing assets in the two districts; West Godavari reports extensive paddy, aquaculture and fishing boat losses

articles.headline: Iran foreign minister calls United States outreach positive while outlining conditions
articles.title: Iran FM says US outreach a ‘positive step’ as delegation in Qatar for talks
articles.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi described a diplomatic overture from United States Vice President JD Vance as a positive step during a statement on October 31, 2026. While an Iranian delegation visited Doha for consultations mediated by Qatar, Araghchi stated that direct meetings with American officials are unnecessary at this stage. Tehran demands the lifting of specific sanctions, reduced regional forces, and the release of frozen funds before implementing proposals.
articles.description: Iran’s Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi tells Al Jazeera Tehran doesn't rule out attack, is ‘prepared for all scenarios’.

articles.headline: South Africa defeats Australia by 176 runs to claim Test series victory
articles.title: Harmer shines as South Africa wins third Test against Australia to claim series 2-1
articles.summary: Simon Harmer claimed career-best figures of 6-16 as South Africa dismissed Australia for 111 runs on October 31, 2026, securing a 176-run victory in the third Test in Cape Town. The win clinched the series 2-1 for the Proteas, who rose to the top of the International Cricket Council rankings. Harmer finished the match with ten wickets, while bowler Kagiso Rabada achieved his 350th Test wicket during the final day.
articles.description: The Proteas rallied from 1-0 down in the first Test series between the teams in South Africa since the ‘Sandpapergate’ scandal in 2018.

articles.headline: Iran supreme leader warns United States and Israel against new attacks
articles.title: Iran’s Supreme Leader warns U.S., Israel against new attacks
articles.summary: Mojtaba Khamenei warned the United States and Israel during a meeting with senior military commanders on October 31, 2026. The supreme leader instructed forces to ensure any threat receives an immediate and geographically unrestricted response. The remarks coincided with diplomatic talks in Tehran involving Qatari officials addressing a letter from United States Vice President JD Vance.
articles.description: According to the statement, Mr. Khamenei ordered the commanders to ensure that "any level or type of threat must be met with an immediate, impactful and geographically unrestricted response".

articles.headline: Israel's parliamentary elections end in deadlock as neither major bloc secures majority
articles.title: Israel voted for Israel: Why Gaza wasn’t on the ballot
articles.summary: Israel remains politically deadlocked after the October 27 polls failed to deliver a 61-seat majority for any coalition, with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's camp securing 53 seats. Despite massive voter turnout, the ongoing conflict in Gaza and related humanitarian crises were largely absent from campaign debates, which focused instead on domestic issues like judicial reforms and military exemptions. Analysts noted that military occupation and security fundamentally shaped voter perspectives across the political spectrum.
articles.description: Despite genocide, regional war and isolation, Israel's election revealed little appetite for political alternatives.

articles.headline: Andy Burnham considers formal slavery apology while ruling out reparations
articles.title: Burnham opens door to formal apology for Britain’s slave trade
articles.summary: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham stated he is open to issuing a formal state apology regarding Britain's role in the transatlantic slave trade, ahead of a Commonwealth leaders summit in Antigua and Barbuda. Speaking on Friday, Burnham rejected financial reparations but proposed an international initiative to reduce debt burdens for poorer nations, supported by former Prime Minister Gordon Brown. Caribbean leaders welcomed talks on broader cooperation.
articles.description: UK Prime Minister rules out financial reparations, despite longstanding Caribbean demands.

articles.headline: Yemen conflict displacement reaches 290,000 as fighting intensifies
articles.title: New Yemen fighting displaces 290,000, says UN, with pregnant women at risk
articles.summary: At least 290,000 people have been displaced in Yemen since August due to escalating conflict between government forces and Houthi rebels, according to the United Nations humanitarian office. The violence has heavily impacted Taiz governorate and caused severe shortages, while pregnant women and refugees face acute risks. Meanwhile, military operations and reported missile attacks continue across multiple fronts, including near Saudi Arabia and the presidential palace in Aden.
articles.description: A new outbreak in fighting in Yemen has forced tens of thousands of people from their homes.

articles.headline: Alphabet revenue growth highlights heavy artificial intelligence infrastructure spending costs
articles.title: Why investors are worried despite Alphabet’s 25% revenue growth and Google Cloud’s revenue more than doubling | Explained
articles.summary: The partial text notes that Alphabet reported strong growth in the September quarter while highlighting significant financial costs dedicated to keeping pace with the artificial intelligence sector. Heavy investments in computing infrastructure are required to develop artificial intelligence models. Additionally, artificial intelligence tools are changing user interaction with Google Search, creating questions regarding future advertising revenue generation and capital expenditure returns.
articles.description: Google’s parent company is investing heavily in artificial intelligence infrastructure as its cloud business expands. But the spending is weighing on cash flow, while AI-powered search raises questions about the future of its advertising business

articles.headline: Iranian lawmakers call for nuclear treaty withdrawal amid ongoing conflict
articles.title: Iran lawmakers call for withdrawal from NPT: Will we have war or peace?
articles.summary: Several Iranian legislators have urged the country to withdraw from the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty and alter its nuclear doctrine following heavy costs from war and sanctions. The demands arrive as the conflict enters its ninth month and Qatari mediators pursue peace talks involving the United States. While Iranian leaders have not formally responded, the International Atomic Energy Agency previously raised concerns regarding Tehran's nuclear compliance.
articles.description: Withdrawal from the nuclear treaty doses not mean that Iran would build a nuclear weapon, observers say.

articles.headline: US approves sale of 500 Patriot missiles to Ukraine
articles.title: US approves sale of 500 Patriot missiles to Ukraine
articles.summary: The United States State Department approved a 2.1 billion dollar sale of 500 Patriot interceptor missiles to Ukraine to defend against Russian aerial attacks. European allies and Canada funded the purchase entirely, with Lockheed Martin serving as the principal contractor. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky warned that the country was facing critical shortages as Russian ballistic missile strikes intensified across multiple regions.
articles.description: The American-made interceptors are the only effective weapon for downing Russia's ballistic missiles.

articles.headline: Iran warns of unfettered retaliation amid ongoing diplomatic efforts
articles.title: Iran warns of unfettered retaliation if attacked as mediators try for peace
articles.summary: Iranian Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei ordered armed forces to prepare for an immediate, geographically unrestricted response if attacked again. Mediators from Qatar held talks in Tehran on Friday to prevent a new war as tensions persist over maritime security and regional conflicts. Meanwhile, local authorities reported that US drone strikes bombed fishing boats south of Qeshm island, injuring several fishermen.
articles.description: Iran’s supreme leader says Tehran’s potential response will not be restricted by geography.

articles.headline: India cuts petrol export duty to nil and raises diesel levy
articles.title: Petrol export duty cut to nil, diesel levy raised by ₹3 a litre
articles.summary: The Indian government reduced export duty on petrol to nil on October 31, 2026, while increasing levies on diesel and aviation turbine fuel by three rupees and fifty paise per litre respectively. The fortnightly adjustment aims to ensure domestic fuel availability amidst global supply constraints. Data from analytics provider Kpler indicated that national diesel exports reached seven hundred thousand barrels per day in October.
articles.description: The government’s fortnightly review raised the export levy on diesel to ₹11.5 per litre from ₹8.5 and on aviation turbine fuel to ₹11 per litre from ₹10.5, while India’s diesel exports touched 700 kilo barrels per day in October, the highest since September 2025, according to Kpler

articles.headline: Hundreds of evacuees from Oleshky arrive in Belarus
articles.title: Evacuees from Russian-occupied Oleshky arrive in Ukraine via Belarus
articles.summary: Evacuees from the Russian-occupied town of Oleshky have arrived in Gomel, Belarus, via four planes as part of an evacuation mission supported by United States First Lady Melania Trump and Pope Leo XIV. The civilians crossed the border during a regional truce that allows residents to choose between Ukrainian-held territory, Russian-held territory, or remaining in the city with replenished medical supplies.
articles.description: Four planes transporting evacuees from the war-ravaged city arrived in Belarus's Gomel earlier on Saturday.

articles.headline: Jio Platforms raises 3.2 billion dollars in stock market debut
articles.title: How Ambani’s Jio became India’s second-largest company
articles.summary: Jio Platforms achieved India's largest initial public offering by raising 3.2 billion dollars, causing its shares to surge 21 percent on Wednesday and valuing the company at 131.5 billion dollars. Backed by Meta and Google, the company serves over 530 million customers, though its rapid rise since 2016 has heavily concentrated India's telecommunications market and sparked intense industry competition.
articles.description: Jio makes India’s largest-ever stock market debut, raising $3.2bn in IPO.

articles.headline: Democrats target four Senate seats to overcome Republican majority
articles.title: Can Democrats win the US Senate? 10 key midterm races to watch
articles.summary: United States Democrats require a net gain of four seats in November midterm elections to wrest Senate control from Republicans who hold a 53-47 majority. Intensified by voter discontent over inflation, trade tariffs, and the war on Iran, tight races in states like Alaska, Iowa, Kansas, and Maine could determine the balance of power in Washington.
articles.description: From Texas to Maine, rising prices and the Iran war put key Senate races in play as Democrats fight for control.

articles.headline: Ashutosh Dixit assumes charge as Indian Chief of Air Staff
articles.title: Air Chief Marshal Ashutosh Dixit takes charge as new Chief of Air Staff
articles.summary: Air Chief Marshal Ashutosh Dixit assumed command as the new Chief of Air Staff, succeeding Air Chief Marshal A.P. Singh following his retirement. Dixit brings four decades of service and over 3,500 flying hours across 20 aircraft types to the role, having previously served as Vice Chief of the force and Chief of Integrated Defence Staff.
articles.description: The IAF accorded a ceremonial guard of honour to the outgoing Air Chief Marshal A.P. Singh at the Race Course Air Force Station before he handed over the baton to Ashutosh Dixit

articles.headline: United Nations Security Council rejects rival US and Russian resolutions
articles.title: Rival US and Russian resolutions on Western Sahara fail at UN
articles.summary: The United Nations Security Council failed to adopt competing United States and Russian resolutions regarding Western Sahara, casting uncertainty on the future of the peacekeeping mission known as MINURSO. Russia vetoed the US-backed proposal on Friday, while a rival Russian draft failed to garner the necessary nine votes before the mission mandate expired.
articles.description: UN Security Council rejected the competing proposals, leaving the peacekeeping mission without an approved extension.

articles.headline: Evacuation corridor opens in Russian-occupied Oleshky under a temporary ceasefire
articles.title: Hundreds evacuated from Russian-occupied Oleshky during rare Ukraine ceasefire
articles.summary: The evacuation of the Russian-occupied Ukrainian city of Oleshky is under way following a ceasefire brokered by United States First Lady Melania Trump. Residents wishing to leave have a four-hour window using a convoy of twenty-five buses organised by Ukrainian human rights ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets and his Russian counterpart Yana Lantratova. The temporary truce is scheduled to remain in effect until the end of November 1, 2026, providing the first pause in fighting in the Kherson region since February 2022.
articles.description: Hundreds of people are also understood to have stayed in the front-line town, despite the dangers.

articles.headline: Russia-Ukraine war devastation causes massive dolphin deaths in the Black Sea
articles.title: Dead dolphins, naval mines: Russia-Ukraine war destroys the Black Sea
articles.summary: Hostilities from the Russia-Ukraine conflict have severely impacted marine life, causing the deaths of over 120,000 cetaceans in the Black Sea by 2026. According to Ivan Rusev of Tuzly Lagoons national park, military sonar systems, explosions, and pollution from damaged warships disorient dolphins, impairing their echolocation and causing self-poisoning and fatal infections. Environmental degradation also threatens birds and fish populations, with cetacean recovery estimated to require up to fifty years.
articles.description: Conflict devastates Black Sea marine life, killing more than 120,000 dolphins and causing ecological damage.

articles.headline: Infant deaths in Attappady renew concerns over tribal health and socioeconomic conditions
articles.title: How infant deaths in Keralam’s Attappady expose a deep-rooted health, social crisis
articles.summary: The recent deaths of 12 infants in Attappady have highlighted a persistent child health crisis affecting tribal communities in Keralam. Figures from tribal activists indicate that 124 infants have died in the region since 2011 alongside numerous abortions and stillbirths. While the State government has initiated an expert assessment, tribal organizations stress that solutions require addressing broader nutritional, maternal health, landlessness, and socioeconomic challenges.
articles.description: 12 infants, including 10 tribals, have died in Attappady this year, sparking a political row as the State government orders an expert probe. Tribal activists say the crisis demands action beyond healthcare, addressing malnutrition, anaemia and deep-rooted social issues

articles.headline: Nations agree on biodiversity pact at the COP17 summit in Armenia
articles.title: Nations commit to get nature goals back on track at UN nature summit
articles.summary: Nearly 200 nations approved key texts at the COP17 biodiversity summit in Yerevan, Armenia, aiming to revive goals of halting nature destruction by 2030. Despite reaching agreements on addressing harmful subsidies and conservation finance, delegates expressed disappointment over missed opportunities and political challenges regarding scientific evidence. Ecuador was selected to host the next biodiversity talks in 2028 after a secret vote.
articles.description: The United Nations had warned that progress was insufficient to meet the goals of the 2030 target including protecting 30% of Earth’s land and oceans, tackling pollution and invasive species, and boosting money for conservation

articles.headline: Donald Trump reinstates rallies in Kansas and Iowa ahead of midterms
articles.title: Trump backtracks on rallies in turbulent end to midterms campaign
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump reversed an earlier decision to reinstate two campaign rallies in Kansas and Iowa ahead of the midterm elections on November 3, 2026. Speaking in Daytona, Florida, the 80-year-old leader urged voters to support Republican candidates. Meanwhile, a record 47.9 million Americans have already voted, including Pope Leo XIV, who became the first pontiff to cast a ballot in a political election.
articles.description: The U.S. President reinstated two rallies in Kansas and Iowa a day after cancelling them, saying Republicans “have a shot” in the midterms as a record 47.9 million Americans have already voted

articles.headline: New York governor signs legislation restricting artificial intelligence chatbot interactions with minors
articles.title: New York restricts AI chatbot interactions with children | Explained
articles.summary: New York Governor Kathy Hochul signed two bills on October 28, 2026, designed to protect children from the risks posed by artificial intelligence chatbots and internet-connected baby monitors. The legislation bans artificial intelligence chatbots from engaging in harmful activities such as simulating romantic relationships or encouraging self-harm among minors. Additionally, the new law requires manufacturers of internet-connected baby monitors to implement security safeguards against unauthorised access to audio and video streams.
articles.description: Governor Kathy Hochul signed two laws on October 28 barring AI chatbots from harmful interactions with minors, including simulating romantic relationships and promoting self-harm, and requiring security safeguards in internet-connected baby monitors

articles.headline: Crypto exchange platform Binance suffers major cyberattack resulting in asset loss
articles.title: What we know about Binance’s multi-billion-dollar crypto hack | Explained
articles.summary: Cryptocurrency exchange platform Binance experienced a cyberattack on October 29 that resulted in asset losses exceeding six billion dollars. Following warnings from independent crypto trackers, Binance acknowledged reports of a potential security issue on October 30 while assuring users that their funds remained entirely safe. Investigations into the exploit remain ongoing as facts continue to emerge from the incident.
articles.description: While the facts are still emerging, the Binance cyberattack could go down as the largest cryptocurrency hack on record

articles.headline: US, South Korea, and Japan urge complete denuclearization of North Korea
articles.title: US, South Korea, Japan call for ‘complete denuclearisation’ of North Korea
articles.summary: Top diplomats from the United States, South Korea, and Japan reaffirmed their commitment to the complete denuclearization of North Korea during meetings in Atlanta. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, South Korean Foreign Minister Cho Hyun, and Japanese Foreign Minister Toshimitsu Motegi called for the full implementation of United Nations Security Council resolutions. The diplomatic push occurs despite speculation regarding potential future talks between Washington and Pyongyang.
articles.description: The joint statement comes as US President Donald Trump seeks a new meeting with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un.

articles.headline: Oman rescues crew from burning ship as Iran halts tankers in strait
articles.title: Oman rescues 25 from burning ship, Iran halts tankers
articles.summary: Oman's navy rescued 25 crew members from the Panamanian-flagged merchant ship RITI after it was attacked and caught fire on October 30, 2026, according to the Maritime Security Centre. Simultaneously, Iran's Revolutionary Guards reported that three oil tankers were halted in the Strait of Hormuz after encountering incidents. U.S. Central Command chief Brad Cooper stated that American forces had cleared primary transit routes of sea mines.
articles.description: Tehran has restricted maritime traffic through the strait since the West Asia war erupted on February 28 with U.S.-Israeli strikes on the Islamic republic

articles.headline: G20 foreign ministers conclude Atlanta meeting without consensus on key global issues
articles.title: G20 foreign ministers to end Atlanta meeting without consensus on key issues
articles.summary: Top diplomats from the Group of 20 largest economies concluded two days of talks in Atlanta without a joint communique on October 31, 2026. According to attending diplomats, divisions over Russia's war in Ukraine and other global security crises prevented agreement, prompting U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio to issue a chairman's statement instead. The meeting was further strained by European objections to Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov's presence.
articles.description: Divisions over Russia’s war with Ukraine overshadowed the talks, with U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio set to release a chairman’s statement instead of a joint communique

articles.headline: US midterms approach as early voting surges and national polls show Democratic lead
articles.title: US midterms: 3 days to go – What latest polls say as early voting surges
articles.summary: With the United States midterm elections approaching on Tuesday, national surveys indicate a Democratic lead while early voter turnout surpasses previous levels. According to an Associated Press analysis, over 43 million Americans cast ballots early. President Donald Trump scheduled weekend rallies in Iowa and Kansas to mobilise supporters, while various candidates concluded their campaigns across multiple states.
articles.description: More than 43 million Americans have voted early as Democrats lead opinion polls and Trump prepares for final rallies.

articles.headline: Amit Shah promises Uniform Civil Code in Uttar Pradesh if BJP wins
articles.title: Uniform Civil Code in U.P. if BJP voted to power again: Amit Shah
articles.summary: Union Home Minister Amit Shah announced that the Bharatiya Janata Party will implement a Uniform Civil Code in Uttar Pradesh if the party wins the 2027 Assembly election. Speaking at a state executive meeting, Mr. Shah praised Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath for governance and challenged opposition leaders to a parliamentary debate regarding voter revision controversies, while accusing the Samajwadi Party of disrupting legislative proceedings.
articles.description: Amit Shah challenges Rahul Gandhi and Akhilesh Yadav to a debate on the special intensive revision in Parliament, but says they just wanted to create a ruckus

articles.headline: At least 14 people killed in attack on Ukraine train station
articles.title: At least 14 people killed in attack on Ukraine train station
articles.description: A Russian drone strike killed at least 14 people at Dnipro’s main railway station in central Ukraine.

articles.headline: Spain train disaster threatens Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez reelection chances
articles.title: Spain train disaster clouds Sánchez chances of re-election
articles.summary: A high-speed train collision in central Spain resulted in 69 recovered bodies, severely damaging public confidence in the rail network and Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez ahead of a snap general election. Transport Minister Oscar Puente defended the infrastructure and blamed human error, while opposition parties called for his resignation. The tragedy compounds existing political crises for Sanchez, whose party trails behind the centre-right People's Party in recent polls.
articles.description: The Spanish PM is hit by a succession of crises just weeks before a snap general election.

articles.headline: Trump tells voters to send El-Sayed ‘back to where he came from’
articles.title: Trump tells voters to send El-Sayed ‘back to where he came from’
articles.description: Speaking at a campaign rally, Donald Trump told voters to send Michigan’s Abdul El-Sayed ‘back to where he came from’.

articles.headline: Russian drone strike kills 13 people at a train station in central Ukraine
articles.title: Ukraine says at least 13 killed in Russian attack on train station
articles.summary: At least thirteen people died and ten others sustained injuries on October 29, 2026, when a Russian drone struck a crowded platform at the Dnipro railway station in central Ukraine. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy condemned the attack, calling for tougher international sanctions against Moscow. Meanwhile, separate Russian strikes across the country resulted in five additional fatalities.
articles.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy labelled the strike "horrific" and said the Russians had attacked a platform "where a regular commuter train and a regular passenger train were standing"

articles.headline: Israel's election confirms Prime Minister Netanyahu's bloc lost its parliamentary majority.
articles.title: Difficult negotiations lie ahead in Israel after Netanyahu's bloc lost its parliamentary majority
articles.summary: Israel's final election results released on October 30, 2026, confirmed that Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc secured 53 seats in the October 27 election, losing its majority in the 120-seat Knesset. The main opposition won 48 seats while Arab-led parties took 19. President Isaac Herzog will task someone with forming a government after results are submitted on November 4, amid controversy over unproven allegations of electoral interference.
articles.description: The election results still need to be certified and submitted to the President next Wednesday (November 4, 2026)

articles.headline: U.S., South Korea and Japan reaffirm complete denuclearisation of North Korea
articles.title: U.S., South Korea, Japan vow ‘complete’ North Korea’s denuclearisation
articles.summary: Diplomats from the United States, South Korea and Japan reiterated their commitment to complete denuclearisation during discussions held on October 30, 2026, in Atlanta. The meeting took place amid ongoing speculation regarding potential talks between Washington and Pyongyang, while North Korea continues to reject disarmament efforts and maintains its status as a nuclear-armed state.
articles.description: Speculation is mounting over a potential meeting between U.S. President Donald Trump and North Korean leader Kim Jong Un at next month’s APEC summit in China, with Mr. Trump making repeated overtures to Pyongyang for nuclear talks

articles.headline: Russia’s Novaya Gazeta ‘killed off’ after murders, arrests and pressure
articles.title: Russia’s Novaya Gazeta ‘killed off’ after murders, arrests and pressure
articles.description: Russia’s most prominent investigative newspaper is closing, with staff accusing the government of killing it off.

articles.headline: Tata Motors acquires controlling stake in Iveco Group for 4.32 billion dollars
articles.title: Tata Motors says Iveco is now part of group; Chandrasekaran appointed Chairperson
articles.summary: Tata Motors Ltd. completed the voluntary tender offer acquisition of Iveco Group N.V. by securing approximately 89.42% of its common shares for about $4.32 billion. Led by Tata Group Chairman N. Chandrasekaran, the transaction involves executive board changes across both companies, including Chandrasekaran taking over as Chairperson of Iveco Group N.V. The final settlement of shares is scheduled for November 13, 2026.
articles.description: The acquisition is valued at approximately $4.32 billion (₹42,561 crore)

articles.headline: Ebola death toll in Democratic Republic of the Congo exceeds five thousand
articles.title: Ebola death toll in DR Congo passes 5,000
articles.summary: Government data released on October 31, 2026, indicates that the death toll from Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has surpassed five thousand. Authorities are struggling to control the outbreak caused by the rare Bundibugyo strain, which has infected over ten thousand people and spread to neighboring African countries, prompting travel restrictions.
articles.description: Authorities ​are struggling to find a way to control the ⁠outbreak, with no approved treatments or vaccines.

articles.headline: Hundreds evacuated from Melania-brokered ceasefire town of Oleshky
articles.title: Hundreds evacuated from Melania-brokered ceasefire town of Oleshky
articles.description: Hundreds have been evacuated from Russia-occupied Oleshky under a localised ceasefire brokered by Melania Trump.

articles.headline: GSLV places navigation satellite NVS-03 into orbit
articles.title: GSLV places next-generation navigation satellite NVS-03 into orbit
articles.summary: The Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle launched the NVS-03 satellite from the Satish Dhawan Space Centre in Sriharikota on October 30, 2026, according to the Indian Space Research Organisation. The 2250 kilogram satellite is the third in the next-generation navigation system designed to provide continuity of navigation services for the Indian Regional Navigation Satellite System series.
articles.description: The NVS-03, with a mission life of 12 years, is expected to restore the functioning of the NavIC constellation; satellite carries an indigenous atomic clock, along with procured atomic clocks

articles.headline: Poland’s president joins protest amid constitutional crisis at top court
articles.title: Poland’s president joins protest amid constitutional crisis at top court
articles.description: Poland’s president has cut short a trip to Senegal, joining protesters facing off with police.

articles.headline: Blockchain analytics firms identify North Korean hackers behind Binance cryptocurrency heist
articles.title: Why North Korea's 'elite' hackers are the prime suspect in major Binance hack
articles.summary: Two blockchain analytics firms, TRM Labs and Chainalysis, have attributed the massive $6.3 billion hack of cryptocurrency exchange Binance to the North Korean state-backed Lazarus Group, also known as TraderTraitor. Investigators state that attackers compromised Binance systems to automatically transfer funds. While Binance reports that approximately 80% of the stolen assets have been successfully secured, the incident highlights escalating cyber threats.
articles.description: If the accusations are true, the record-making heist shows how powerful suspected North Korean hackers have become.

articles.headline: External affairs minister criticises global energy market disruptions caused by sanctions and chokepoints
articles.title: India slams global energy disruptions through sanctions, chokepoints
articles.summary: External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar strongly condemned deliberate disruptions in global oil supplies during the G20 Foreign Ministers' Meeting in Atlanta. Addressing U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio and international delegates, Mr. Jaishankar stated that sanctions and chokepoints are being used as calculated strategies to hold energy prices hostage. He emphasised the severe impact on low-income countries and called for predictable energy markets.
articles.description: The Minister emphasised that continuous distortions of energy markets through obstacles, sanctions and chokepoints were happening with increasing frequency, greater complexity and wider impact

articles.headline: Delegates at Yerevan summit reach agreement on biodiversity action plan
articles.title: Global nature talks reach deal but money remains an issue
articles.summary: Delegates from nearly 200 countries meeting in Yerevan successfully negotiated the key elements of a new biodiversity action plan following prolonged discussions. Environment advocates welcomed the agreement despite widespread warnings that nations are severely falling behind on targets set during the 2022 framework. Participants highlighted that insufficient funding and ongoing environmental subsidies remain major obstacles to global conservation efforts.
articles.description: Countries have been trying to get a global agreement to halt nature decline back on track.

articles.headline: Brazil summons Argentina diplomat following Flavio Bolsonaro departure to United States
articles.title: Brazil summons Argentinian diplomat over Bolsonaro’s flight to US
articles.summary: Brazilian authorities summoned charge d'affaires Maria Emilia Cortes to address right-wing politician Flavio Bolsonaro fleeing the country after losing Sunday's presidential election. Bolsonaro faces money-laundering allegations involving Banco Master. He travelled through Argentina to Miami, declaring himself president-elect. The incident strains ties between President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and Argentina's libertarian leader Javier Milei, who supported the departure.
articles.description: The move threatens to further strain relations between Brazilian President Lula and his Argentinian counterpart, Milei.

articles.headline: G20 family photo cancelled following European diplomatic boycott over Russia
articles.title: G20 'family photo' cancelled after protests over presence of Russian minister
articles.summary: Organisers cancelled the scheduled family photograph at the Group of Twenty foreign ministers meeting in Atlanta after European diplomats refused to stand alongside Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov. United States Secretary of State Marco Rubio hosted the gathering. British Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband participated in the boycott, citing longstanding policies against direct engagement with Russian officials since the invasion of Ukraine.
articles.description: UK Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband confronted his Russian counterpart at the meeting and accused his government of killing innocent civilians in Ukraine.

articles.headline: Binance freezes half of funds stolen in record cyber attack
articles.title: Crypto giant Binance attempting to recover $6.3bn stolen in hack linked to North Korea
articles.summary: Cryptocurrency exchange Binance has frozen roughly half of the six point three billion dollars stolen in a recent cyber heist. Co-chief executive officer Richard Teng stated the attack involved a self-destruct mechanism and multiple points of breach. Analytics firms and the United States Secret Service are working to trace the funds, while experts warn customers that promises to cover losses may not be legally binding.
articles.description: The cyber-attack, which the company describes as complex, is believed to be the largest ever of its kind.

articles.headline: Prominent Russian independent news outlet Novaya Gazeta announces its permanent shutdown.
articles.title: They strangled us, says founder of Russian newspaper shut under pressure from authorities
articles.summary: Novaya Gazeta, one of Russia's most high-profile independent news outlets, is shutting down after receiving an eviction order and having its reader donation system disabled by authorities. In a statement, the newspaper accused Russian special services and the repressive state apparatus of forcing it to stop operations. The closure marks the end of an era for fearless investigative journalism under increasing authoritarian pressure.
articles.description: Novaya Gazeta has been one of the most high-profile independent news outlets in Russia over the last three decades.

articles.headline: US appeals court rejects Trump bid to discard California ballots
articles.title: US appeals court again rejects Trump bid to set aside California ballots
articles.summary: An appeals court in the United States has rejected a petition from the administration of President Donald Trump to set aside 20,000 ballots in California over concerns about non-citizen voting. The ruling arrived on Friday, with less than four days until the November 3 midterm elections. Judges Mark Bennett and Gabriel Sanchez formed the majority, ruling the request violated the US Constitution.
articles.description: The 9th Circuit Court calls the petition to remove 20,000 ballots from California's vote count unconstitutional.

articles.headline: G20 drops group photo as Europeans refuse to stand with Lavrov
articles.title: G20 drops group photo as Europeans refuse to stand with Lavrov
articles.summary: The United States scrapped a traditional group photo of foreign ministers after European officials refused to be pictured alongside Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov in Atlanta. The move exposes deep rifts within the Group of 20, whose foreign ministers are meeting for talks overshadowed by ongoing conflicts in Ukraine and Iran. Russian state media reported that Lavrov arrived ahead of the discussions.
articles.description: Sanctioned Russian FM attends Atlanta talks as Iran war, Hormuz disruption and Ukraine divide G20 members.

articles.headline: US tech stocks fall sharply amid mounting concerns over artificial intelligence costs
articles.title: US tech stocks see sharp falls as AI spending nears $1tn
articles.summary: United States technology stocks dropped on Friday as financial markets reacted to escalating expenditures associated with artificial intelligence development. Major firms including Intel, Amazon, Alphabet, Reddit, and Roblox experienced notable share price declines following disappointing quarterly earnings reports and warnings about slowing sector growth and search revenue impacts, according to market analysts.
articles.description: Shares in Intel continue to fall while the tech-heavy Nasdaq opens at its lowest level in more than two months.

articles.headline: Supreme Court rules failed relationships cannot transform consensual sex into rape
articles.title: Failed relationships cannot turn consensual sex into rape: Supreme Court
articles.summary: The Supreme Court of India ruled on October 30, 2026, that women cannot retrospectively classify past consensual sexual acts as rape simply because a relationship has ended. Justice B.V. Nagarathna cautioned against the misuse of criminal laws in failed relationships from Kerala, emphasizing that genuine sexual assault cases must be vigorously pursued while preventing the justice system from becoming a tool of vengeance.
articles.description: Court distinguishes between consent allegedly obtained through deception and regret over consensual intimacy after a relationship ends

articles.headline: OpenAI, Google, Microsoft and Anthropic back new scraping opt-out
articles.title: The biggest names in AI are backing a new way to opt out of scraping
articles.summary: OpenAI, Google, Microsoft, and Anthropic announced they will adopt a new standard allowing publishers to opt out of web scraping by artificial intelligence companies. Proposed by Kevin Kelley at the Internet Engineering Task Force, the shared policy token will live within a website's robots.txt file. Anthropic has already adopted the signal, while Google and Microsoft plan to support it next year.
articles.description: OpenAI, Google, Microsoft, and Anthropic say they will adopt a new standard that publishers can use to opt out of being scraped by AI, as reported earlier by Search Engine Roundtable. With this control, publishers can apply their AI training preferences across multiple AI companies, instead of setting them individually. The shared "policy token" signal […]

articles.headline: Rubio hosts G20 talks as Russia’s Lavrov presence sparks tensions
articles.title: Rubio hosts G20 talks as Russia’s Lavrov presence sparks tensions
articles.description: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio urged G20 officials to work together to confront threats to the economic order.

articles.headline: European Union and Canada launch Alliance for the Future
articles.title: EU and Canada seek deeper ties amid worsening global uncertainty
articles.summary: The European Union and Canada launched an Alliance for the Future in Montreal, where Prime Minister Mark Carney hosted European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen and European Council President Antonio Costa. The two sides signed a digital trade deal and announced measures to increase affordability and secure sovereignty. Carney also announced Canada's participation in a support loan for Kyiv.
articles.description: Both sides signed a digital trade deal, as Trump's trade threats push Washington's allies to seek closer ties elsewhere.

articles.headline: Supreme Court directs Election Commission to submit report on Form 7 misuse
articles.title: Supreme Court seeks report from ECI on Form 7 misuse allegations
articles.summary: The Supreme Court of India directed the Election Commission of India to investigate allegations regarding the fraudulent bulk filing of Form 7 applications for voter deletions during the Uttar Pradesh Special Intensive Revision. While responding to a petition filed by Congress Member of Parliament Tanuj Punia, the electoral body stated that although false forms were discovered, none of them were accepted. The bench ordered authorities to file a compliance report.
articles.description: Election Commission says it did not accept any Form 7s filed in violation of norms in U.P.; poll officials took prompt corrective steps, it says after Congress MP alleges widespread fraud during SIR

articles.headline: Google tests first space-based AI server response in orbit
articles.title: Google’s satellite AI server transmits its first response to Earth
articles.summary: Google has successfully generated its first response from space using an artificial intelligence chip-equipped satellite. The on-board Gemma four model created a haiku after mission operators booted up its tensor processing units earlier this month during Project Suncatcher. Engineers plan to evaluate how the hardware performs under thermal stress and radiation exposure before attempting to launch twin interconnected satellites in 2027.
articles.description: Google's AI chip-equipped satellite has generated its first response from space. In a blog post on Friday, Google says it successfully booted up the satellite's Tensor Processing Units (TPUs), allowing the on-board Gemma 4 model to follow through on a prompt to create a haiku about being in space: Blue marble below Data streams in […]

articles.headline: US Federal Reserve holds interest rates steady amid surging inflation
articles.title: U.S. Fed holds interest rates steady despite surging inflation
articles.summary: The Federal Open Market Committee voted 10-2 to maintain interest rates between 3.75 and 4.00 percent on Wednesday, October 28, 2026, citing the need for more economic data. The decision comes ahead of midterm elections and follows US President Donald Trump's energy and tariff policies, which have driven inflation while the unemployment rate remains near 4.2 percent.
articles.description: The 12-member FOMC voted 10-2 to hold rates at a target range between 3.75 and 4.00%, citing the need for more data in the fight against inflation

articles.headline: Indian regulators order Sun Pharma to halt eye-care drug production
articles.title: India orders Sun Pharma to halt eye-care drug production at plant after quality lapses
articles.summary: Indian drug regulatory authorities ordered Sun Pharmaceutical Industries to suspend the manufacturing and distribution of ophthalmic products at its Assam facility following quality management lapses identified during a joint inspection. The action follows the company's voluntary recall of multiple batches of eye-care brands. Sun Pharma stated that it has implemented remedial measures and submitted a compliance report currently under review by regulators.
articles.description: India’s drug quality standards have come under increased scrutiny at home and overseas in recent years after locally made cough syrups were linked to ‌the deaths of children in India and also in countries including Gambia and Uzbekistan

articles.headline: Novaya Gazeta shuts down citing severe state pressure in Russia
articles.title: Independent Russian newspaper Novaya Gazeta shuts under Kremlin pressure
articles.summary: Independent Russian newspaper Novaya Gazeta announced its closure on October 30, 2026, stating that state pressure and years of repression had killed the publication. Editor-in-chief Sergei Sokolov and Nobel Prize-winning founder Dmitry Muratov blamed Russian special services for forcing the newsroom to end operations. Founded in 1993, the outlet was one of the last remaining independent news organisations openly critical of the Kremlin and its war in Ukraine.
articles.description: The closure of Novaya Gazeta — one of the last outlets to openly criticise Russia's offensive — marks a new low in Moscow's campaign against dissenting voices that gained speed after the Kremlin sent troops into its neighbour in 2022

articles.headline: Chinese Communist Party official claims elimination of hidden dangers after expulsions
articles.title: China ruling party says 'eliminated dangers' after 33 expelled
articles.summary: A senior official stated that China has eradicated serious hidden dangers within its ruling party and military following a Central Committee plenum that confirmed the expulsion of 33 figures, including former general Zhang Youxia. Zhang Fuhai, deputy secretary of the Central Commission for Discipline Inspection, announced that disciplinary organs have punished 7.9 million individuals since 2012. Analysts suggest the anti-graft drive aims to consolidate President Xi Jinping's leadership.
articles.description: In more than a decade in charge, Xi has cracked down hard on graft, ensnaring thousands of officials and purging dozens of members of the powerful Central Committee and a string of top military brass

articles.headline: Helicopter carrying six people crashes near Joshimath in Uttarakhand
articles.title: Uttarakhand chopper crash: All six on board killed, says Chamoli District Magistrate
articles.summary: A Trans Bharat Aviation Private Limited helicopter carrying six people crashed into a hillside near Joshimath during an overcast afternoon on October 30, 2026. The aircraft, operating from Badrinath to Dehradun, lost communication at approximately 2:20 p.m., prompting the Uttarakhand Civil Aviation Development Authority to ground the company's entire fleet. Disaster management officials, police, the State Disaster Response Force, and military units have been dispatched to conduct search and rescue operations.
articles.description: Five pilgrims from Karnataka and pilot from Delhi killed as helicopter from Badrinath crash amid adverse weather conditions; Congress alleges government negligence and poor safety measures; govt. grounds entire chopper fleet operated by Trans Bharat Aviation; CM orders probe; DGCA and AAIB to reach Dehradun

articles.headline: Jerusalem Daily: Israel’s siege on Hebron displaces thousands
articles.title: Jerusalem Daily: Israel’s siege on Hebron displaces thousands
articles.description: Israel has announced its final election results, tightened its siege on Hebron, and arrested people returning to Gaza.

articles.headline: Yemenis in Aden prepare for potential conflict after recent Houthi missile attacks
articles.title: ‘Need a Plan B’: Yemenis in Aden prepare for another war as missiles fall
articles.summary: Residents in the southern Yemeni city of Aden are stockpiling food and mapping out evacuation routes following a series of recent missile and drone strikes claimed by the Houthis. The attacks on civilian infrastructure, including the international airport, have disrupted daily life and triggered widespread anxiety over a potential escalation in violence.
articles.description: As Houthi missiles strike Aden, residents stockpile food and prepare escape plans, fearing a return to all-out war.

articles.headline: Reliance Industries reports forty one percent rise in second quarter net profit
articles.title: RIL Q2 profit jumps 41% to ₹25,548 crore on O2C, Jio strength
articles.summary: Indian conglomerate Reliance Industries Ltd reported a consolidated net profit of ₹25,548 crore for the second quarter ended September 30, 2026, marking a 41 percent increase compared to the previous year. Chairman Mukesh D. Ambani attributed the strong financial results to robust performances within the Oil-to-Chemicals and Jio Platforms business segments despite volatile global commodity markets.
articles.description: The O2C business emerged as a key growth driver, with revenue surging 44.2% YoY, reflecting a sharp rise in crude and product price.

articles.headline: US warns West Asian allies to prepare for possible Iran military strikes
articles.title: U.S. warns allies to prepare for possible Iran strikes, retaliation after elections, say sources
articles.summary: United States officials have advised several West Asian governments to prepare for potential military action against Iran following the United States midterm elections on November 3, 2026. According to two anonymous diplomats, the campaign could last several days and trigger regional retaliation targeting infrastructure. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi stated that Tehran continues pursuing diplomatic solutions, while the United Arab Emirates urged political restraint to prevent wider conflict.
articles.description: The U.S. has told regional allies that the new round of military action could last for several days, but regional officials are bracing for Iran and its proxy groups to retaliate — leading to a fight that could last even longer, the sources said

articles.headline: Israeli opposition condemns Benjamin Netanyahu over foreign interference allegations
articles.title: Israeli opposition accuses Netanyahu of trying to 'delegitimise' election
articles.summary: Israeli opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot and Arab-led party leaders accused Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of attempting to delegitimise recent election results following allegations of foreign funding. The Likud party alleged that voters were bribed to support Arab parties that won nineteen seats. Qatar denied the claims while the Shin Bet security service investigated the suspicions.
articles.description: The PM's Likud party has alleged foreign interference and said Arab-led parties "stole" the election after his coalition lost its majority.

articles.headline: Helicopter crashes in northern Indian state carrying six people
articles.title: Six dead after helicopter crashes in northern Indian state
articles.summary: A search operation is under way after a helicopter carrying five pilgrims and a pilot crashed in Uttarakhand's Chamoli district on Friday afternoon, according to officials. Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami stated that the aircraft lost contact near Joshimath amid heavy rain and poor visibility. The incident follows previous fatal crashes on the region's pilgrimage routes.
articles.description: The aircraft reportedly took off from the Hindu pilgrimage site of Badrinath on Friday afternoon before losing contact.

articles.headline: Israeli forces blow up homes of Palestinians accused of killing soldiers
articles.title: Israeli forces blow up homes of Palestinians accused of killing soldiers
articles.description: Israeli forces demolished the homes of two Palestinians accused of killing two Israeli soldiers in Hebron last week.

articles.headline: Spain's transport minister refuses to resign over a fatal high-speed rail disaster.
articles.title: Spain transport minister says he won't resign over high-speed rail disaster
articles.summary: Spain's Transport Minister Óscar Puente stated he will not resign following a high-speed train collision near Urda in Toledo province that killed at least 69 people. The crash occurred on Wednesday morning when a Renfe train struck a stationary Iryo train. Speaking in Madrid, Puente emphasized his duty is to resolve the crisis rather than step down, while preliminary investigations and leaked audio continue.
articles.description: Óscar Puente has been facing calls to resign after two high-speed trains collided earlier in the week, killing at least 69 people.

articles.headline: Pope Leo urges United Nations to ban lethal autonomous artificial intelligence weapons
articles.title: Pope Leo calls for the disarmament of AI: ‘Machines are tools, not persons’
articles.summary: During a papal address on Friday, Pope Leo XIV called upon United Nations member states to implement concrete measures prohibiting lethal autonomous weapons. The pontiff emphasized that artificial intelligence systems must remain under responsible human oversight and warned against granting legal personhood to machines, echoing sentiments from his previous encyclical regarding technological risks.
articles.description: Pope Leo XIV says AI systems should be "disarmed," adding that humans "have the responsibility to guide, change and, when necessary, reject its applications." In Friday's Papal Address, Pope Leo encourages United Nations member states to "take concrete steps toward banning lethal autonomous weapons" during their meeting in Geneva next month. The address reflects many […]

articles.headline: Pope Leo XIV becomes first pontiff to vote in US election
articles.title: Pope Leo XIV becomes first pontiff to vote in a US election
articles.summary: Pope Leo XIV submitted a mail-in ballot in Illinois for the upcoming midterm elections, marking the first time a sitting pope has voted in a United States election. The Holy See Press Office confirmed the Chicago-born pontiff exercised his civic duty as an eligible citizen, amidst ongoing political tensions and preparations for his upcoming international travels in November.
articles.description: The Chicago-born pontiff, who has a tense relationship with Trump, mailed in a ballot for the midterm elections that will decide control of the US Congress.

articles.headline: Senators briefed on Trump’s ‘insane’ plan to restart war on Iran
articles.title: Senators briefed on Trump’s ‘insane’ plan to restart war on Iran
articles.description: Senator Chris Murphy says he’s been briefed on Trump’s plan to restart the war on Iran.

articles.headline: Bhutan glacial lake flood triggers evacuations along Sankosh River
articles.title: 4,000 moved to safety in Bengal after Bhutan glacial lake outburst triggers flood alert
articles.summary: The Shintaphu glacial lake burst its banks in Bhutan, damaging infrastructure at the Gasa Tshachu hot springs and washing out regional roads. Although no casualties were reported, Indian authorities in West Bengal issued urgent evacuation alerts for residents living near the Sankosh River as floodwaters surged downstream. State officials urged immediate relocations to prevent potential disasters.
articles.description: While the State government says the situation is currently normal, those living in the catchment areas of the Sankosh river and all its tributaries have been asked to evacuate

articles.headline: Russian, Ukrainian humanitarian officials enter Oleshky
articles.title: Russian, Ukrainian humanitarian officials enter Oleshky
articles.description: A humanitarian aid convoy containing both Russian and Ukrainian officials entered the besieged Ukrainian city of Oleshky

articles.headline: Palestinian child survives Israeli gunshot to the head
articles.title: Palestinian child survives Israeli gunshot to the head
articles.description: Imad Salem Zahra, the Palestinian child whose photo went viral after he was shot in the head by Israeli soldiers.

articles.headline: Ukraine reports record Russian casualties as European allies increase military support
articles.title: Ukraine invests in firepower as it inflicts a new Russian casualty record
articles.summary: Ukraine reported a record 49,040 Russian casualties in October, driven largely by extensive drone warfare operations led by military commanders. Meanwhile, European nations including the Netherlands and the United Kingdom pledged billions in fresh military financing and weapon supplies, while Ukraine and Finland agreed to jointly develop an independent sovereign military satellite system starting in 2028.
articles.description: Recent Starlink suspension did not much affect Ukrainian lethality, but Kyiv shows it is losing trust in the US.

articles.headline: Senators briefed on Trump’s ‘insane’ plan to restart war on Iran
articles.title: Senators briefed on Trump’s ‘insane’ plan to restart war on Iran
articles.description: Senator Chris Murphy warns Trump’s reported plan to restart war with Iran could have devastating consequences.

articles.headline: Alphabet shares plunge 12.6% on Nasdaq as AI spending concerns mount
articles.title: Google parent Alphabet’s shares plunge 12.6% as investors question returns from AI spending
articles.summary: Alphabet shares fell 12.64% on the Nasdaq on October 29, 2026, wiping out $482 billion in market value after quarterly results renewed investor anxiety over high artificial intelligence spending. Chief financial officer Anat Ashkenazi reported negative free cash flow of $9.1 billion, driven by $51.4 billion in capital expenditure. Chief business officer Philipp Schindler noted that growing AI Mode search queries reduced advertising revenue.
articles.description: Company reports 25% revenue growth, but quarterly infrastructure spending crosses $51 billion; lower advertising revenue from AI-powered Search queries adds to concerns

articles.headline: Binance reports approximately 6.3 billion dollars stolen in a massive cryptocurrency heist.
articles.title: Binance says $6.3bn stolen in biggest crypto heist in history: What we know
articles.summary: Binance suspended deposits and withdrawals after hackers stole about 6.3 billion dollars in what is recorded as the largest crypto heist in history. Two United States blockchain analysis firms, TRM Labs and Chainalysis, attributed the attack to North Korean hackers. The breach caused significant market drops, while Binance announced it would use company funds to cover all user losses.
articles.description: The world’s largest crypto exchange halts withdrawals as the theft is linked to North Korean hackers.

articles.headline: What we know about Binance's $6.3bn hack
articles.title: What we know about Binance's $6.3bn hack
articles.description: Cyber correspondent Joe Tidy explains more about what is suspected to be the biggest hack in history.

articles.headline: Qatari mediators arrive in Tehran to discuss potential United States and Iran ceasefire
articles.title: Qatari officials in Iran in bid to revive ceasefire deal with US
articles.summary: A delegation of Qatari mediators travelled to Tehran on Friday for high-level consultations aimed at reviving a ceasefire between the United States and Iran. Led by senior adviser Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman bin Jassim Al Thani, the diplomatic mission followed the delivery of a respectful letter from United States Vice President JD Vance to Iranian security chief Mohsen Rezaei, proposing a new framework for negotiations.
articles.description: The mediation mission comes amid speculation about a potential resumption of hostilities.

articles.headline: Constitution must guide judiciary when laws are silent, says Chief Justice Surya Kant
articles.title: Constitution must guide judiciary where law is silent: CJI Surya Kant
articles.summary: Chief Justice of India Surya Kant emphasized that the Constitution must serve as the primary guide for the judiciary when statutory laws fail to address modern challenges such as artificial intelligence and deepfakes. Speaking on October 30, 2026, at the sixtieth anniversary of the Delhi High Court, the Chief Justice praised the institution for its pivotal role in handling complex commercial and civil jurisprudence alongside other Supreme Court officials.
articles.description: Chief Justice of India Surya Kant said the judiciary is now confronted with questions which were scarcely imaginable a decade ago

articles.headline: Google parent Alphabet loses significant market value amid spending concerns
articles.title: Google value plunges by $500bn as its own AI search hits ad sales
articles.summary: Google parent company Alphabet lost over $500 billion in market value after reporting that artificial intelligence summaries on its search engine negatively impacted advertising revenue and profits. Despite total quarterly revenue reaching $127.6 billion, profits fell by 25 percent and free cash flow dropped into negative territory by more than $9 billion. Executives defended the heavy investments in artificial intelligence as necessary for future growth despite investor concerns.
articles.description: Google spooked investors so badly that its stock hit a six-month low, after it revealed its AI own search summaries were affecting ad revenue.

articles.headline: Israel election results show no clear winner as vote counting continues
articles.title: No clear winner in Israel election with nearly 90 percent of votes counted
articles.summary: Nearly ninety percent of ballots have been counted in Israel, leaving both major political blocs short of the sixty-one seats needed to form a government. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s bloc leads with fifty-three projected seats, while Gadi Eisenkot’s opposition bloc expects forty-eight. Final results are expected as soon as Thursday evening. President Isaac Herzog will begin consultations with party leaders next week.
articles.description: Netanyahu's right-wing bloc leads but is falling short of the votes needed to form a government.

articles.headline: British actor Patrick Stewart passes away at age 86
articles.title: Patrick Stewart, Shakespearean actor turned 'Star Trek' and 'X-Men' star, dies at 86
articles.summary: Renowned stage and screen actor Sir Patrick Stewart died at his home in Los Angeles at the age of 86, according to a family statement released on his X account. Known globally for his roles in Star Trek and X-Men, he was knighted by Queen Elizabeth II in 2010. The acclaimed British star passed away following a brief journey with Alzheimer’s disease and Lewy body dementia.
articles.description: Stewart became an actor at age 18 and gained acclaim on the stage as a member of the Royal Shakespeare Company beginning in the 1960s

articles.headline: Russian independent newspaper Novaya Gazeta announces forced closure amid state pressure
articles.title: Russia ‘forces’ closure of investigative newspaper Novaya Gazeta
articles.summary: Independent Russian newspaper Novaya Gazeta announced it will permanently cease operations following intense pressure and scrutiny from authorities amid the ongoing war in Ukraine. Editor-in-chief Sergei Sokolov stated that the editorial staff was compelled to shut down the publication after thirty years, marking another major blow to press freedom in Russia following previous government crackdowns, police raids, and the arrest of several staff members.
articles.description: A symbol of independent journalism, Novaya Gazeta has been classed as a 'foreign agent' by Moscow.

articles.headline: Maine Senate race spotlighted by rural voter backlash against artificial intelligence data centers
articles.title: Maine’s data center revolt will decide who controls the Senate
articles.summary: Rural voters in Maine are pushing back heavily against the rapid expansion of resource-hungry artificial intelligence data centers, making the technology a pivotal issue in the state's expensive Senate race between Republican incumbent Susan Collins and challenger Troy Jackson. With tech billionaires pouring record funds into the campaign, residents have expressed serious concerns over rising utility costs, water usage, and a lack of long-term jobs.
articles.description: Maine Sen. Susan Collins, a Republican, was midway through defending her record during the final debate of the midterms when an audience member cut her short. "I'm terrified," a man shouted. "AI data centers are destroying our climate. They are poisoning our water." Collins brushed off the outburst, tying the man to her Democratic challenger, […]

articles.headline: Aid convoy enters Russian-held Oleshky amid ongoing ceasefire
articles.title: Aid convoy enters besieged Ukrainian town Oleshky
articles.summary: An aid convoy carrying food and medical supplies reached the Russian-held town of Oleshky in Ukraine under a six-day localised truce. Ukrainian and Russian officials met to coordinate evacuations for residents remaining without power, heat or running water. Meanwhile, separate Russian strikes targeted Kyiv, Kharkiv and other regions, while air defences intercepted dozens of drones near Moscow.
articles.description: Moscow and Kyiv have so far observed the six-day truce as evacuations from Oleshky get under way.

articles.headline: United States weighs renewed military strikes on Iran while diplomatic outreach continues
