articles.description: Flávio Bolsonaro vows to continue father's political fight in Brazil

articles.headline: Venezuelan opposition leader Maria Corina Machado calls for elections next year
articles.title: Venezuela opposition leader María Machado calls for elections upon return
articles.summary: Venezuelan opposition leader María Corina Machado has called for national elections to be held in 2027 during a news conference in Caracas on Thursday. The Nobel Peace Prize winner dismissed interim president Delcy Rodríguez's plans for a transition as illogical. Machado returned to the country following the United States seizure of former president Nicolás Maduro and praised the Trump administration for opening the floodgate to freedom.
articles.description: Machado, who was in exile for nearly a year, said the transition in Venezuela's government would be "irreversible, organised, pacific".

articles.headline: Watch: What leaked audio reveals about Spain train crash
articles.title: Watch: What leaked audio reveals about Spain train crash
articles.description: Recordings between a control centre and the train drivers appear to show one train was given clearance to move even though another train had stalled on the track.

articles.headline: Israeli forces escalate raids and displacement across West Bank
articles.title: Palestinians injured, arrested in Israeli raids across West Bank
articles.summary: Israeli military forces and settlers have intensified raids, arrests, and home demolitions across the occupied West Bank. A military offensive in the Hebron governorate has entered its seventh day, displacing thousands of residents and disrupting education for over two hundred thousand students. The United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs has called for an end to the forced displacements.
articles.description: This comes as more than 3,300 Palestinians are forced from homes in Hebron as Israel's military offensive continues.

articles.headline: Telangana farmers shift toward horticulture crops to combat weather challenges
articles.title: Telangana farmers’ preference for veggies, spices over paddy continues in Yasangi 2026
articles.summary: Farmers in Telangana continue cultivating vegetables and spices instead of traditional paddy during the Yasangi season due to weather impacts. State Horticulture Director Shaik Yasmeen Basha reported increased sowing areas and noted that officials are providing drought-resistant seeds and irrigation resources. District officers stated that market demand and borewell irrigation heavily drive this ongoing agricultural transition across several districts.
articles.description: Excessive heat conditions in the next few months may bring down horticulture produce by around 20%, which may drive demand, says Telangana Horticulture Department’s Director Shaik Yasmeen Basha

articles.headline: Telangana plans public-private partnership model to improve hospital MRI services
articles.title: Telangana plans PPP model to ensure uninterrupted MRI services at govt hospitals
articles.summary: The Telangana government plans to adopt a Public-Private Partnership model to operate magnetic resonance imaging services across state hospitals, aiming to resolve technical disruptions. Health Minister C. Damodara Raja Narasimha announced that scans will remain free for referred patients, following a pilot project in Mahabubnagar. Officials estimate the arrangement will reduce government expenditure by approximately twenty percent compared to existing systems.
articles.description: Health Minister C. Damodara Raja Narasimha clarified that scans will remain free of cost for patients referred by doctors at Telangana government hospitals

articles.headline: Aam Aadmi Party releases first candidate list for Punjab Assembly elections
articles.title: AAP announces first list of 40 candidates for 2027 Punjab Assembly elections
articles.summary: The Aam Aadmi Party released its first list of forty candidates for the Punjab Assembly election scheduled early next year, fielding exclusively sitting legislators. Chief Minister Bhagwall Mann confirmed his candidacy from the Dhuri constituency in Sangrur district during a press briefing on October 31, 2026. The ruling party selected candidates based on public survey responses to campaign effectively ahead of the March 16 poll.
articles.description: Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann will seek re-election from the Dhuri constituency in Sangrur district

articles.headline: Israeli elections conclude with neither political bloc winning majority
articles.title: Israel election result shows no overall majority as vote count complete
articles.summary: Vote counting is complete in Israel's parliamentary elections, leaving both Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc and the opposition short of the sixty-one seats required for a majority. Opposition leaders have met to explore coalition options as provisional results indicate Netanyahu's bloc secured fifty-three seats while the opposition led by Gadi Eisenkot won forty-eight seats in the Knesset.
articles.description: Opposition explores options to form coalition as no party secures the 61 seats required for parliamentary majority.

articles.headline: One Planet Partners launches maiden fund to deploy over 3,000 crore rupees in India
articles.title: One Planet Partners to deploy over ₹3,000 crore in high-growth business in India
articles.summary: India-focused private equity firm One Planet Partners announced a partnership with Japan's Sumitomo Mitsui Trust Bank on October 29, 2026. The collaboration includes a maiden fund targeting over 3,000 crore rupees for mid-market businesses in energy, mobility, and manufacturing. Bengaluru electric mobility company Yulu serves as the first investment. The founding team includes industry veterans Mukund Rajan, Bobby Pauly, Mrinalini Mirchandani, and Sheetal Thakkar.
articles.description: The fund would focus on high-growth mid-market businesses across energy, mobility and manufacturing, with scale-up capital of ₹ 100–500 crore for enterprises with revenue between ₹200 and 2,000 crore, says One Planet Partners, an India-focused private equity firm

articles.headline: Narendra Modi inaugurates tourism and infrastructure projects in Ekta Nagar
articles.title: PM Modi inaugurates tourism, infrastructure projects worth ₹307 crore in Gujarat's Ekta Nagar
articles.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated twenty-three development projects worth 307.83 crore rupees and laid foundation stones for eight others in Ekta Nagar, Gujarat, on October 31, 2026. The initiatives aim to upgrade visitor facilities and civic infrastructure around the Statue of Unity. The program coincided with Rashtriya Ekta Diwas, marking the birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel.
articles.description: The Prime Minister also laid the foundation stones for eight development projects worth ₹118.88 crore, taking the total outlay for the 31 projects to ₹426.71 crore

articles.headline: Sudan paramilitary commander Siddiq Ander defects from Rapid Support Forces
articles.title: RSF senior commander defects, accusing Sudan group’s leadership of nepotism
articles.summary: A senior commander of Sudan‘s Rapid Support Forces announced his departure in video footage published on Friday, accusing relatives of group leader Mohamed Hamdan Dagalo of tightly controlling finances and military promotions. The exit follows several high-profile defections this year amid an ongoing conflict between the army and the paramilitary group that has displaced millions.
articles.description: In exclusive footage obtained by Al Jazeera, Siddiq Ander describes RSF as a 'purely family-based project'.

articles.headline: Russian satellites assist Houthi attacks against Saudi Arabia, investigation reveals
articles.title: Are Houthis using Russian satellites as Saudi Arabia fends off strikes?
articles.summary: An investigation by Geneva-based firm AURORAH Geosignal Intelligence revealed that Russian military and reconnaissance satellites observed targeted areas before and after forty attacks against Saudi Arabia. Three officials confirmed that the Iran-aligned Houthis have benefited from Russian intelligence alongside Chinese capabilities to target energy infrastructure.
articles.description: Analysts say the seizure of state arsenals, external backing and extensive military evolution has helped the Houthis.

articles.headline: Coastal Andhra Pradesh fisherfolk face financial crisis amid weather bans
articles.title: Coastal Andhra Pradesh fisherfolk face severe financial crisis amid Cyclones and frequent weather bans
articles.summary: Marine fishing communities in coastal Andhra Pradesh are facing severe financial distress due to frequent weather warnings and compulsory fishing bans issued by the India Meteorological Department. Cumulative losses have exceeded 36 crore rupees following multiple severe weather events, prompting fisherfolk organisations to petition Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu for enhanced financial compensation.
articles.description: Repeated bans across four major weather alerts since June have caused cumulative losses exceeding ₹36 crore

articles.headline: German companies view Hyderabad as base for innovation and research
articles.title: German companies looking at Hyderabad as base for innovation, research: Consul General Michael Hasper
articles.summary: German businesses are increasingly looking at Hyderabad as a hub for technology development due to the city's pharmaceutical ecosystem, engineering talent, and global capability centres. Speaking in Hyderabad on October 30, 2026, German Consul General Michael Hasper highlighted the mutual benefits of connecting Telangana's skilled workforce with opportunities in Germany.

articles.headline: Saudi air defences intercept hostile drone in Riyadh region
articles.title: Saudi Arabia says intercepted ‘hostile drone’ in Riyadh region
articles.summary: Military coalition spokesman Turki al-Malki stated that air defences destroyed an incoming drone on October 31, 2026. Debris fell without causing injuries, and the perpetrator remains unidentified. The incident occurs amid heightened regional hostilities involving Yemen's Houthis, who have recently increased attacks on Saudi infrastructure following the collapse of a 2022 truce over the summer.
articles.description: No information yet on who launched the drone

articles.headline: Prime Minister Modi praises ISRO scientists for successful satellite launch
articles.title: Launch of NVS-03: PM Modi congratulates scientists, engineers at ISRO
articles.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi congratulated teams at the Indian Space Research Organisation following the October 31, 2026, launch of the GSLV-F18 rocket carrying the NVS-03 satellite. Officials noted the mission strengthens the indigenous NavIC navigation system and supports civilian applications like real-time tracking, advancing the nation toward technological self-reliance.
articles.description: Mr. Modi also said that equipped with enhanced capabilities, NVS-03 will further India’s pursuit of self-reliance in critical technologies and support navigation services that benefit the people

articles.headline: Donald Trump describes Brazil election as a disgrace
articles.title: Trump says won’t ‘take sides’ in Brazil election, but calls it a ‘disgrace’
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump stated he did not take sides in Brazil's presidential election won by Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, but described the contest as a disgrace. The remarks followed the arrival in Miami of former Brazilian Senator Flavio Bolsonaro, who fled Brazil with his family. The Brazilian real dropped twelve percent following the election outcome.
articles.description: Comments come after Trump ally Flavio Bolsonaro fled to Miami in US and claimed, without evidence, that vote was stolen.

articles.headline: Netanyahu attacks Palestinian-Israeli parties as he falls short of majority
articles.title: Netanyahu attacks Palestinian-Israeli parties as he falls short of majority
articles.description: With all votes now counted, opposition parties could join forces with Palestinian-Israeli parties to unseat Netanyahu.

articles.headline: Arab political parties secure surge in votes during Israeli parliamentary elections
articles.title: ‘Arab voice doesn’t count’: Jewish Israeli blocs reject Palestinian support
articles.summary: Palestinian citizens of Israel turned out in high numbers during Tuesday's parliamentary elections, securing nineteen seats for the United Arab List and the Joint List. While analysts noted motivations included anger over the war in Gaza, ruling politicians and several Jewish opposition figures rejected potential cooperation, with Likud calling for a security investigation into the turnout.
articles.description: Palestinian voters could decide Israel’s future, but its political class refuses to accept their mandate

articles.headline: US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth fires Lieutenant General Brett Sylvia
articles.title: Pentagon fires general it says leaked classified information to media
articles.summary: United States Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth dismissed Lieutenant General Brett Sylvia from his role as director of the Strategy, Plans and Policy Directorate at the Joint Chiefs of Staff. According to Pentagon officials, Sylvia faces an ongoing investigation for allegedly leaking classified information regarding military conflicts to journalists outside the department.
articles.description: Army Lieutenant General Brett Sylvia was subject of investigation into leaking information about Iran and Ukraine.

articles.headline: K.T. Rama Rao questions Union government over proposed IDBI Bank sale
articles.title: KTR questions proposed sale of IDBI Bank, asks if its valuable real estate assets were factored in valuation
articles.summary: Bharat Rashtra Samithi working president K.T. Rama Rao questioned the Union government's proposed sale of IDBI Bank to a private entity, raising concerns regarding valuation methods, bidding norm changes, and employee grievances. In a statement on October 31, 2026, the BRS leader asked whether prime real estate assets in Hyderabad were factored into the valuation and questioned the urgency behind the privatization of the public sector bank.
articles.description: BRS working president sought to know why the concerns raised by IDBI Bank employees over the proposed disinvestment were not being addressed

articles.headline: Tamil Nadu Congress and VCK mobilise cadres for New Delhi protest
articles.title: Tamil Nadu Congress, VCK mobilise cadres for Nov. 1 INDIA bloc protest in New Delhi
articles.summary: Demanding the removal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, the Tamil Nadu Congress Committee and Viduthalai Chiruthaigal Katchi have activated party networks to mobilise cadres for an INDIA bloc protest in New Delhi on November 1, 2026. According to Mayiladuthurai Member of Parliament R. Sudha, the Indian National Congress expects over five lakh participants, while alleging that the Bharatiya Janata Party-led Centre is curtailing parliamentary privileges.
articles.description: “We expect more than five lakh Congress cadres to participate. From Tamil Nadu, we are expecting at least 100 party workers to reach New Delhi from each district,” says MP R. Sudha

articles.headline: Authorities resume operations to recover chopper crash victims in Uttarakhand
articles.title: Operation underway to recover bodies from remote chopper crash site in Uttarakhand
articles.summary: Rescue operations resumed on October 31, 2026, to recover the bodies of six victims from a helicopter crash in Joshimath, Uttarakhand. The Trans Bharat Aviation private helicopter was returning from Badrinath when it crashed, killing the pilot and five pilgrims from Karnataka. Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami stated that an investigation into the cause is underway by the Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau.
articles.description: A team from the forest department, Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau officials, a DGCA team have all been dispatched to the crash site

articles.headline: Karnataka places three-year moratorium on new private PU colleges
articles.title: Karnataka places three-year moratorium on permission for new private PU colleges
articles.summary: To regulate pre-university education, the Karnataka government has proposed a three-year moratorium on new private PU colleges for the 2027 to 2030 academic years. The draft rules follow data showing available seats outpace passing students, leaving thousands vacant. The Karnataka State Pre-University Colleges Lecturers Association welcomed the move while calling for improved government college infrastructure.
articles.description: The decision to restrict opening of new colleges comes in the backdrop of the number of seats available in I PU increasing every year, outpacing the number of students passing SSLC exams

articles.headline: Kerala Crime Branch registers FIR against KPSC chairperson and members
articles.title: Keralam PSC exam fraud: Crime Branch indicts chairperson, members on charges of corruption, political favouritism
articles.summary: The Special Investigation Team of the Crime Branch registered an FIR on October 28 against Kerala State Public Service Commission chairperson M.R. Baiju and other members. Investigators allege criminal breach of trust and misuse of authority to favor Communist Party of India Marxist candidates in Fisheries Extension Officer recruitment exams. The action follows previous arrests and a gubernatorial recommendation for removal.
articles.description: FIR indicts chairperson, other members for criminal breach of trust and wrongful employment of their constitutionally sanctioned authority to tilt the playing field in favour of candidates owing allegiance to CPI(M) by tweaking rank list for post of Fisheries Extension Officer

articles.headline: Andaman Sea low pressure system intensifies into well-marked low
articles.title: Low pressure over Andaman Sea intensifies further
articles.summary: A low-pressure area over the Andaman Sea intensified into a well-marked low-pressure system by October 31, 2026, according to the India Meteorological Department in Amaravati. The system is projected to move west-northwestwards, potentially becoming a depression near the Andhra Pradesh coast. Forecasters noted that further intensification into a cyclone remains uncertain until subsequent cyclogenesis occurs.
articles.description: IMD says the well-marked low pressure is centred near southeast Bay of Bengal as of Saturday morning and is expected to concentrate into a depression off Andhra Pradesh by night

articles.headline: Isro launches NVS-03 satellite with open pyro valves to ensure mission reliability
articles.title: To overcome technical hurdles, ISRO flew NVS-03 satellite with pyro valves open: Narayanan
articles.summary: Indian Space Research Organisation successfully deployed the 2,240 kg NVS-03 navigation satellite using the GSLV-F18 rocket on October 31, 2026. Chairman V. Narayanan stated the spacecraft flew with three pyro valves open to bypass previous technical hurdles. The mission restores NavIC to four active satellites, aiding location services for thousands of locomotives and fishing vessels across India.
articles.description: Pyro valves are crucial in spacecraft propulsion, and it may be recalled that the NVS-02 (launched in 2025), the second spacecraft in the NVS series, was a failure

articles.headline: Telangana broadens instant pension access for women who lose their husbands
articles.title: Telangana extends ‘Instant pension’ facility beyond old-age pension category for women
articles.summary: The Telangana government expanded its instant pension scheme to include families of individuals with disabilities, handloom weavers, and dialysis patients. Eligible widows under 57 will receive widow pensions, while those aged 57 and older will obtain old-age pensions. Applicants must submit documents to local authorities in rural or urban areas to ensure uninterrupted financial support.
articles.description: The decision will benefit the families of persons with disabilities, toddy tappers, handloom weavers, dialysis patients and those affected by HIV and filariasis

articles.headline: Field trainers prepare enumerators for upcoming population enumeration phase of census
articles.title: Census 2027: What are the new questions, and how are enumerators being trained? | Explained
articles.summary: Field trainers are preparing enumerators in Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Goa and Punjab for the second phase of the census beginning on December 1, 2026. Enumerators will ask forty questions, including thirteen new categories covering details such as caste, religion and Aadhaar numbers, requiring approximately twenty to twenty-five minutes per respondent across blocks of up to eight hundred people.
articles.description: As Uttar Pradesh and three other poll-bound States — Uttarakhand, Goa and Punjab — prepare to launch the second phase of Census 2027 on December 1, field trainers are briefing about 34 lakh enumerators on 40 questions that will require longer, more sensitive interviews and digital data entry, including caste, religion, Aadhaar access and parents’ details

articles.headline: S. Jaishankar meets G20 counterparts to discuss bilateral cooperation and trade
articles.title: Jaishankar, Anita Anand agree that Modi’s Canada visit in December will be ‘another building block’
articles.summary: External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar met Canadian counterpart Anita Anand on October 30, 2026, in Atlanta during the G20 Foreign Ministers' Meeting to evaluate bilateral cooperation. Jaishankar also held discussions with foreign ministers Pablo Quirno of Argentina, Roberto Velasco Alvarez of Mexico, Mauro Vieira of Brazil, and Johann Wadephul of Germany, focusing on trade, defence, and critical minerals.
articles.description: External Affairs Minister Jaishankar met Canadian counterpart Anita Anand in Atlanta on the sidelines of the G20 Foreign Ministers’ Meeting

articles.headline: What has it cost to keep Al Jazeera on air for 30 years?
articles.title: What has it cost to keep Al Jazeera on air for 30 years?
articles.description: For 30 years, Al Jazeera went where others couldn’t. Or wouldn’t. AJLabs traces the price of staying on air.

articles.headline: Cyclone Arnab causes estimated forty six billion rupees damage in Andhra Pradesh
articles.title: Cyclone Arnab: Andhra Pradesh puts estimated loss at ₹4,600 crore
articles.summary: Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu reported an estimated loss of forty six billion rupees following Cyclone Arnab. Naidu conducted aerial surveys and interacted with flood victims in the Krishna and Godavari regions. Seven casualties were recorded while restoration efforts continue. A Central team will visit affected districts on Friday to assess agricultural damage and provide compensation to residents.
articles.description: Central team to arrive in Andhra Pradesh to assess cyclone damage October 30; A.P. urges Telangana to deploy 1,000 personnel for power restoration work in the Godavari region

articles.headline: Yemeni families face deep economic hardship following heavy fighter casualties
articles.title: After the ‘martyr’s’ funeral: The families left behind by Yemen’s war
articles.summary: Grieving relatives in Houthi-controlled Sanaa struggle with severe financial strain and soaring fuel prices after losing family members in ongoing conflict. Houthi authorities provide irregular food assistance, but bereaved relatives argue that the support remains insufficient against widespread food insecurity. The United Nations reports millions facing severe food insecurity across Yemen amidst escalating fighting.
articles.description: Rising fatalities in Yemen’s conflict deepen the burden on families of fighters, both emotionally and financially.

articles.headline: Global powers race to place nuclear reactors on moon for lunar base power
articles.title: Why are US, Russia and China racing to put nuclear reactors on the moon?
articles.summary: The United States, Russia, and China are developing compact nuclear reactors to power future lunar bases and water ice mining near the moon's south pole. NASA aims to launch a 20-kilowatt reactor by 2030, while Russia plans the Selena reactor by 2036. Experts note that nuclear energy is essential due to the limitations of solar power during lunar nights.
articles.description: Reactors could revolutionise moon exploration, providing energy for bases and mining, but risks of contamination remain.

articles.headline: Prime Minister Modi pays tribute to Sardar Patel in Gujarat
articles.title: PM Modi offers floral tributes to Sardar Patel at Statue of Unity
articles.summary: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi paid floral tributes to Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel at the Statue of Unity in Ekta Nagar, Gujarat, on the leader's 151st birth anniversary. October 31 is observed nationally as Rashtriya Ekta Diwas to honor Patel, who served as India's first home minister and integrated over 560 princely states into the Indian Union following independence in 1947.
articles.description: October 31 is observed every year as National Unity Day to commemorate the birth anniversary of Sardar Patel, who played a pivotal role in integrating princely states into the Indian Union after Independence

articles.headline: France deploys security forces ahead of weekend protests
articles.title: Fears of violence as France braces for Halloween protests
articles.summary: French authorities deployed approximately 70,000 security personnel across the country to prevent widespread street violence during a third weekend of demonstrations coinciding with Halloween. Interior Minister Laurent Nunez warned of a high risk of public disorder amid cost-of-living protests and political tension, prompting businesses to board up storefronts and authorities to implement curfews and transport disruptions in Paris.
articles.description: Around 70,000 security personnel will be deployed on Saturday (October 31, 2026), matching the number mobilised a week ago, as authorities seek to avert a repeat of the October 17 unrest

articles.headline: Emirati court sentences eight individuals to life imprisonment over Sudan arms supplies
articles.title: UAE sentences eight people to life over arms supplies to Sudan’s army
articles.summary: An Emirati court sentenced eight people to life imprisonment for arms trafficking and money laundering linked to Sudan's army. The Abu Dhabi Federal Court of Appeal stated the accused operated an illicit network supplying military equipment while forging documents through local companies. The convicts will face deportation after serving their sentences, according to state media reports published Thursday.
articles.description: Defendants handed ⁠life sentences amid tensions between Khartoum and Abu Dhabi over Sudan's war and the RSF.

articles.headline: Supreme Court expresses concern over widespread violation of firecracker restrictions
articles.title: Our orders breached ‘left and right’, Deepavali was a festival of lights before gunpowder, Supreme Court says in firecrackers case
articles.summary: The Supreme Court stated that its orders restricting firecrackers during Deepavali had been breached repeatedly. Justices M.M. Sundresh and P.B. Varale emphasized that religious freedom remains subject to public health protections. The bench directed authorities to enhance enforcement against sellers of banned crackers and requested an affidavit detailing preventive measures taken by the government.
articles.description: A complete ban may have a ‘spiralling effect’, the court says, asks the Centre and the Delhi government to ensure enforcement against sellers of spurious and banned crackers

articles.headline: Mohammed Deif, rare footage and October 7 documents
articles.title: Mohammed Deif, rare footage and October 7 documents
articles.description: Rare footage obtained by Al Jazeera offers a look at the life of former Hamas military commander, Mohammed Deif.

articles.headline: Record Pacific ocean heat indicates potential for ferocious El Nino event
articles.title: A ferocious El Niño is brewing thanks to record Pacific heat
articles.summary: Climate scientists are monitoring record-breaking sea surface temperatures in the central-equatorial Pacific Ocean. According to the United States National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration Climate Prediction Center, a strong to very strong El Nino carries an 83 percent probability. The natural climate pattern frequently triggers global extreme heatwaves and altered rainfall patterns across the world.
articles.description: Since the modern era of instrumental records began, there have only been three very strong El Niño events, in 2015-16, 1997-98, and 1982-83, with the three-month averages of the temperature anomaly being 2.6°, 2.4°, and 2.1°C, respectively. The 2026-27 El Niño is projected to peak with an anomaly of 3.8°C

articles.headline: Kashmiri traditional rice varieties reveal genetic links to East Asia
articles.title: In Kashmir’s traditional rice, clues to a journey from East Asia
articles.summary: Researchers at the Sher-e-Kashmir University of Agricultural Sciences and Technology in Srinagar published a study in The Plant Genome revealing that traditional Kashmiri rice varieties possess cold-tolerance genes and share close genetic ties with crops from the Korean Peninsula and Northeast China. These locally adapted traits could prove valuable for agriculture as climate change places increasing environmental stress on modern crop yields.
articles.description: Kashmir’s traditional varieties carry cold-tolerance and other locally adapted genes that modern varieties have partly lost, making them potentially valuable as climate change increases stress on crops, new research has found. The analysis also indicated the varieties are more closely related to those from the Korean Peninsula and Northeast China

articles.headline: Researchers document a rare biological phenomenon of transmissible malignancies in wildlife populations.
articles.title: Scientists unearth new instance of ‘contagious cancer’ in animals
articles.summary: Although neoplasms typically arise internally from an individual host cell and remain non-transmissible, researchers have previously identified three exceptional cases where naturally occurring malignancies in fauna became transmissible between hosts. Published on October 21, 2026, this finding highlights a rare biological phenomenon in which malignant cells physically transfer to new organisms to establish tumors, expanding scientific understanding of how certain diseases spread among animal populations globally.
articles.description: Researchers studied melanoma in the brown bullhead catfish, a resident of Lake Memphremagog, between Quebec in Canada and Vermont in the U.S.; the finding is interesting because it could reveal clues to keeping a human’s body from rejecting a transplanted organ

articles.headline: Oracle will offer Google Tensor Processing Units through cloud platform from 2027
articles.title: Oracle opens cloud to Google’s AI chips, challenging GPU dominance
articles.summary: Oracle announced on October 27 at an event in Las Vegas that it will offer Google's Tensor Processing Units through its cloud infrastructure platform starting in 2027. The partnership allows Oracle customers to access Google's custom AI chips alongside other architectures, providing more options for training and deploying artificial intelligence models.
articles.description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure will offer Google’s TPUs from 2027, giving customers another option for AI training and inference

articles.headline: Cyclone Arnab brings heavy rain and severe flooding to southern Odisha districts
articles.title: Post-Arnab cyclone, heavy rain wreaks havoc in Odisha’s Ganjam, Gajapati districts
articles.summary: Severe downpours triggered by cyclone Arnab inundated hundreds of villages and washed away roads in the Ganjam and Gajapati districts of Odisha on October 29, 2026. The India Meteorological Department reported record rainfall totals, prompting the state government to deploy disaster response units. The Indian Coast Guard also airlifted stranded residents from severely flooded areas.
articles.description: More than 200 villages in 22 blocks across Ganjam and Gajapati districts severely affected; roads washed away, villages marooned and three rivers are in spate

articles.headline: Two Chinese nationals sentenced to prison for US espionage
articles.title: US jails two Chinese nationals for spying
articles.summary: Two Chinese nationals, Liren Lai and Yuance Chen, were sentenced to 30 months in prison by a United States court after admitting to attempting to recruit military service members to spy for Beijing. The United States Department of Justice stated the men operated a scheme involving secret cash payments and gathered information on naval facilities and military personnel starting around May 2021 before being arrested.
articles.description: Liren Lai and Yuance Chen admitted to facilitating 'dead drop' cash payments worth at least $30,000 to people in the US.

articles.headline: Supreme Court voids Karnataka law validating the disputed 2011 civil services recruitment
articles.title: Supreme Court strikes down Karnataka law validating ‘corrupt’ 2011 recruitment
articles.summary: The Supreme Court on October 29, 2026, struck down a Karnataka state law that sought to validate the 2011 recruitment of gazetted probationers. A bench comprising Justices J.B. Pardiwala and K. Vinod Chandran ruled that the legislation was unconstitutional because it attempted to override previous court judgments against the corrupt selection process. The court ordered a fresh recruitment drive with age relaxations for affected candidates.
articles.description: Top court says cancellation of the recruitment process was upheld by both HC and SC, and that the 'power does not lie with the legislature to annul the cancellation, even by a legislation, and thus nullify the judgments of the Constitutional courts’

articles.headline: European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde announces her early resignation
articles.title: European Central Bank President Lagarde to step down early
articles.summary: European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde announced on October 29, 2026, that she will step down on February 7, nine months before her term concludes. The early departure aims to allow European Union leaders to choose her successor prior to the French presidential election in April. Lagarde steered the institution through multiple crises since taking office in October 2019.
articles.description: Christine Lagarde will leave the post in February, nine months before the end of her eight-year term.

articles.headline: Four tankers catch fire after striking naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz
articles.title: Iran says four tankers on fire after hitting mines in Hormuz
articles.summary: Four oil tankers caught fire after hitting naval mines while navigating the Strait of Hormuz on October 29, 2026, according to statements from the Iranian armed forces. The incidents occurred shortly after the United States military asserted that it had cleared key transit routes through the strategic waterway. Furthermore, the Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps claimed responsibility for capturing a United States reconnaissance drone.
articles.description: The vessels had "switched off all their radar and navigation systems" and disregarded warnings from the IRGC navy, the statement said

articles.headline: Flavio Bolsonaro confirms departure from Brazil following presidential election defeat
articles.title: Flavio Bolsonaro says he left Brazil because he is the victim of 'persecution'
articles.summary: Former conservative presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro confirmed during an Instagram livestream that he fled Brazil for the United States to escape political persecution. Having lost the October 25 election runoff to President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, the senator secretly left the country after authorities cancelled his passports amid a money laundering investigation. He criticised Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes and alleged election irregularities.
articles.description: "The persecution began even sooner than I imagined," Mr. Bolsonaro said during an Instagram livestream in which he discussed his decision to flee after his Brazilian passports were cancelled as part of a money laundering investigation

articles.headline: Microsoft expands global data centre network as quarterly revenue rises
articles.title: Microsoft expands AI infrastructure, adds 24 data centres to its 500-plus global kitty in Q1 FY27
articles.summary: Technology giant Microsoft added twenty-four data centres globally during the September quarter to meet rising cloud and artificial intelligence demand, CEO Satya Nadella announced on October twenty-eighth, 2026. The company reported ninety-two point three billion dollars in revenue and thirty-six point six billion dollars in net profit, driven by strong growth in Azure and overall cloud services.
articles.description: Company spends $45.2 billion on capital expenditure in Q1; says GPU deployment times fell 20% and Copilot workload throughput rose over 50%

articles.headline: Census trainers address complex questions on Aadhaar and caste ahead of enumeration
articles.title: Census trainers flag queries on Aadhaar, caste, age and birthplace of parents as key challenges
articles.summary: Field trainers in Uttar Pradesh are preparing enumerators for the second phase of India's digital Census 2027 by addressing challenging queries regarding Aadhaar, parental birthplace, and open-ended caste data. Senior Census officials clarified that Aadhaar collection remains optional and is not linked to citizenship verification, while field training sessions continue across poll-bound states ahead of door-to-door data collection starting December first, 2026.
articles.description: At an enumerator training session attended by The Hindu, a trainer explains how to coax respondents to share Aadhaar data, including that it could be used as citizenship proof, though Census officials denied giving any instructions in this regard

articles.headline: Cybersecurity experts link North Korean hackers to record cryptocurrency thefts
articles.title: North Korean hackers linked to crypto thefts among world's best, experts say
articles.summary: Cybersecurity experts and blockchain firms stated on October 31, 2026, that North Korean hacking groups are responsible for massive cryptocurrency heists, including a record theft from Binance. According to researchers, these cyberattacks and illicit overseas operations generate vital funds for the regime of leader Kim Jong Un to support its nuclear and military programs.
articles.description: A US State Department ‌spokesman said North Korean cybercrime is a “global problem”

articles.headline: Bharatiya Janata Party wins thirteen of twenty-eight legislative council seats
articles.title: Why are paper ballots used for MLC polls? Explained
articles.summary: The Bharatiya Janata Party won thirteen of twenty-eight seats in recent legislative council elections held on October 23, 2026, while coalition partners secured additional victories. Prime Minister Narendra Modi publicly criticized the Congress party following its poor performance and use of paper ballots, noting its previous demands to abandon electronic voting machines.
articles.description: MLC elections use proportional representation through a single transferable vote. Voters rank candidates instead of picking just one. EVMs are built for “first-past-the-post elections” in India in which voter chooses one candidate, so they cannot record ranked preferences

articles.headline: Microsoft offers voluntary buyouts to employees amid artificial intelligence transition
articles.title: Microsoft’s AI future has fewer jobs
articles.summary: Microsoft is offering voluntary exit packages to approximately sixty thousand employees across the United States, United Kingdom, Canada, and India as CEO Satya Nadella restructures the workforce around artificial intelligence infrastructure. The company reduced its headcount by five thousand people over the past year, bringing total employment to roughly two hundred twenty-three thousand by June thirtieth, 2025, while continuing strategic investments in graphics processing units.
articles.description: To anyone listening closely to what Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella has been saying over the past couple of years, this week felt like the clearest sign yet that AI is about to fundamentally change the size of Microsoft's workforce. Microsoft is now offering voluntary buyouts to around 60,000 employees across the US, UK, Canada, and […]

articles.headline: Netanyahu leads Israel election with partial results showing no majority
articles.title: Netanyahu's bloc leading Israel election but short of majority, partial results show
articles.summary: Partial results from Israel's general election on October 27, 2026, indicate Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's right-wing bloc leads rival Gadi Eisenkot, though both remain short of a parliamentary majority. With high voter turnout recorded across the country, Arab-led parties are positioned to win a record number of seats, potentially serving as crucial kingmakers as President Isaac Herzog prepares to oversee coalition negotiations.
articles.description: With 99% of ballots counted, Netanyahu's Likud party and its allies are set to win 53 seats in the 120-seat Knesset.

articles.headline: Serbian student movement demands resignations of top police and judicial officials
articles.title: Serbia’s students demand resignations in police, judiciary as they prepare to take power
articles.summary: Serbia's student movement demanded the immediate resignations of senior police, intelligence, and judicial officials on October twenty-ninth, 2026, following a historic parliamentary election victory over former leader Aleksandar Vucic. Student representatives urged election authorities to finalize results after upcoming reruns, while calling on public servants to protect institutional documents from destruction during the ongoing political transition.
articles.description: The Students’ List movement swept the parliamentary election on October 25, 2026 against Vucic’s right-wing Serbian Progressive Party, which has ruled unchallenged for 14 years

articles.headline: US execution survivor Christa Pike speaks out after botched lethal injection
articles.title: US execution survivor Christa Pike says she is now in ‘constant pain’
articles.summary: Christa Pike, a fifty-year-old prisoner in Tennessee who survived a botched execution on September thirty, stated through her legal team that she experiences constant physical and emotional pain. Her lawyers requested that Republican Governor Bill Lee commute her sentence to life in prison following the failed lethal injection administered by the Tennessee Department of Correction.
articles.description: Pike, 50, is being held in solitary confinement and faces an uncertain future after surviving a failed lethal injection.

articles.headline: Gaza health ministry urges Rafah crossing reopening amid ongoing Israeli strikes
articles.title: Israeli strikes hit Gaza as Health Ministry urges Rafah opening
articles.summary: Recent Israeli attacks across the Gaza Strip killed at least two people and wounded dozens, prompting the Ministry of Health to urgently call for the reopening of the Rafah border crossing. According to the ministry, over 21,000 patients require medical treatment abroad, but prolonged border closures have led to numerous deaths. The escalation involves continuous drone and artillery strikes in multiple areas including Gaza City, Jabalia, and Khan Younis.
articles.description: Gaza's Health Ministry says dozens died awaiting treatment abroad as Israeli attacks continue despite a 'ceasefire'.

articles.headline: U.S. cancels G20 foreign ministers photo over Russia
articles.title: U.S. scraps G20 family photo after Europeans object to being pictured with Russia's Lavrov
articles.summary: United States Secretary of State Marco Rubio cancelled a traditional group photograph at the Group of Twenty talks in Atlanta after European diplomats objected to appearing alongside Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov. The diplomatic gathering precedes a December leaders summit in Florida hosted by President Donald Trump amidst widespread international and domestic political tensions.
articles.description: The cancellation has added to concerns about the poor prospects for the G20 diplomats to reach consensus on many of the most contentious issues they face

articles.headline: Police in Odisha arrest doctor and activist following violent clashes
articles.title: Jailhouse rock, the ‘others’ in the dock
articles.summary: Law enforcement personnel detained 39-year-old Dr. Randall Sequeira and Dalit activist Laxman Naik at a residence in Hilltown on October 16. Authorities subsequently connected the two men to a violent incident from 192 days prior. Although neither individual appeared in the initial police report filed in Rayagada district, investigators later implicated them by utilizing a category of unnamed suspects listed in the documentation.
articles.description: A doctor serving Odisha’s tribal heartland was arrested for allegedly supporting the resistance against bauxite mining. His name, along with those of other activists, did not figure in the FIR, but the police arrested them under a category of unnamed ‘others’. Satyasundar Barik speaks to Adivasi and Dalit communities, which allege the police are using the legal process for intimidation

articles.headline: Isro schedules NVS-03 satellite launch to restore navigation system
articles.title: Why is ISRO’s NVS-03 satellite launch crucial? | Explained
articles.summary: The Indian Space Research Organisation is scheduled to launch the NVS-03 satellite on October 30, 2026, to help restore the functioning of India's indigenous satellite navigation system, NavIC. This mission comes after the constellation was weakened by repeated failures of onboard atomic clocks and the inability to properly place the previous replacement satellite in its intended orbit.
articles.description: The mission could help restore the functioning of India’s regional satellite navigation system NavIC; its development began following the 1999 Kargil War, when the U.S reportedly clamped down on GPS data access

articles.headline: US tariffs threaten the survival of a Canadian paper mill town
articles.title: The fight to save Canadian town threatened by Trump's tariffs
articles.summary: Residents in the Quebec town of Témiscaming are fighting to save their local paper mill after American owner RYAM indefinitely shut down the facility following US President Donald Trump imposing steep tariffs. Most of the three hundred sixty employees are currently out of work while local leaders and workers mobilize to attempt a buyout of the plant.
articles.description: A century-old paper mill in Témiscaming, Quebec is indefinitely closed after the US imposed 50% tariffs on its products, putting hundreds out of work.

articles.headline: Palestinian President Abbas hopes for peace talks with new Israeli government
articles.title: Palestinian President says hopes for peace talks with new Israeli government
articles.summary: Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas expressed optimism that the formation of a new Israeli administration would allow dialogue to resume, according to his remarks in Nicosia during a meeting with Cypriot President Nikos Christodoulides. The statement follows an inconclusive Israeli election outcome where neither Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu nor opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot secured a parliamentary majority.
articles.description: With almost all ballots counted from Israel's pivotal election, neither the bloc of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu nor the opposition bloc led by former military chief Gadi Eisenkot looked able to secure a majority in parliament.

articles.headline: Formula 1 season preview highlights early competition and team performance dynamics
articles.title: How Red Bull tapped Max Verstappen’s sensitive side
articles.summary: Formula One fans witnessed Mercedes establish an early competitive advantage at the start of the 2026 season, according to reports published on October 31, 2026. While Ferrari emerged as the closest early challenger, the racing championship lacked a definitive indication that Italian outfit Scuderia Ferrari could sustain a championship challenge against the dominant front-runners throughout the lengthy motorsport calendar.
articles.description: The four-time champion’s extraordinary feel for the car has proven invaluable in the energy drink giant’s maiden attempt at building its own power unit. Red Bull’s turnaround — although too late to affect the title race — shows why Verstappen evokes such reverence within F1 .

articles.headline: Israel faces political deadlock after general election yields no clear majority
articles.title: Israel election 2026: Benjamin Netanyahu is down but not out
articles.summary: Israel’s October 27, 2026 election resulted in a divided parliament where no single bloc secured the 61 seats needed for a majority in the Knesset. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s right-religious coalition won 53 seats, while the opposition bloc led by Gadi Eisenkot secured 48 seats. Arab parties emerged as a third bloc with 19 seats, creating a political deadlock that could lead to another election within months.
articles.description: Israel’s tight election leaves Benjamin Netanyahu with a fractured majority and a possible caretaker role amid a three-bloc divide and looming coalition uncertainties

articles.headline: U.S. imprisons two Chinese nationals for spying
articles.title: U.S. imprisons two Chinese nationals for spying
articles.summary: Two Chinese men pleaded guilty to acting as foreign agents for China's Ministry of State Security and were sentenced to thirty months in federal prison in California. According to the United States Department of Justice, Liren Lai and Yuance Chen facilitated cash payments for national security information and targeted military personnel before their arrest in June 2025.
articles.description: The U.S. Department of Justice said the men had carried out clandestine intelligence activities in the United States that included facilitating "dead drop" cash payments in exchange for information related to the national security of the United States

articles.headline: Russian drone strike on Dnipro railway station kills fourteen people
articles.title: Russian drone attack on Ukrainian train station kills at least 14, officials say
articles.summary: At least fourteen people died and fourteen others sustained injuries after a Russian drone struck a crowded platform at the main railway station in Dnipro, local officials reported. Ukrzaliznytsia stated that a passenger train bound for Zaporizhzhia was at the platform during the attack, while Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky condemned the strike and called for increased international sanctions against Russia.
articles.description: At least 14 others were wounded in the attack in the central city of Dnipro, including an 11-year-old boy.

articles.headline: Indian chef Ranji Smile introduced curry to America
articles.title: The Indian chef who brought curry to America - then vanished
articles.summary: In 1901, an enigmatic immigrant chef known as Joe Ranji Smile established Omar Khayyam in Manhattan, marking an early attempt at dedicated Indian fine dining in the United States. Backed by financier Roland Conklin after success at Sherry's Restaurant, Smile faced swift closure, legal troubles over smuggled staff, and eventual obscurity by the 1920s.
articles.description: Indian chef Ranji Smile opened America’s first Indian restaurant in 1901 - then became a fake prince.

articles.headline: U.S. midterm elections decide control of Congress
articles.title: What are U.S. midterm elections?
articles.summary: Midterm elections held nationwide halfway through a presidential term determine control of all four hundred thirty-five House seats and roughly one third of the Senate. The November 3 vote serves as a referendum on the administration, impacting legislative power, foreign policy, and immigration rules while remaining crucial for upcoming presidential races.
articles.description: The U.S. midterm elections on November 3 determine control of Congress, with all 435 House seats, about one-third of the 100 Senate seats, and numerous state governorships up for grabs, in a nationwide vote that weakens or strengthens the President’s agenda depending on which party prevails.

articles.headline: Households worldwide prepare emergency supplies amid rising global uncertainties
articles.title: Responsible or panicked? Meet the people around the world already preparing for crisis
articles.summary: Citizens around the world are increasingly assembling personal crisis kits containing long-life food, water, and emergency equipment following government preparedness guidance issued in response to extreme weather, natural disasters, and geopolitical tensions. Individuals in countries such as Sweden, the United States, Japan, and the Netherlands have adopted various stocking strategies, ranging from basement pantries to specialized apps, to ensure household self-sufficiency during disruptions.
articles.description: Filter straws to a disposable toilet - people in the US, Japan, Sweden and Netherlands on what's in their emergency stashes.

articles.headline: Pope Leo votes in U.S. election from Vatican
articles.title: Pope Leo becomes first pontiff to vote in US general election
articles.summary: Pope Leo XIV voted in a United States general election by submitting a mail-in ballot from Chicago, according to Vatican statements confirming his civic participation. Formerly known as Robert Prevost, the pontiff holds dual citizenship and previously participated in multiple primary elections prior to his election to the papacy in May 2025.
articles.description: Vatican confirms the pope submitted a mail-in ballot in his native Chicago ahead of November 3 midterm elections

articles.headline: Fake political polling highlights vulnerabilities in United States elections
articles.title: Fake polls expose vulnerabilities in US elections ahead of midterms
articles.summary: Fraudulent political polling firms in the United States have released fictitious results during the midterm elections, raising concerns about misinformation. Wedgewood Polls and Median Strategies admitted their datasets were fake social experiments. The fabricated surveys reached media outlets like The New York Times, damaging campaigns and eroding voter confidence in election information across several battleground states.
articles.description: Fabricated surveys are adding to tensions in the country's increasingly polarised political environment.

articles.headline: Dog walker threatened with gun during ICE arrest in North Hollywood
articles.title: Dog walker threatened with gun during ICE arrest in North Hollywood
articles.description: Footage shows masked ICE agents pointing a handgun at a bystander walking his dogs as they arrest another man in the US.

articles.headline: Government extends import duty exemption for cotton until December
articles.title: Government extends import duty exemption for cotton
articles.summary: The Finance Ministry extended the import duty exemption for cotton until December 31, 2026, to support the textile industry. Announced in a notification, the measure follows low daily cotton arrivals caused by a poor Southwest monsoon after the marketing season began on October 1. The textile industry previously demanded the removal of the duty to manage expected increases in consumption.
articles.description: In a notification issued on October 30, the Finance Ministry said the exemption, which had been granted in May this year, will continue until October 31

articles.headline: Polish riot police secure constitutional court amid government and judiciary dispute
articles.title: Police deployed during stand-off over control of top Poland court
articles.summary: Riot police deployed at Poland's Constitutional Court in Warsaw to block protesters during a political stand-off involving Prime Minister Donald Tusk and right-wing opponents. Justice Minister Waldemar Żurek sought to strip top court officials of their immunity to face criminal charges. The institution stated the actions constituted a coup d'état, while critics warned the intervention severely damages the rule of law.
articles.description: The escalation came after the government suspended two senior justices and moved to bring criminal charges against them.

articles.headline: Supreme Court mandates bank compensation for digital fraud victims facing negligence
articles.title: SC calls for mandatory compensation to digital fraud victims in case of banks' due diligence
articles.summary: Financial institutions must indemnify digital fraud victims for their total losses when negligence is established, the Supreme Court stated on October 29, 2026. A Bench led by Chief Justice Surya Kant is reviewing Reserve Bank of India regulatory guidelines. While government authorities reported a fifty percent decline in digital arrest cases, total financial losses reached nearly eight hundred crore rupees this year.
articles.description: The Bench stressed that the proposed regulatory framework must provide for suitable compensation to victims where financial institutions are found to have failed in their due diligence obligations

articles.headline: Fighting escalates near Yemen city Taiz amid worsening humanitarian crisis
articles.title: Fighting rages near Yemen’s Taiz as UN urges humanitarian access
articles.summary: Hostilities intensified south of Taiz as government forces clashed with Houthi rebels across multiple fronts, according to reports from Yemen Today TV. The United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs warned that time is running out to deliver aid to eight hundred thousand people trapped inside the city due to damaged roads.
articles.description: Fighting has forced more than 281,000 people from their homes in Yemen since the beginning of August, the UN said.

articles.headline: Supreme Court declines to mandate full public disclosure for AIFs and FPIs
articles.title: Supreme Court refuses to order ‘full public disclosure’ of ultimate beneficiaries of AIFs, FPIs without ‘legal framework’
articles.summary: The Supreme Court of India on Thursday declined to direct the Securities and Exchange Board of India to mandate full public disclosure for Alternative Investment Funds and Foreign Portfolio Investors. A Bench led by Justice B.V. Nagarathna stated that such orders require an existing legal framework, though it asked authorities to consider transparency regulations.
articles.description: Rapid expansion of Alternative Investment Funds and Foreign Portfolio Investors raises serious concerns over transparency, the petition says; the court asks why an MP wants to file a public interest petition under Article 32 when she could raise the issue in the Parliament

articles.headline: South Korean prosecutors seek death penalty for former President Yoon Suk-yeol
articles.title: South Korean prosecutors press for death sentence in Yoon martial law case
articles.summary: South Korean prosecutors are pressing for the death penalty for former President Yoon Suk-yeol over his failed attempt to impose military rule in December 2024. During an appeal hearing in Seoul on Thursday, prosecutors argued that his actions threatened democracy, following his February conviction and life sentence for leading an insurrection.
articles.description: Former president faces renewed death penalty demand as he appeals life sentence for insurrection.

articles.headline: Israeli army maintains military lockdown of Hebron for seventh consecutive day
articles.title: A week of Israel’s lockdown in Hebron: What’s happened, when will it end?
articles.summary: The Israeli army is continuing a military lockdown of Hebron in the occupied West Bank for the seventh consecutive day, resulting in raids, injuries, and detentions. The siege follows the killing of two Israeli soldiers last week, with Israeli forces closing entrances, restricting movement, and forcing thousands of residents from the city.
articles.description: Israel is imposing a tight siege of Hebron amid raids, home demolitions and displacement.

articles.headline: Former civil servant challenges Central Armed Police Forces deployment in Delhi High Court
articles.title: Ex-bureaucrat moves Delhi HC against ‘large-scale’ CAPF deployment during protests
articles.summary: Former civil servant Ashish Joshi filed a public interest litigation in the Delhi High Court challenging the extensive deployment of Central Armed Police Forces during protests. The petition questions the constitutional basis, necessity, and periodic extensions of forces under Articles 14, 19, and 21, while seeking official deployment records and risk assessments from authorities.
articles.description: The PIL seeks directions to the authorities to disclose details of requisitions made by the Delhi Police and the sanction and extension order of the Union Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA)

articles.headline: Germany and France deploy security forces ahead of weekend youth-led protests
articles.title: Germany and France brace for protests on Halloween weekend
articles.summary: Germany and France are deploying thousands of security officers as approximately 150,000 protesters register for demonstrations coinciding with Halloween weekend. Driven by economic grievances and high living costs, youth-led movements have sparked security concerns across multiple cities, prompting store owners to board up windows and authorities to ban face-covering masks.
articles.description: A wave of youth-led protests has swept Europe, with demonstrators denouncing rising prices and a lack of prospects.

articles.headline: US Vice President JD Vance sends peace letter to Iran’s Mohsen Rezaei
articles.title: What we know of Vance’s letter to Rezaei, as Trump warns Gulf to ‘prepare’
articles.summary: United States Vice President JD Vance sent a letter to Iran security chief Mohsen Rezaei on Sunday, proposing direct negotiations to prevent a new round of United States strikes. Qatari mediators delivered the message in Qatar or Turkiye. While Iranian leaders reportedly welcomed the outreach, President Donald Trump warned Gulf allies to prepare for a brief military campaign following the midterm elections.
articles.description: Letter to Iran's security chief reportedly pushes for swift return to peace talks, with Vance leading US delegation.

articles.headline: Supreme Court reserves verdict on ED plea for CBI probe against Mamata Banerjee
articles.title: I-PAC raids case: SC reserves verdict on ED plea for CBI probe into Mamata Banerjee’s conduct
articles.summary: The Supreme Court reserved its judgment on October 29, 2026, regarding a petition from the Directorate of Enforcement seeking a Central Bureau of Investigation probe. The agency accused then West Bengal Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee and state officials of obstructing raids at political consultancy firm I-PAC in Kolkata, alleging vital evidence in a coal smuggling investigation was removed.
articles.description: The ED had blamed the former CM for removing records and devices from the sites of the raids; Ms. Banerjee had at the time countered that the raids were a deliberate attempt to derail the Trinamool Congress ahead of the 2026 Assembly election

articles.headline: Thai human rights lawyer Arnon Nampa sentenced to prison
articles.title: He questioned Thailand's monarchy dressed as Harry Potter. Now he's in jail for 34 years
articles.summary: Arnon Nampa, a forty-two-year-old human rights lawyer, was sentenced by a Bangkok court to two years and eight months in prison for violating Thailand's lèse-majesté law during a 2020 protest. This ruling brings his cumulative prison sentence across multiple cases to over thirty-four years, following a period of extensive legal prosecutions targeting student-led calls for public discussion regarding the monarchy.
articles.description: Thailand has prosecuted 294 people since 2020 under its lèse majesté law, with sentences going up to 50 years.

articles.headline: European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde announces early resignation for February
articles.title: European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde will resign February 7, nine months early
articles.summary: European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde will step down on February 7, 2027, nine months before her eight-year term ends. The departure allows European Union leaders to select a successor before the French presidential election. European Council President Antonio Costa stated that the replacement process would begin immediately alongside filling two other upcoming leadership vacancies.
articles.description: European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde has announced her resignation effective February 7

articles.headline: United States sanctions Rwanda defence ministry over eastern DR Congo conflict
articles.title: US sanctions Rwanda's defence ministry over DR Congo conflict
articles.summary: The United States Treasury imposed sanctions on Rwanda's defence ministry and the Zigama Credit and Savings Society, citing their alleged support for the M23 rebel group in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent urged Kigali to withdraw its troops, while Rwandan government spokesperson Yolande Makolo stated that Rwanda remains ready to implement the Washington Accords.
articles.description: Congo accuses Rwanda of backing M23 rebels and plundering minerals in its conflict hit East

articles.headline: Polish police deployed to Constitutional Tribunal after head judge suspended
articles.title: Polish police deployed to top court after head judge suspended
articles.summary: Polish police entered the Constitutional Tribunal in Warsaw on Friday after demonstrators gathered to protest the suspension of its head, Bogdan Swieczkowski. Minister of Justice Waldemar Zurek requested the removal of immunity for Swieczkowski and his deputy for failing to perform their duties. Prime Minister Donald Tusk supported the suspension on X, while opposition supporters and President Karol Nawrocki criticized the actions.
articles.description: Judge's suspension is part of a long dispute over politicisation of the Constitutional Tribunal under former government.

articles.headline: How has the ceasefire in Russian-occupied Oleshky been unfolding?
articles.title: How has the ceasefire in Russian-occupied Oleshky been unfolding?
articles.description: Ukraine correspondent Dan Johnson explains the temporary ceasefire in the devastated town of Oleshky.

articles.headline: AI tools uncover critical security flaws in open-source digital infrastructure
articles.title: Why AI could threaten much of the world’s digital infrastructure
articles.summary: Independent cybersecurity experts and advanced artificial intelligence models discovered critical security vulnerabilities known as PHP2Shell in the widely used programming language PHP. Foundations maintaining open-source digital infrastructure face resource shortages to address the rising volume of bugs found by AI. Organizations like the Apache Software Foundation and the PHP Foundation rely on volunteer efforts to fix these issues.
articles.description: Volunteer-led PHP, which powers most websites, is increasingly under threat from cyberattacks using AI capabilities.

articles.headline: Pentagon reports war on Iran has cost United States $47 billion
articles.title: Pentagon says Iran war has cost US taxpayers $47bn: What that means
articles.summary: The Pentagon informed United States lawmakers that the military campaign against Iran has cost taxpayers at least $47.1 billion as of October 16, 2026. Disclosed ahead of the November 3 midterm elections, the estimate covers operational expenses and munitions replacements. Democratic senators criticized the administration over the rising costs and economic impacts from the closure of the Strait of Hormuz.
articles.description: With five days to go before the US midterms, analysts say the war could affect how people vote.

articles.headline: Spanish authorities investigate audio recordings following deadly train collision
articles.title: Audio reveals exchanges between Spain train operators and drivers moments before deadly crash
articles.summary: Published audio recordings from Spanish media reveal communications between railway control personnel and train drivers preceding a fatal collision in Spain on Wednesday. The crash involved a state-operated Renfe train and a stationary Iryo service, resulting in at least sixty-nine deaths. According to Spain's transport minister Oscar Puente, investigators are reviewing why the moving train received clearance to proceed despite a technical failure affecting signaling systems.
articles.description: The leaked tapes appear to show one high-speed train was given clearance to move at normal speed, even though another up ahead had stalled.

articles.headline: US judge orders ethics inquiry into government lawyers over golf course case
articles.title: US judge orders ethics inquiry into Trump lawyers over golf course case
articles.summary: United States District Judge Ana Reyes opened a formal inquiry into whether government lawyers misled the court regarding plans to redevelop the East Potomac Golf Links in Washington, DC. The legal dispute follows contradictory statements from officials and President Donald Trump regarding the closure and renovation of the historic public space, prompting environmental and historical concerns from plaintiffs.
articles.description: Judge Ana Reyes calls on US government lawyers to explain contradictory statements about the East Potomac Golf Links.

articles.headline: High-speed train crash in central Spain kills at least 68 people
articles.title: What we know about Spain’s second high-speed rail tragedy this year
articles.summary: At least 68 people were killed and roughly 80 injured when a Renfe state-owned high-speed train collided with a stationary Iryo train near Urda on Wednesday. Transport Minister Oscar Puente blamed an inexplicable control centre order that permitted the moving train to resume normal speed following a signalling failure. Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez declared three days of national mourning.
articles.description: Officials blame a control centre order for Wednesday's crash following a critical train signalling system failure.

articles.headline: Rescue teams search wreckage after deadly train crash in Spain
articles.title: Rescue teams search wreckage for survivors after train crash in Spain
articles.summary: Emergency workers in Toledo province searched through derailed carriages following a collision that killed 68 people. Regional spokeswoman Esther Padilla stated that fifty-three individuals remain hospitalized with fifteen in critical condition. Transport Minister Oscar Puente attributed the accident to a signal failure that preceded the crash involving state and private operators.
articles.description: A canine unit and cranes have been deployed to aid search and rescue efforts following the deadly crash.

articles.headline: Apple Intelligence launches in China with iOS 27.3
articles.title: Apple Intelligence is finally coming to China with iOS 27.3
articles.summary: Apple announced plans to introduce initial artificial intelligence features to the Chinese market through the iOS 27.3 operating system. A beta version is scheduled to launch on November 4, followed by a full release in December. The rollout includes notification summaries, translation tools, and photo editing functions, while omitting the new Siri assistant and incorporating support for Alibaba's Qwen chatbot.
articles.description: Apple will launch Apple Intelligence in China with iOS 27.3, the company announced on its Chinese newsroom website, as reported by MacRumors. The Apple Intelligence features will be available first in an iOS 27.3 beta that's set to launch on November 4th, with a full iOS 27.3 release scheduled for December. This launch doesn't bring […]

articles.headline: Trump demands removal of Alaska Senate candidates over alleged ballot scheme
articles.title: Trump demands Alaska candidates be removed over alleged ballot scheme
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump urged the removal and prosecution of Democratic Senate candidate Mary Peltola and Daniel J Sullivan Jr following a New York Times report on an alleged voter manipulation scheme in Alaska. According to the investigation, campaign aides sought to recruit namesakes to split Republican support. Peltola and the Democratic committee denied the allegations.
articles.description: A New York Times investigation links Democratic operatives to a namesake candidate in Alaska’s Senate race.

articles.headline: US Federal Reserve holds interest rates steady at October meeting
articles.title: U.S. Fed holds rates steady; pressure on emerging markets expected with stronger dollar outlook
articles.summary: The United States Federal Reserve maintained benchmark interest rates between 3.75 percent and 4.0 percent during its October meeting, following a 10 to 2 vote. Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh noted the decision addresses sticky inflation. Economists warn the stronger dollar outlook may cause volatility and fund outflows in emerging markets such as India, where the rupee recently declined.
articles.description: The U.S. Fed is expected to keep the rates elevated, making U.S. Treasuries and the dollar relatively more attractive than emerging market economies for foreign investors

articles.headline: Spain declares three days of mourning following deadly high-speed train collision
articles.title: Spain train crash puts its high-speed rail safety record under scrutiny | Explained
articles.summary: Spain declared a three-day national mourning period after a high-speed train collision on October 28, 2026, killed 68 people and injured numerous others. Occurring in Toledo, this tragedy marks the second major railway accident in the country this year, intensifying national scrutiny regarding the safety and operational standards of Spain's high-speed rail network.
articles.description: Authorities have so far blamed both system issues and human error for the accident which claimed 68 lives; Until this year, Spain had not witnessed such fatal incidents on its dedicated high-speed lines since the network opened in 1992

articles.headline: Rescuers search crash site as Spain mourns fatal train collision
articles.title: Day after Spain train accident, rescuers search crash site for survivors
articles.summary: Emergency personnel continued searching through wreckage in Toledo on October 29, 2026, following a high-speed train collision that claimed 68 lives. Spanish Transport Minister Oscar Puente stated the crash occurred after an authorized Renfe train struck a stationary Iryo train following a signal failure. Meanwhile, train drivers proceeded with a planned strike demanding improved safety investments.
articles.description: Rescue teams use cranes, dog teams in search for survivors of fatal crash; death toll stands at 68

articles.headline: Train collision in Spain leaves at least 30 people dead
articles.title: What we know so far about deadly Spain train crash
articles.summary: At least 30 people died when two trains collided south of Madrid on Wednesday morning, according to local media citing the regional government. State-owned Renfe and private operator Iryo trains crashed between Mora and Orgaz at around 09:00 local time, carrying over 500 passengers combined. Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez and the royal family expressed shock while emergency services deployed helicopters and fire crews to the scene.
articles.description: More than 500 passengers were on board the trains when the crash occurred in the province of Toledo, south of Madrid.

articles.headline: Phoenix economic growth drives semiconductor expansion amid local water concerns
articles.title: AI has come for Arizona’s water
articles.summary: The Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company has expanded its microchip manufacturing operations in Phoenix, Arizona, with projected expenditures reaching 265 billion US dollars. Spearheaded by economic development official Christine Mackay, the project consumes millions of gallons of water daily from municipal supplies. While local leaders welcomed the facility, new data center proposals face intense grassroots opposition over dwindling regional water resources.
articles.description: A hulking gray giant rises from the desert. Inside, engineers create the force behind our phones and computers and appliances, our streaming services and search engines and chatbots and vibe-coded apps and websites. The complex is simultaneously massive and squat, dwarfed by the mountains that surround it, and it is endless. I drive past one […]

articles.headline: Why Michigan could decide the future of Trump’s presidency
articles.title: Why Michigan could decide the future of Trump’s presidency
articles.description: Michigan has swung between Republicans and Democrats in the past three presidential elections.

articles.headline: Glacial lake outburst flood damages roads and bridges in Bhutan
articles.title: Glacial Lake Outburst Flood damages roads, washes away bridge in Bhutan
articles.summary: A glacial lake outburst flood from Shintapu Tsho in northwestern Bhutan triggered severe flooding along the Mochhu on October 29, 2026. Disaster management officials reported no casualties, but infrastructure suffered extensive damage, including washed-out bridges and blocked roads in the Gasa and Punakha districts. Authorities evacuated nearby residents and placed neighboring regions on high alert due to fears of additional sudden outbursts from a newly formed artificial lake.
articles.description: Vulnerable revenue circles in Dhubri and Kokrajhar districts of Assam have been put on high alert

articles.headline: Israeli settler take-over
articles.title: Israeli settler take-over
articles.description: How Israeli settlers use outposts and violence to seize Palestinian land in the occupied West Bank.

articles.headline: Police secure Poland's Constitutional Tribunal amid protests over suspension
articles.title: Police secure Poland's Constitutional Tribunal as protests erupt over court chief's suspension
articles.summary: Polish police secured the Constitutional Tribunal and detained three individuals after protesters breached the fence and threw objects during demonstrations against the suspension of court president Bogdan Swieczkowski. Prime Minister Donald Tusk defended the action as part of efforts to restore judicial independence. Meanwhile, Polish President Karol Nawrocki cut short a flight to Senegal to return to the country following the unrest.
