articles.description: Police said they detained three people after some protesters breached the tribunal's fence and others threw objects at officers

articles.headline: Israel faces political deadlock as election results leave both leading blocs without majorities
articles.title: How could Israel break election deadlock? Here are four scenarios
articles.summary: Following Tuesday's election in Israel, neither Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's coalition nor challenger Gadi Eisenkot's bloc secured a parliamentary majority with 85% of votes counted. Potential resolutions include a national unity government, an opposition coalition reliant on Arab parties, right-wing defections to Netanyahu, or holding new elections, a recurring outcome between 2019 and 2022.
articles.description: With more than 90% of votes counted, all signs point to an impasse. The most likely outcome may be new elections.

articles.headline: Swiss supreme court upholds 20-year sentence for former Liberian rebel commander
articles.title: Swiss supreme court upholds Liberian ex-rebel commander’s 20-year sentence
articles.summary: The Federal Supreme Court of Switzerland upheld a 20-year prison sentence for former Liberian rebel commander Alieu Kosiah for war crimes committed between 1993 and 1995. However, the court overturned his conviction for crimes against humanity based on the principle of non-retroactivity because the specific charge was not added to Swiss law until 2011. Kosiah was originally arrested in 2014 after settling in Switzerland in the late 1990s.
articles.description: Alieu Kosiah killed civilians and unarmed soldiers, and ordered lootings and other crimes against humanity.

articles.headline: Obama and Trump clash over foreign policy during rival campaign rallies
articles.title: Obama and Trump spar at rallies in Georgia and Ohio: Key takeaways
articles.summary: Former United States President Barack Obama and President Donald Trump held competing campaign events in Georgia and Ohio on Wednesday, exchanging sharp criticism regarding the ongoing war in Iran and controversial trade tariffs. According to Barack Obama, United States military actions have left the nation vulnerable and driven up domestic fuel prices. Meanwhile, Donald Trump defended his foreign policy decisions and criticized the 2015 nuclear agreement established during the previous administration.
articles.description: Obama and Trump traded barbs over the Iran war, tariffs and the White House ballroom ahead of the US midterm elections.

articles.headline: OpenAI chief executive officer Sam Altman defends data center RAM allocation
articles.title: Sam Altman says it’s better for RAM to be in a data center than on your desk
articles.summary: OpenAI Chief Executive Officer Sam Altman argued in a podcast interview that concentrating limited global DRAM supplies in data centers is better than placing them in personal computers. He stated that local inference leads to poor utilization rates. Memory companies such as Samsung and SK Hynix have secured long term deals with cloud operators, driving up consumer tech hardware prices.
articles.description: Asked about supply chain shortages, like the ongoing RAM shortage, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said in an interview that it's "terrible" to have RAM in personal PCs instead of data centers. During his appearance on the Cheeky Pint podcast, where he also commented on AI's impact on math, Altman said: "A lot of people want […]

articles.headline: National Conference legislators issue ultimatum to party leadership in Srinagar
articles.title: 17 NC MLAs issue 15-day ultimatum to address ‘coterie culture’, other issues in party
articles.summary: Seventeen legislators from the ruling National Conference held a four-hour meeting at a residence in Srinagar on October 30, 2026. They issued a 15-day ultimatum to party president Farooq Abdullah and vice-president Omar Abdullah to address unilateral decisions and coterie culture. Meanwhile, Member of Parliament Aga Syed Ruhullah announced plans to resign from his parliamentary seat on November 3, 2026.
articles.description: Four-hour meeting of the 17 NC legislators in Srinagar comes three days after party vice-president and J&K CM Omar Abdullah expanded the Cabinet, leaving several leaders disgruntled at not being given a berth

articles.headline: Odisha prepares to airlift flood-stranded residents as cyclone brings heavy rain
articles.title: Cyclone Arnab: Odisha prepares to airlift people stranded by floodwater
articles.summary: Roads were cut off and hundreds of villages were inundated by floodwaters in Odisha’s Ganjam and Gajapati districts as the State government prepared to airlift stranded people on Thursday, October 29, 2026. Union Home Minister Amit Shah spoke to Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi regarding the situation after Cyclonic Storm Arnab weakened. State Chief Secretary Anu Garg stated that approximately 2,000 people were marooned in Ganjam district.
articles.description: Two rain gauge stations at Patrapur and Sorada in Odisha’s Ganjam district received rainfall above 50 cm in 24 hours

articles.headline: Seven killed in Delhi building collapse as authorities face safety scrutiny
articles.title: When home in Delhi became a death trap: Satya Niketan building collapse
articles.summary: Seven people died and twelve were rescued following the collapse of the Hostel Daze building in south Delhi’s Satya Niketan on September 6, 2026. Students, shopkeepers, and residents initiated rescue efforts before emergency personnel arrived through narrow lanes. According to the Municipal Corporation of Delhi, the five-storey building lacked a sanctioned plan, fire no-objection certificate, and occupancy certificate, exposing widespread regulatory and safety enforcement failures.
articles.description: The collapse of a five-storey building in Delhi’s Satya Niketan on September 6 killed seven people. The incident has exposed the precarious housing conditions for students in the capital, where the demand for affordable accommodation far outstrips the availability of institutional hostels. Lavpreet Kaur reports on the rescue and the questions being raised over the safety of paying guest accommodation

articles.headline: Election Commission appeals regarding West Bengal electoral rolls face scrutiny
articles.title: Election Commission’s appeals against 16.10 lakh cleared voters raise legal questions
articles.summary: The Election Commission of India filed appeals challenging the inclusion of over 16 lakh voters in West Bengal whose names were previously cleared by judicial officers during the state electoral roll revision. Opposition parties and petitioners questioned whether the officials who filed these bulk appeals possessed proper legal authority under the Representation of the People Act.
articles.description: The officials who filed appeals against the inclusion of the 16.10 lakh voters may not have had the authority to do so under the Representation of the People Act; according to the Act, the CEO/DEO/ERO/AERO are the authorities with respect to electoral rolls

articles.headline: Ethiopia acquires Russian fighter jets amid escalating regional tensions
articles.title: Ethiopia acquires Russian fighter jets and air defence systems amid war in Tigray
articles.summary: Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed announced the delivery of twelve Su-35 fighter jets from Russia during the Russia-Africa summit in Moscow. According to the Ethiopian leader, the advanced military hardware will significantly enhance national defense capabilities amid ongoing conflict in the northern Tigray region. Ethiopia also plans to procure four S-400 air defense systems to protect critical infrastructure and establish strategic air superiority in the region.
articles.description: The acquisition of the warplanes comes amid ongoing fighting in northern Tigray region that started last month.

articles.headline: Supreme Court asks ministry to prevent online misuse of court proceedings
articles.title: Supreme Court asks Centre to take measures against online misuse of court feeds
articles.summary: The Supreme Court on October 30, 2026, directed the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology to formulate measures against the commercial exploitation of live-streamed judicial proceedings. Solicitor General Tushar Mehta stated that suggestions from High Courts were forwarded to the ministry. Advocate Prashant Bhushan suggested adding verifiable digital watermarks to official clips to prevent manipulation.
articles.description: Solicitor General Tushar Mehta submits that suggestions from various High Courts and other stakeholders have been received and forwarded to the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology

articles.headline: At least 68 killed in high-speed train collision in central Spain
articles.title: ‘I held this woman in my arms. She died’: Spain mourns train crash victims
articles.summary: At least 68 people were killed and 77 others injured after a high-speed train traveling from Madrid to Seville collided with a stationary locomotive in a rural area between Urda and Los Yebenes on Wednesday. Spain’s national train operator Renfe launched an investigation into the disaster. Transport Minister Oscar Puente stated that the train was authorized to continue despite an active red signal caused by a computer communications failure.
articles.description: Second tragedy on line in about nine months raises questions about levels of investment in railway maintenance.

articles.headline: Port Sudan residents struggle with severe water shortages and high costs
articles.title: Port Sudan families can barely afford water as shortages persist
articles.summary: Residents in Port Sudan face daily financial burdens to secure safe drinking water following the August 2024 collapse of the Arbaat Dam and ongoing conflict. Families spend significant portions of their monthly incomes purchasing water from street vendors. Medical officials warn that these ongoing supply shortages heighten risks of waterborne diseases, threatening vulnerable populations across the coastal city.
articles.description: Despite efforts to restore damaged infrastructure, residents face soaring water costs as war, displacement strain supply

articles.headline: United States bans imports from three Chinese genomics companies over forced labour
articles.title: U.S. bans imports from Chinese genomics companies over forced labour concerns
articles.summary: The United States Department of Homeland Security banned imports from BGI Genomics, MGI Tech, and Shenzhen BGI Technology on Wednesday, October 28, 2026, alleging they collected genetic material used to track persecuted ethnic minorities in Xinjiang. The companies were added to the Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act Entity List. Beijing strongly condemned the ban, while the firms denied all allegations involving forced labour.
articles.description: According to the U.S. Homeland Security, the companies “helped collect genetic material used to track persecuted ethnic minorities, including people subjected to forced labour...”

articles.headline: Haryana Bharatiya Janata Party MLA criticises merit-based government job recruitment policy
articles.title: Haryana BJP MLA questions party’s merit-based jobs policy, warns of anti-incumbency
articles.summary: Ram Kumar Gautam, a Bharatiya Janata Party legislator from Safidon, criticised former Chief Minister Manohar Lal’s merit-based government job policy. He argued that the system alienates loyal party workers whose children remain unemployed. While opposition leaders pointed to alleged corruption and reliance on contractual hiring, party representatives defended the policy as a fair approach without political recommendations or bribes.
articles.description: The BJP has consistently projected its policy of providing jobs without political recommendations or bribes as one of its biggest achievements in Haryana

articles.headline: Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu announces relief package after Cyclone Arnab
articles.title: Cyclone Arnab claims five lives in Andhra Pradesh; Naidu announces relief package
articles.summary: Cyclone Arnab resulted in five fatalities across Andhra Pradesh, leading Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu to unveil a comprehensive compensation package on October 28, 2026. Addressing reporters in Visakhapatnam, Naidu detailed financial aid for damaged homes, crops, and businesses following winds reaching 150 kmph. The government aims to assist affected residents while recovery efforts continue.
articles.description: ₹5 lakh ex gratia for each victim; aid announced for farmers, fishermen, households and businesses

articles.headline: Poland pivots toward India to strengthen economic and defense cooperation
articles.title: Poland pivots towards India as ‘strategic partnership’ with China develops cracks
articles.summary: Poland is strengthening its strategic partnership with India through improved economic and defense collaboration following Prime Minister Donald Tusk’s recent visit. This diplomatic shift comes as Warsaw distances itself from China due to trade imbalances and concerns regarding the Russia-Ukraine war. A recent Polish government study warned that European industries face significant economic pressure and job losses from Chinese state-led industrial strategies.
articles.description: Poland and India seek to raise bilateral trade from $6 bn to $12 bn; PM Modi visited Poland in 2024, during which ties were elevated to ‘strategic partnership’; Warsaw is also trying to diversify partnerships as trade imbalance and Beijing’s support for Russia deepen disillusionment with China

articles.headline: Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary demands priority in Ganga Water Treaty
articles.title: Bihar’s interests must be considered in the Ganga Water Treaty: Samrat Choudhary
articles.summary: Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary stated that Bihar’s interests must be prioritized in matters concerning the Ganga Water and the Farakka Treaty. Speaking at a seminar in Patna on October 30, 2026, he highlighted the resolution of a 25-year-old dispute over Sone River water sharing. He also announced plans for a new state-level silt management policy to support infrastructure development and agriculture.
articles.description: The CM mentioned that Bihar’s rivers hold immense potential for the State, and through the proper management of their water and silt, new opportunities can be created in agriculture, industry, infrastructure, and employment

articles.headline: Omron Healthcare launches its first manufacturing plant in Tamil Nadu
articles.title: Japan’s Omron Healthcare opens first India manufacturing facility near Chennai
articles.summary: Omron Healthcare inaugurated its inaugural Indian production facility in Gummidipoondi near Chennai, built three years after signing a memorandum of understanding with the Tamil Nadu government. The plant currently produces three models of blood pressure monitors with a capacity of 300,000 units annually, which the company aims to scale tenfold over two years while also targeting European exports by next year.

articles.headline: Karnataka milk price increase draws criticism for threatening household budgets and nutrition
articles.title: Karnataka’s milk price hike draws flak for impact on budget and nutrition
articles.summary: Experts and public figures have criticised the Karnataka government's decision to raise milk prices by eight rupees per litre, effective November 1. Critics argue the fourfold increase since 2023 strains household budgets, wages, and working-class nutrition, potentially worsening deficiencies among women and children amidst broader rises in essential commodity and fuel costs.
articles.description: Experts warn of increased household expenses and reduced access to essential nutrition, particularly for low-income families

articles.headline: California midterm elections shape congressional balance and policy ballot measures
articles.title: What to know about California’s midterm elections
articles.summary: Voters in California head to the polls for midterm elections featuring competitive congressional races and high-stakes ballot initiatives. New district maps drawn under Proposition 50 aim to secure additional Democratic seats in the United States House of Representatives, while gubernatorial candidates Xavier Becerra and Steve Hilton vie to succeed Governor Gavin Newsom amid debates over economy and taxes.
articles.description: Redistricting in California, the most populous US state, could flip control of US House from Republican to Democrat.

articles.headline: Benjamin Netanyahu accuses Palestinian Israeli parties of election fraud
articles.title: Why is Netanyahu accusing Palestinian Israeli parties of fraud?
articles.summary: Following an inconclusive general election in Israel, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu alleged that Palestinian Israeli parties engaged in vote-theft and accepted foreign funding from Qatar. These parties denied all wrongdoing, while the Electoral Commission reported no evidence of fraud and Qatari officials rejected any involvement in the electoral process.
articles.description: Prime Minister claims the parties accepted foreign funding.

articles.headline: United Nations reports surge in Afghan opium poppy cultivation despite Taliban ban
articles.title: Afghanistan opium poppy cultivation surges despite Taliban government ban: UN
articles.summary: Opium poppy cultivation in Afghanistan quadrupled to 43,000 hectares in 2026 despite an ongoing Taliban government ban, according to a United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime report released on October 29, 2026. Executive Director Monica Juma stated that impoverished farmers lack viable alternatives to the lucrative trade. The United Nations emphasized the urgent need for international support and sustainable livelihoods.
articles.description: Afghanistan’s 2022 crackdown drove cultivated areas down from more than 2,00,000 hectares to 10,000 hectares in 2025

articles.headline: Karnataka chief minister requests sugar minimum selling price revision from prime minister
articles.title: CM writes to PM seeking revision of sugar MSP, order on ethanol production
articles.summary: Karnataka Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar wrote to Prime Minister Narendra Modi requesting a revision of the minimum selling price of sugar, noting it has remained unchanged since 2019 despite rising sugarcane fair and remunerative prices. The chief minister also urged changes to ethanol production directives to help sugar mills maintain timely payments to farmers during the ongoing crushing season.
articles.description: The farmers are awaiting an assurance from the Centre even as the cane crushing season has been delayed amidst prospects of cane yield getting reduced this year due to drought: CM

articles.headline: India offers counter-terror expertise to ASEAN and dialogue partners
articles.title: India ready to share 'battle-tested' anti-terror expertise with ASEAN, its dialogue partners: Rajnath Singh
articles.summary: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh announced on October 29, 2026, at an ADMM-Plus conclave in Cebu, Philippines, that India is prepared to share battle-tested counter-terrorism expertise through joint exercises and intelligence sharing. He emphasized maritime security and criticized state-sponsored terrorism, referencing Operation Sindoor, as regional states face growing tensions in the South China Sea.
articles.description: The Defence Minister flagged concerns over disruptions in certain maritime trade routes and asserted that India will continue to act as a "trusted net security provider" in the Indian Ocean region and the wider Indo-Pacific

articles.headline: North Korea launches short-range ballistic missiles following border dispute tensions with Seoul
articles.title: North Korea fires missiles as row over landmine blast intensifies
articles.summary: North Korea fired approximately ten short-range ballistic missiles off its east coast into the Sea of Japan on Thursday, as reported by South Korea’s Joint Chiefs of Staff. The launch occurred amid escalating hostility surrounding a landmine explosion in the Demilitarized Zone on September 21. Pyongyang rejected joint investigation findings and dismissed recent dialogue overtures proposed by South Korea.
articles.description: Seoul accuses Pyongyang of causing a landmine explosion that injured three of its soldiers, an accusation North denies.

articles.headline: Akhilesh Yadav criticizes Uttar Pradesh chief minister over legislative council election results
articles.title: U.P. CM prioritised his home turf over 2 Varanasi seats in MLC polls: Akhilesh
articles.summary: Samajwadi Party president Akhilesh Yadav accused Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath of prioritizing his home turf in Gorakhpur at the expense of Varanasi seats during Legislative Council elections. While the Bharatiya Janata Party secured six of the eleven contested seats, the opposition leader claimed the ruling administration's overall electoral performance reflected a failure regarding education and employment.
articles.description: As per the final tally, declared on Thursday afternoon, of the 11 U.P. Legislative Council seats that went to the polls on October 23, the BJP won six while the SP raised its tally from the previous MLC polls by two

articles.headline: U.S. judge rejects Department of Justice effort in California vote
articles.title: U.S. judge rejects Trump administration’s interference in California midterm vote
articles.summary: U.S. District Judge David O. Carter rejected Department of Justice efforts on October 28, 2026, to set aside ballots of over 20,000 California voters, condemning the legal challenge as pre-election interference. Democratic leaders had sued over the push, which sought to question voter eligibility ahead of the November 3 midterm elections across the United States.
articles.description: Those registered on California’s voter roles “must not be deprived of a core right merely because of unfounded allegations stemming from a procedure rife with uncertainty and errors,” U.S. District Judge David O. Carter said

articles.headline: Andhra Pradesh plans ₹3,000 crore investment for Godavari drainage modernisation
articles.title: Andhra Pradesh to spend ₹3,000 crore on irrigation drain modernisation in Godavari region
articles.summary: Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu announced a ₹3,000 crore project to modernise irrigation drains in the Godavari region to prevent agricultural and horticultural flooding. The funding aims to provide a permanent solution to backwater inundation caused by choked confluences, following significant crop damage and infrastructure destruction during Cyclone Arnab.
articles.description: Modernisation of irrigation drains will offer a permanent solution to crop inundation problems, says Chief Minister, adding that 4.68 TMC of rainwater has been diverted to reservoirs during Cyclone Arnab

articles.headline: Texas grand jury indicts ICE officer for hitting Mexican worker
articles.title: Texas grand jury indicts ICE officer accused of running over man in Houston
articles.summary: A Texas grand jury indicted United States Immigration and Customs Enforcement officer Mario Alberto Morales for aggravated assault with a deadly weapon following an October 10 incident in Houston. Harris County District Attorney Sean Teare stated that Morales deliberately struck 48-year-old Miguel Parra-Hernandez with a vehicle during an operation, causing severe leg fractures that required surgery.
articles.description: The officer faces charges after allegedly striking a fleeing construction worker with an SUV during an immigration raid.

articles.headline: United States Democrats lead national polls as key midterm elections approach
articles.title: US midterms: Five days to go – What the polls say as Trump, Harris campaign
articles.summary: Democrats hold an 8.2 percentage point lead nationally ahead of the United States midterm elections, though several Senate races remain competitive. Political figures including President Donald Trump and former President Barack Obama campaigned across key states on Wednesday to influence voters. Both parties are heavily targeting control of Congress with just five days remaining until the ballot.
articles.description: With five days until the US midterms, here's what polls show, the latest campaign news and what's next.

articles.headline: Kerala forest department and Plantation Corporation to survey disputed Athirappilly land
articles.title: Leased forest land at Athirappilly in Keralam to be surveyed amid disputes over blocking elephant corridor
articles.summary: Authorities will jointly inspect a two-hectare plot in Athirappilly held by the Plantation Corporation Kerala following lease expiration and environmental concerns. Officials aim to evaluate wildlife movement corridors, address human-wildlife conflicts, and investigate alleged lease violations involving private farming activities. The corporation defends its operations while environmentalists criticise the blockade of animal pathways.
articles.description: Forest department strongly opposes Plantation Corporation, Kerala’s proposal to renew the lease agreement and access more land, citing violation of lease conditions, including engaging private agencies for pineapple farming on the holding

articles.headline: Pakistan army expresses cautious optimism regarding US-Iran mediation efforts
articles.title: Pakistan army ‘cautiously optimistic’ about US-Iran mediation efforts
articles.summary: Pakistan’s military announced cautious optimism about ongoing mediation efforts between Iran and the United States to revive a collapsed ceasefire in the eight-month-old war. Speaking in Rawalpindi, military spokesman Lieutenant General Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry highlighted recent diplomatic visits to Tehran by army chief Field Marshal Asim Munir alongside Saudi and Turkish officials.
articles.description: Pakistan's military spokesman warns of 'powerful spoilers and detractors' who still believe the conflict serves them.

articles.headline: Tasmac raises liquor prices in Tamil Nadu with bottle return refund
articles.title: Tasmac revises liquor prices from November 1, links refund to bottle returns
articles.summary: The Tamil Nadu State Marketing Corporation will increase the maximum retail price of all liquor variants by ten rupees starting November 1, 2026, by adding an environment cess. Customers can receive a full reimbursement of the ten rupees by returning empty bottles. The policy applies to all domestic and imported alcoholic beverages, and the corporation warned staff against collecting any unauthorized additional fees.
articles.description: Environment cess to be added to the existing maximum retail price of Indian Made Foreign Liquor, beer, wine, liquor from other States and imported liquor; those who return the bottles will get a refund of ₹10

articles.headline: Kerala orders anti-corruption probe into land acquisition financed by KIIFB
articles.title: Orders issued on Vigilance probe into KIIFB-financed land acquisition in Kannur
articles.summary: The Kerala government ordered the Vigilance and Anti Corruption Bureau to investigate alleged procedural lapses regarding the acquisition of 4,896 acres in Kannur district. According to an official order issued by Additional Chief Secretary Minhaj Alam, the decision follows a cabinet recommendation based on an expert committee report examining whether the Rs 12,240 crore project violated land acquisition laws.
articles.description: Move follows Cabinet nod for VACB probe based on panel report. Procedural lapses alleged in land acquisitions for Kannur industrial zones, where 4,896 acres were bought for ₹12,240 crore amid questions of due diligence, compliance with LARR Act.

articles.headline: Israeli forces demolish homes of Palestinians following Hebron military offensive
articles.title: Israel demolishes homes of Palestinians blamed for attack on soldiers
articles.summary: Israeli troops used explosives to destroy the homes of two brothers accused of killing two soldiers during an attack. The demolitions occurred during a military offensive in Hebron that has displaced thousands of residents, led to numerous arrests, and prompted widespread condemnation from local officials and Palestinian groups regarding collective punishment.
articles.description: Troops hold at least 12 Palestinians near demolished homes as nearly 5,000 remain displaced from Hebron neighbourhoods

articles.headline: Ten people die in collision involving two high-speed trains in Toledo province
articles.title: At least 68 dead after two trains collide in Spain’s Toledo Province
articles.summary: At least ten people died following a collision between two trains in central Spain on October 28, 2026. According to rail operator ADIF, the crash occurred in Toledo province, disrupting services between Madrid, Ciudad Real, and Andalusia. State broadcaster TVE reported that one high-speed train struck the rear of another traveling in the same direction, causing carriages to derail.
articles.description: The second such accident to strike Spain this year will raise fresh questions about the country’s rail safety, with the Transport Minister speaking of an “error” and “inexplicable circumstances” that led to the collision.

articles.headline: Oman rescues crew from burning oil tanker in Strait of Hormuz
articles.title: Oman rescues 25 from burning oil tanker in Strait of Hormuz
articles.summary: Omani maritime authorities successfully evacuated 25 crew members from a Panamanian-flagged crude oil tanker after the vessel caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz. The incident occurred while the Iranian Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps reported halting multiple vessels attempting to use unauthorised routes, even as the United States military denied claims regarding naval mines in the area.
articles.description: Incident comes as Iran says three oil tankers were halted while attempting to use 'unauthorised routes' to cross Hormuz.

articles.headline: Press Club of India condemns inclusion of journalist in search warrants
articles.title: PCI shocked at inclusion of senior journalist in search warrant requests
articles.summary: The Press Club of India expressed shock and condemnation after Arunachal Pradesh Police included senior journalist Tongam Rina in search warrant requests related to recent violence in Pasighat. The press organization stated that targeting journalists covering protests against the Siang dam project constitutes an unacceptable attack on media freedom.
articles.description: “PCI condemns all attempts by State authorities to intimidate and harass journalists who are reporting on the ongoing protests against the Siang dam project,” read the statement

articles.headline: Flavio Bolsonaro claims leadership in Brazil after fleeing to U.S.
articles.title: Flavio Bolsonaro claims he is Brazil’s true leader after fleeing to U.S.
articles.summary: Defeated right-wing candidate Flavio Bolsonaro arrived in Florida on October 28, 2026, claiming he is Brazil's rightful leader following the election victory of leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva. The senator faces corruption investigations in Brazil and departed despite surrendered passports, while U.S. and Argentine authorities reviewed his valid travel documents.
articles.description: “I am the elected president, and the criminals who stole Brazil’s election are part of a criminal organization that has established a tyranny,” Flavio Bolsonaro said; U.S. President Donald Trump said he “won’t get involved” in Mr. Bolsonaro’s claim

articles.headline: European wealth gap shows older households vastly richer than youth
articles.title: Europe’s wealth gap: Older households eight times richer than young ones
articles.summary: Households in eurozone countries headed by individuals aged 55 to 64 possess a median net wealth of approximately 208,000 euros, which is over eight times the 25,000 euros held by those under 35, according to a 2023 European Central Bank survey. Meanwhile, student protests over housing costs and inflation have expanded across eleven European nations.
articles.description: As protests over living costs and programme cuts spread across Europe, under-35s hold 2.8%t of household wealth.

articles.headline: Mirwaiz Umar Farooq calls for political engagement to resolve Kashmir issue
articles.title: Kashmir issue cannot be addressed through security approach alone, requires political engagement: Mirwaiz
articles.summary: Kashmir chief cleric Mirwaiz Umar Farooq stated during a sermon at Jama Masjid that the region requires political engagement and reconciliation rather than relying solely on security measures. Citing an International Crisis Group report and government data on anti-terror law detentions, he urged authorities to release political prisoners, restore civil liberties, and pursue dialogue.
articles.description: Kashmir chief cleric Mirwaiz Umar Farooq said peace cannot simply be measured by the absence of protests

articles.headline: U.S. labour leader and civil rights icon Dolores Huerta dies at 96
articles.title: Pioneering U.S. labour leader Dolores Huerta dies at 96
articles.summary: Dolores Huerta, a prominent United States labour leader and civil rights icon who co-founded the United Farm Workers union, passed away on October 28, 2026, at the age of 96, according to her family. Throughout her career, she organised strikes to improve conditions for migrant workers and received accolades such as the presidential medal of freedom from Barack Obama.
articles.description: Dolores Huerta took the reins of the U.S. farmworker movement in the 1960s with Chavez

articles.headline: Karnataka government suspends hospital medicine price disclosure circular until November
articles.title: Will not enforce circular on hospital medicine price disclosure for now: Karnataka government to HC
articles.summary: The Karnataka government informed the High Court on October 30, 2026, that it will temporarily halt enforcing a circular requiring hospital pharmacies to display purchase and retail prices of medicines and medical devices. The Food Safety and Drug Administration agreed to pause the mandate until the next hearing on November 12 while officials re-examine the policy following a petition by private healthcare associations.
articles.description: The circular mandates that all hospital pharmacies disclose the landing base/purchase price and maximum retail price of medicines, medical devices and consumables on bills.

articles.headline: North Korea fires ballistic missile barrage toward eastern sea
articles.title: North Korea fires missile barrage toward sea as tensions with South rise
articles.summary: North Korea launched approximately ten short-range ballistic missiles from Wonsan toward the sea on October 29, 2026, according to South Korea's military. The weapons tests followed leader Kim Jong Un's visit to China and rising cross-border animosity after land mine explosions in September, prompting Seoul to monitor the situation alongside the United States and Japan.
articles.description: Seoul accused North Korea of planting mines south of the military demarcation line that caused the September 21 blasts, but Pyongyang has denied responsibility for the explosions and warned of retaliation if provoked

articles.headline: Kim Jong Un calls for North Korea’s drone technology superiority
articles.title: Kim Jong Un calls for North Korea’s drone technology superiority
articles.description: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un calls for “absolute superiority” in drone capabilities.

articles.headline: European officials warn of escalating Russian shadow war and sabotage threats
articles.title: Russia’s alleged sabotage campaign in Europe raises fears of escalation
articles.summary: European security figures and Ukrainian experts report an escalation in Russian hybrid warfare tactics throughout the continent. Incidents include airspace violations, downed drones, maritime cargo ship sinkings in October near Bulgaria, and border provocations in Latvia. Officials caution that inadequate deterrence encourages Moscow to continue threatening regional stability and critical infrastructure.
articles.description: From drone incursions to an alleged campaign of assassinations, Russia is feared to be pressing a shadow war.

articles.headline: Jammu and Kashmir High Court seeks update on deported citizen's retrieval
articles.title: J&K High Court seeks status on retrieval of Pakistan-born son of Indian deported after Pahalgam attack
articles.summary: The Jammu and Kashmir High Court directed Senior Additional Advocate General Monika Kohli on October 30, 2026, to provide status updates regarding the retrieval of Aasim Sajjad. The 18-year-old son of an Indian citizen was previously deported to Pakistan following the Pahalgam attack. The court had earlier ordered his return to join his father, Sajjad Ahmed, citing human rights and citizenship considerations.
articles.description: Scores of Pakistan-born citizens, married to citizens of J&K, were deported from the Union Territory after the Pahalgam attack, which left 26 civilians dead

articles.headline: Pentagon military planner fired as United States considers potential Iran strikes
articles.title: Hegseth fires Pentagon's top military planner even as Trump considers new Iran strikes
articles.summary: Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth removed Army Lieutenant General Brett Sylvia as head of strategy, plans and policy on the Joint Chiefs of Staff. A defence official confirmed the dismissal on Wednesday as President Donald Trump considers new military operations against Iran following an eight-month-long war. Sylvia is the second general to be ousted from the J5 post during Hegseth's tenure.
articles.description: The defence official, who spoke on condition of anonymity to discuss sensitive personnel matters, said there is no immediate replacement for Mr. Sylvia and no reason has been given for the firing

articles.headline: Colombia advances budget cuts and legislative bill threatening special peace court
articles.title: How cuts under Colombia’s de la Espriella threaten a key human rights court
articles.summary: The administration of Colombian President Abelardo de la Espriella announced significant budget reductions totaling 181 billion Colombian pesos for the Special Jurisdiction for Peace, a transitional justice court established in 2016. Concurrently, a Senate committee advanced a bill to dissolve the court entirely by March 2028. Victims and advocates warn the measures will jeopardize ongoing investigations into conflict-related disappearances.
articles.description: Colombia's president plans to slash spending on a transitional justice court. But war crimes victims fear the cost.

articles.headline: Academics uncover major digital influence operation promoting anti-Qatar and racist narratives
articles.title: Report reveals campaign promoting racist, Islamophobic, anti-Qatar views
articles.summary: Two academics published an investigation detailing a multi-year digital disinformation campaign costing over $11 million across 30 countries. The operation generated at least 533 million exposures on platforms like YouTube and TikTok between October 2023 and October 2026, promoting anti-Muslim, anti-migrant, and anti-Qatar views. Evidence suggests the influence campaign originated in Israel to shape political environments ahead of international elections.
articles.description: Investigation finds that years-long operation sought to portray Qatar as driving force behind mass migration to Europe.

articles.headline: Air Marshal Inderpal Singh Walia appointed as next IAF Vice Chief
articles.title: Air Marshal Inderpal Singh Walia named next IAF Vice Chief
articles.summary: The Defence Ministry announced on October 30, 2026, that Air Marshal Inderpal Singh Walia will assume the role of Vice Chief of the Air Staff. He will succeed Air Marshal Ashutosh Dixit, who is becoming the 29th Chief of the Air Staff. Currently heading the Eastern Air Command, Walia brings nearly four decades of fighter pilot experience to the position.
articles.description: Air Marshal Walia headed the Directorate of Air Staff Inspection (DASI) of the IAF, served as the defence attache at Indian embassies in Japan and South Korea, and was the Senior Air Staff Officer of Eastern Air Command.

articles.headline: India defeats Japan to secure semifinal spot in Asian Champions Trophy
articles.title: ACT: India extends winning run, seals spot in the semifinals
articles.summary: India defeated Japan 4-1 on October 30, 2026, to maintain its winning streak and advance to the semifinals of the Asian Champions Trophy hockey tournament. Despite a resilient defensive performance from Japan that kept the score level through the first three quarters, goals from Abhishek and Harmanpreet Singh in the final period secured the victory for the defending champions.
articles.description: Malaysia also advances to the last-four stage with a third win on the row

articles.headline: Russia intercepts majority of over six hundred drones launched toward Moscow
articles.title: Russia says more than 600 drones launched towards Moscow overnight
articles.summary: Russian air defence forces intercepted most of the 613 drones launched toward Moscow overnight, according to state news agency TASS. Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin reported on Telegram that 231 unmanned aerial vehicles were destroyed on approach, while the rest were neutralised on distant paths between Wednesday and Thursday. Meanwhile, a separate strike damaged an educational institution in Kharkiv.
articles.description: The attack is the latest in a series of major drone assaults targeting the Moscow region.

articles.headline: Tens of thousands of young Germans prepare for youth protests
articles.title: Germans to join Europe's youth protest wave
articles.summary: About 150,000 young people have registered to demonstrate across approximately 30 German cities, including Berlin, Frankfurt, and Cologne, on October 31, 2026. Organised by the non-partisan alliance GenZ regelt!, the protesters complain about the high cost of living, poorly maintained schools, government spending cuts, and military rearmament. While the movement rejects violence, German authorities and police are deploying thousands of officers amid concerns of potential rioting similar to recent unrest in France and Italy.
articles.description: In Germany, about 150,000 people have so far registered to turn out on October 31 in around 30 cities, including Berlin, Frankfurt and Cologne, for protests led by a group dubbed "GenZ regelt!" (Gen Z has got this!).

articles.headline: Ukraine resumes attacks on Russian oil refineries, Russia says
articles.title: Ukraine has resumed strikes on Russian oil refineries, Russia says
articles.summary: Russia announced on October 30, 2026, that Ukraine resumed drone strikes against its oil-processing facilities, targeting three refineries and one gas-chemical complex. Alexander Novak, Russia's deputy prime minister for energy issues, stated that the attacks could reduce diesel export volumes for November, potentially impacting global markets. The renewed strikes follow a brief lull after U.S. President Donald Trump pressured Kyiv to halt such attacks to lower global fuel prices.
articles.description: There was no immediate comment from Ukraine

articles.headline: Christa Pike shares statement on physical and mental pain after failed execution
articles.title: US inmate Christa Pike says she woke up 'confused and in pain' after failed execution
articles.summary: US death row inmate Christa Pike released her first public statement since surviving a botched execution involving two lethal injections of pentobarbital in September. Discharged from the hospital late last month, Pike stated she struggles with continuous pain. Convicted for murdering Colleen Slemmer in 1995, Pike expressed distress over the execution failure. Tennessee Governor Bill Lee subsequently paused all executions for the year and ordered an independent review.
articles.description: It is Pike's first public statement since she survived an execution attempt by lethal injection in September.

articles.headline: Federal judge rejects challenge to California noncitizen voter ballots
articles.title: Judge rejects Trump effort to block California ‘noncitizen’ ballots
articles.summary: United States District Judge David Carter on Wednesday rejected a Department of Justice request to temporarily stop California from counting mail ballots from 20,000 alleged noncitizens. The ruling came six days before the midterm elections as the Trump administration expands voter investigations across at least 13 states. The Justice Department swiftly appealed the decision to the Ninth US Circuit Court of Appeals.
articles.description: More than 100 subpoenas issued across 13 states as government ramps up search for alleged noncitizen voters.

articles.headline: Beijing dismisses report alleging Chinese spy plot targeting Nvidia CEO
articles.title: China denies spying on Nvidia's Jensen Huang
articles.summary: China rejected a report by The New York Times claiming that a Chinese executive connected to a Singapore-based data centre company acted as part of a spy plot targeting Jensen Huang, the head of U.S. chip giant Nvidia. Foreign Ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun called the report groundless speculation on October 30, 2026. An Nvidia spokesperson stated that the executive only received ordinary business information and that allegations of chip smuggling were investigated and debunked.
articles.description: China is in a race for tech dominance with the United States, which restricts the export to China of the most cutting-edge silicon chips, designed by industry leader Nvidia and used to train and run AI models

articles.headline: Manisha Bhanwala becomes first Indian woman to win wrestling world championship gold
articles.title: Manisha wins historic World title
articles.summary: Manisha Bhanwala secured a historic victory on Friday at the World wrestling championships in Astana by defeating United States competitor Abigail Elizabeth Nette 8-6 in the 59kg final. The twenty-nine-year-old wrestler overcame a six-point deficit to become the first Indian woman to win a world title, contributing to India's best-ever female team performance at the event.

articles.headline: Helicopter crash in Uttarakhand raises safety concerns following weather warnings
articles.title: Helicopter sorties were allowed despite orange alert and CMO advice to regulate tourists, says activist
articles.summary: A helicopter crash on October 30, 2026, along the Badrinath-Dehradun route killed six people, prompting scrutiny over why flights operated despite an orange alert for heavy rain and snow issued by officials. Activist Anoop Nautiyal stated that weather warnings were ignored, while Prateek Jain, Chief Executive Officer of the Uttarakhand Civil Aviation Development Authority, defended the operations by saying the weather was clear at the time of the incident.
articles.description: Activist Anoop Nautiyal said the tragedy was particularly disturbing as weather warnings had been issued in advance. An orange alert (for heavy to very heavy rainfall and snowfall) had been issued for five districts, including Chamoli, for October 30.

articles.headline: Madras High Court Chief Justice calls for speeding up criminal justice system
articles.title: Victim of crime should never become victim of process: Madras High Court Chief Justice
articles.summary: Madras High Court Chief Justice Sushrut Arvind Dharmadhikari stated in Chennai on October 30, 2026, that criminal justice procedures must be expedited to prevent victims from suffering further trauma. Speaking at a national conference at the University of Madras, Justice Dharmadhikari emphasized that legal frameworks should offer immediate support and unconditional dignity to those affected by crime.
articles.description: Legal and administrative procedures must never inflict fresh trauma on those who are really broken, they must offer immediate support, public care, and unconditional dignity, Justice Dharmadhikari said

articles.headline: Vehicular pollution remains unmitigated despite strict screening protocols
articles.title: Polluting vehicles remain unchecked despite strict PUC norms
articles.summary: Heavy smoke emissions from city buses and heavy vehicles continue to go unchecked in Keralam despite stringent screening protocols for pollution under control certificates. According to transport and traffic enforcement officials, local squads lack mobile testing units to catch violators. Meanwhile, residents allege that polluting vehicles are often used for illegal smuggling activities. Published on October 30, 2026, the report highlights growing air quality concerns in Kozhikode.
articles.description: Emissions containing pollutants such as carbon monoxide, nitrogen oxides and fine particulate matter, which can adversely affect human health, remain a concern despite initiatives by the State and Union governments to promote electric vehicles through attractive financing schemes and subsidies.

articles.headline: Indraprastha Gas Limited reports sharp drop in second-quarter net profit
articles.title: IGL net profit plummets 93% on higher input gas cost and consumer price protection
articles.summary: Indraprastha Gas Limited reported a 93 percent year-on-year drop in net profit to 24.38 crore rupees for the second quarter due to rising input gas costs and measures to protect consumers from global price volatility. Despite the profit decline, gross sales turnover surged by 35.4 percent to 5,999.13 crore rupees alongside an eight percent increase in overall sales volumes.
articles.description: Indraprastha Gas Ltd’s overall sales grew 8% on a year-over-year basis.

articles.headline: Police in Scotland launch investigation into former Prince Andrew and Jeffrey Epstein
articles.title: Police in Scotland launch Andrew and Epstein royal castle investigation
articles.summary: Police Scotland opened an inquiry into visits by the former Prince Andrew to King Charles III's Balmoral estate with Jeffrey Epstein and Ghislaine Maxwell. According to Police Scotland, the investigation is at an early stage. United States Department of Justice documents previously showed the figures at Balmoral in 1999, prompting several United Kingdom forces to examine Epstein-related material.
articles.description: Media reports say the inquiries are related to claims that women were trafficked to the king’s Balmoral estate.

articles.headline: Sun Pharmaceutical Industries reports drop in net profit for the September quarter
articles.title: Sun Pharma Q2 profit plunges 36% on exceptional charges despite revenue growth
articles.summary: Sun Pharmaceutical Industries reported a 36.4 percent year-on-year decline in consolidated net profit to 1,988.5 crore rupees for the quarter ending in September. Managing director Kirti Ganorkar stated that performance was driven by momentum in India and emerging markets. The results were weighed down by exceptional charges of 1,268.8 crore rupees related to an acquisition and an antitrust litigation settlement.
articles.description: Excluding the exceptional items, adjusted net profit stood at ₹3,162 crore.

articles.headline: Supreme Court declines to extend deadline for electoral records verification in Keralam
articles.title: Updating electoral records a ‘continuing process’, says Supreme Court
articles.summary: The Supreme Court on October 30, 2026, found no need to extend the Special Intensive Revision deadline in Keralam, stating that updating electoral records is a continuing process. A Bench led by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant permitted petitioners to submit details of individuals who missed the deadline. The Election Commission of India agreed to examine these representations and submit a report.
articles.description: Bench finds it unnecessary to formally extend deadline for re-verification of Special Intensive Revision in Keralam

articles.headline: Thousands of students and workers protest across Italy amid high police presence
articles.title: Thousands of students, workers protest in Italy under heavy security
articles.summary: Thousands of students, teachers, and workers protested across Italian cities on October 30, 2026, demanding increased school funding and cost of living relief. Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni's government recently proposed a 175.2-million-euro aid package for fuel-impacted workers and tougher laws on public gatherings. Demonstrators in cities including Rome and Milan marched past heavy police deployments to voice opposition to rearmament and economic pressures.
articles.description: Marches were held in dozens of cities up and down the country, including in Bologna, Genoa, Naples, and Turin — where a few minor skirmishes between protesters and riot police occurred at the start of the protest

articles.headline: Andhra Pradesh chief minister minimises cyclone damage through prompt response
articles.title: Chandrababu Naidu’s prompt response helps minimise cyclone damage
articles.summary: Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu mitigated property damage and prevented major loss of life following Cyclone Arnab. By monitoring the situation via the Real Time Governance Society and coordinating with district collectors during his October 2026 field visits, he ensured rapid restoration of power, blocked highway clearance, and submitted preliminary loss estimates to the Union government for financial assistance.
articles.description: Round-the-clock monitoring, field visits and swift relief measures help contain losses and restore essential services; CM seeks Central assistance for recovery

articles.headline: Andhra Pradesh readies for local body elections on November 1
articles.title: Andhra Pradesh SEC gears up for polls in 100 Urban Local Bodies on November 1
articles.summary: The State Election Commission has finalized security and administrative measures to conduct polls across 100 Urban Local Bodies on November 1 after previous delays caused by candidate nomination disputes. Authorities have deployed over 36,000 police personnel, drones, and CCTV cameras to maintain law and order, while 17 candidates have already been elected unanimously ahead of the upcoming voting process.
articles.description: 36,351 police personnel, drones and CCTV cameras deployed to ensure peaceful polling; 400-plus flying squads to enforce Model Code of Conduct; counting of votes on November 3

articles.headline: Police Scotland investigates Jeffrey Epstein stay at Balmoral estate
articles.title: Scottish police probe Andrew, Epstein stay at royal castle: U.K. media
articles.summary: Police Scotland is conducting early inquiries into the late U.S. sex offender Jeffrey Epstein's reported 1999 visit to the royal Balmoral estate in Scotland. According to U.K. media, the investigation follows the release of U.S. documents mentioning the trip arranged by ex-prince Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor. The former prince, recently stripped of royal titles amid ongoing scrutiny, has consistently denied all allegations of wrongdoing.
articles.description: Epstein, who died in prison in 2019 while awaiting trial for sex trafficking, is believed to have visited the British monarch's estate in northeast Scotland in 1999 along with his jailed ex-girlfriend and accomplice, Ghislaine Maxwell

articles.headline: Indian Oil Corporation reports soaring net profit in September quarter
articles.title: IOC Q2 profit soars 184% on higher refining margins
articles.summary: State-owned Indian Oil Corporation reported a standalone net profit exceeding ₹21,630 crore for the September quarter of 2026, driven by higher refining margins and lower benchmark crude oil prices between mid-June and mid-August. Revenue grew by nearly 30% to over ₹2.62 lakh crore, while domestic petroleum product sales reached 23.98 million metric tonnes. However, the company warned of future earnings pressure from potential inventory losses.
articles.description: Indian Oil’s gross refining margins, after subtracting for special additional excise duty (SAED), during the reported quarter stood at $18.52 per barrel.

articles.headline: India cuts U.S. and Russian oil imports amid sanctions
articles.title: India slashed U.S. and Russian oil in September, coinciding with ‘Russia Sanctions Act’; import from UAE increases
articles.summary: Official data shows India reduced its September 2026 oil imports from the United States to zero and significantly cut Russian oil purchases, coinciding with the U.S. passing the Russia Sanctions Act. To make up the shortfall, India increased oil imports from the United Arab Emirates by 67 percent compared to August, driving the UAE's share to an all-time high of twenty-six point five percent.
articles.description: Government data shows that India’s oil sourcing remains highly concentrated, with just Russia and the UAE accounting for 60% of oil imports

articles.headline: GAIL doubles net profit driven by natural gas marketing
articles.title: GAIL profit more than doubles on strong gas marketing performance
articles.summary: State-owned Gas Authority of India Ltd more than doubled its net profit to ₹4,650.22 crore in the September quarter, bolstered by strong performance in its natural gas marketing vertical. Revenue from operations rose 31.2% year-on-year to ₹45,924 crore. Director of Finance Satish Kumar Sinha noted that portfolio flexibility and spot sourcing helped offset supply disruptions stemming from the ongoing West Asia crisis.
articles.description: Profit before taxes of their natural gas marketing business rose more than two-and-half times during the quarter.

articles.headline: Swiss foreign minister visits North Korea to discuss political ties
articles.title: Swiss foreign minister talks political ties on rare visit to North Korea
articles.summary: Swiss Foreign Minister Ignazio Cassis concluded a two-day visit to Pyongyang on October 31, 2026, marking the first trip by a Swiss government minister in over two decades. During his visit, he met North Korean officials to discuss regularising political relations and formally reopened Switzerland's diplomatic office. Cassis subsequently traveled to South Korea to address regional security and bilateral ties.
articles.description: Switzerland formally reopens diplomatic office in North Korea after its closure in 2020.

articles.headline: US President Donald Trump reinstates previously cancelled midterm rallies in Kansas and Iowa
articles.title: Trump reverses course, reinstates cancelled campaign rallies
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump reversed his earlier decision and will now headline in-person rallies in Kansas and Iowa ahead of the midterm elections. According to a source speaking to Al Jazeera, the events were rearranged to include tele-rallies. The reversal follows competitive polling data in both states and comes as Republican candidates face scrutiny over living costs.
articles.description: The decision marks a sharp reversal after the US president said he didn't feel like he had to hold the events.

articles.headline: Airline head says Flavio Bolsonaro getaway plane paid via US bank account
articles.title: Bolsonaro's getaway plane paid for from U.S. bank: Airline
articles.summary: The airline executive who flew Flavio Bolsonaro to the United States following his election defeat told Agence France-Presse that an intermediary paid for the charter using a United States bank account. Luis Grande, head of Baires Fly, stated that a broker transferred one hundred fifty thousand dollars to an Argentine bank. The travel occurred after Bolsonaro lost to Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva.
articles.description: Following the vote, the 45-year-old snuck out of Brazil via Argentina and Ecuador in a cloak-and-dagger operation, after being ordered to surrender his passports due to several ongoing investigations against him

articles.headline: Sri Lankan President Anura Kumara Dissanayake maintains economic stability after two years
articles.title: Anura Dissanayake running to stay in the same place
articles.summary: Sri Lankan President Anura Kumara Dissanayake has preserved national economic stability and policy continuity during his first two years in office, following the economic chaos of 2022 and the Argalaya uprising. Despite his party previously campaigning against International Monetary Fund packages, the administration maintained commitments established by predecessor Ranil Wickremesinghe, working alongside an inexperienced cabinet.
articles.description: Anura Kumara Dissanayake, in two years in office, has ensured stability to Sri Lankan economy but he has a lot to accomplish in terms of political reforms

articles.headline: Senator Chris Murphy blames US military aid waiver for Egyptian press crackdown
articles.title: Democratic senator blames Egypt press crackdown on US military aid decision
articles.summary: United States Senator Chris Murphy accused the administration of abandoning the Egyptian people by waiving human rights conditions on over three hundred million dollars in military funding. Speaking at the Middle East Institute, Murphy linked the funding release to recent arrests and outlet closures targeting independent journalists in Cairo, while the State Department defended the waiver citing national security interests.
articles.description: Chris Murphy said waiving a human rights condition on aid paved the way for arrests of journalists.

articles.headline: Activists accuse Israeli settlers of assaulting foreign nationals in West Bank
articles.title: Activists accuse Israeli settlers of assault in occupied West Bank
articles.summary: Russian activist Adele Shoko reported that armed Israeli settlers attacked her and two colleagues in the Palestinian village of Umm al-Khair within the occupied West Bank. According to Shoko, the victims suffered physical abuse and detention by authorities following the incident. This event follows an earlier October 16 attack in Abu Falah where masked settlers targeted Palestinian olive farmers and injured Washington Post photojournalist Heidi Levine.
articles.description: Footage shows men, some armed, beating a US journalist and an Israeli-Russian activist in Umm al-Khair.

articles.headline: Namma Metro transports a human kidney between Bengaluru stations in 37 minutes.
articles.title: Namma Metro facilitates swift transport of human kidney for transplant
articles.summary: Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Limited facilitated the rapid transit of a human kidney from Jalappa Hospital in Kolar to Fortis Hospital in Nagarabhavi, Bengaluru. Transported via a metro train from Benniganahalli to Attiguppe stations, the organ completed its journey in 37 minutes on Friday to ensure a timely transplant procedure, marking the seventh organ transport operation managed by the network.
articles.description: With Friday’s transfer, Namma Metro has facilitated seven organ transportation operations so far.

articles.headline: Karnataka government outlines urbanisation plan to decentralise regional growth
articles.title: Government plans balanced urban growth beyond Bengaluru, as demography shifts
articles.summary: Karnataka Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar unveiled a strategic development agenda aimed at managing demographic shifts and curbing migration toward Bengaluru by promoting balanced industrial and infrastructural expansion across districts. Projections indicate the state urban population will reach 70 percent by 2047, prompting targeted investments in public transport, digital governance, and regional employment opportunities.
articles.description: ‘The proportion of Karnataka’s population living in urban areas is expected to increase from the present 46% to 70% by 2047’

articles.headline: Bank of Baroda reports record quarterly profit driven by non-interest income
articles.title: BoB posts record Q2 profit of ₹6,532-cr on 96% surge in non-interest income
articles.summary: Bank of Baroda achieved its highest-ever quarterly net profit of 6,532 crore rupees for the quarter ending in September, supported by a significant increase in non-interest income and improved asset quality metrics. The public sector lender reported a decline in gross non-performing assets to 1.78 percent alongside broad growth across global advances and domestic deposits.
articles.description: Asset quality improved, with gross non-performing assets (GNPA) declining to 1.78% from 2.16% a year ago.

articles.headline: Crime branch alleges deliberate manipulation in Kerala public service commission exam
articles.title: Crime Branch alleges ‘deliberate manipulation’ in Kerala PSC examination
articles.summary: Investigators allege that 10 questions were intentionally excluded from a Kerala Public Service Commission examination conducted for the State Planning Board to alter candidate rankings and secure appointments for preferred individuals. The Special Investigation Team has issued questioning notices to multiple officials and commission members following the arrest of a former deputy secretary.
articles.description: Irregularities in the State Planning Board exam were carried out with the knowledge of officials, including P. Satheesh, former deputy secretary of PSC, say police in his remand report

articles.headline: Drone strikes on Darfur market in Sudan kill over one hundred people
articles.title: Strikes on Darfur market in Sudan killed more than 100, rights group says
articles.summary: Military drone strikes targeting a busy market in Nyala, South Darfur, killed more than 100 people, predominantly women and children, according to the rights group Emergency Lawyers. Witnesses reported that the attack struck an area frequented by paramilitary Rapid Support Forces fighters and civilian vendors. Doctors Without Borders stated that a local hospital received 36 bodies and treated over 150 wounded individuals following the bombardment.
articles.description: Women and children killed as witnesses say attack struck civilian shopkeepers, RSF fighters.

articles.headline: Israeli settlers savagely attack journalists in occupied West Bank
articles.title: Israeli settlers savagely attack journalists in occupied West Bank
articles.description: Videos circulating on social media show Israeli settlers assaulting three foreign journalists in the West Bank

articles.headline: Kerala health minister visits Attappady following tribal infant deaths
articles.title: Keralam Health Minister to visit Attappady amid infant deaths; expert team begins probe
articles.summary: Health Minister K. Muraleedharan announced a personal visit to Attappady alongside deployed expert medical teams to investigate recent infant deaths in tribal colonies and assess local healthcare delivery. The inquiry involves examining pregnant women, auditing child mortality cases from 2026, and reviewing facility performance, while political figures have criticised the administration for persistent systemic failures.
articles.description: Keralam government deputes two teams of experts from the Health department and the Directorate of Medical Education, who will camp at Attapady and conduct a detailed inquiry into the circumstances leading to infant deaths; CPI leader says government has failed to identify the root causes or find a permanent solution to the issue

articles.headline: Christa Pike speaks out about constant pain following failed execution
articles.title: Christa Pike says she feels constant pain in her first statement since failed Tennessee execution
articles.summary: Death row inmate Christa Pike stated in her first public statement on October 30, 2026, that she remains in constant physical and mental pain after surviving a lethal injection in Tennessee on September 30. Convicted for the 1995 murder of Colleen Slemmer, Pike expressed gratitude to medical workers and supporters. Tennessee Governor Bill Lee has ordered an independent review and paused all executions for the remainder of the year.
articles.description: Pike survived two doses of pentobarbital as the State tried to execute her on September 30 for the 1995 stabbing death of classmate Colleen Slemmer

articles.headline: Glacial lake outburst floods Gasa Tshachu hot springs in Bhutan
articles.title: Bhutan hot springs hit by flood from glacial lake burst
articles.summary: A flash flood triggered by the Shintaphu glacial lake bursting its banks washed away infrastructure and roads at the Gasa Tshachu natural hot springs in Bhutan. State broadcaster BBS reported no injuries or deaths from the Thursday night incident, though damage assessments remain difficult. Authorities issued flood warnings for surrounding river valleys and neighbouring India, while the road to Laya village was closed indefinitely following the disaster.
articles.description: No injuries reported after glacial lake burst, causing a flash flood and disrupting Bhutan's Gasa Tshachu hot springs.

articles.headline: Serbians storm TV studio as pro-Vucic media faces reckoning
articles.title: Serbians storm TV studio as pro-Vucic media faces reckoning
articles.description: Serbians stormed a TV studio and confronted its editor-in-chief after a student-led protest movement swept into power.

articles.headline: Jio Platforms shares surge nearly 28 percent since market debut
articles.title: Jio Platforms shares surge 28% since market debut
articles.summary: Shares of digital services company Jio Platforms surged 27.89 percent on the BSE to reach ₹1,431.20 from the issue price of ₹1,119 following their market debut on October 28, 2026. The company added ₹12,754.51 crore in market valuation over three days, maintaining its position as India's second most valuable firm. The initial public offering closed last week after receiving bids for 22.19 times the shares on offer.
articles.description: The stock of the country's second most valuable firm by market capitalisation jumped 27.89% to ₹1,431.20 from the issue price of ₹1,119 on the BSE

articles.headline: Department of Homeland Security personnel details leaked in major United States cyber breach
articles.title: Details of thousands of US immigration agents leaked in major hack
articles.summary: Personal details of more than 41,000 personnel from the United States Department of Homeland Security were leaked online in a breach publicized on Wednesday. The leaked database, dubbed Icepick, included names and work addresses of agents from Immigration and Customs Enforcement and Customs and Border Protection. Officials stated the agency is actively investigating the incident involving single sign-on service Okta.
articles.description: A group called the Department of Peace released information on more than 41,000 DHS staff.

articles.headline: Cabinet approves three percent dearness allowance hike for central employees
articles.title: Cabinet approves 3% hike in dearness allowance for central government employees
articles.summary: The Union Cabinet approved a three percent increase in dearness allowance and dearness relief on October 28, 2026, benefiting over 1.17 crore central government employees and pensioners ahead of Diwali. Information and Broadcasting Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw stated the hike is effective from July 1, 2026. Additionally, the Cabinet cleared the Container Manufacturing Promotion Scheme with a budgetary outlay of Rs 10,000 crore.
articles.description: The DA and DR increase will be effective from July 1, 2026 and will benefit 48.54 lakh employees and 68.71 lakh pensioners

articles.headline: Italy tightens security as nationwide protests target living costs
articles.title: Italy tightens security as students, unions launch nationwide protests
articles.summary: Italy deployed a heavy police presence and enhanced security at major landmarks as tens of thousands of demonstrators joined nationwide rallies on Friday. Organised by trade unions and student groups, the protests addressed soaring living costs, higher fuel prices, and Middle East conflicts. Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni recently introduced a 175 million euro aid package and proposed family benefits in the draft 2027 budget.
articles.description: Rallies across the country target living costs, investment in education and the wars in the Middle East.

articles.headline: Flávio Bolsonaro arrives in Miami after losing Brazilian presidential election
articles.title: Flávio Bolsonaro denies fleeing Brazil after landing in Miami
articles.summary: Brazilian Senator Flávio Bolsonaro arrived in Miami after traveling through Argentina following his defeat in Sunday's presidential run-off election against Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva. The United States State Department granted visas to Bolsonaro and his family, while Brazilian authorities have cancelled his passport and continue investigations into alleged money laundering and banking irregularities.
articles.description: The defeated Brazilian candidate claims to be the victim of a coup d’état and political persecution, recycling unsubstantiated allegations of “electoral fraud”.

articles.headline: Anthropic files initial public offering prospectus detailing artificial intelligence risks
articles.title: Silicon Valley wants you to invest in miracles
articles.summary: Anthropic filed a massive 335-page S-1 prospectus with Wall Street, blending financial targets with extensive risk warnings regarding advanced technology. The founders urged prospective investors to view their purchase as a long-term commitment to safe artificial intelligence development. As a public benefit corporation, the firm must balance its social mission with shareholder interests while acknowledging potential existential threats to humanity.
articles.description: Investing in any stock is kind of like gambling in the sense that you're betting your money on a company's future performance. But how do you bet on a technology that could, in the worst-case scenario, "pose catastrophic or existential risks to humanity," or best case, "bring forth an age of miracles"? To some extent, […]

articles.headline: Irish government plans body to assess potential united Ireland
articles.title: Irish government to assess potential for united Ireland
articles.summary: The Irish government announced plans to establish a dedicated body to research models and challenges for a united Ireland. Prime Minister Micheal Martin stated that Dublin must prepare for various constitutional outcomes regarding Northern Ireland, following the 1998 Good Friday peace agreement. Although opinion polls indicate continued support for remaining within the United Kingdom, the margin has narrowed since the UK left the European Union.
articles.description: London has to call a referendum on Irish unity if it appears likely that most Northern Irish voters would ​back it.

articles.headline: Sam Altman defends OpenAI math discoveries despite researcher criticism over chaotic releases
articles.title: Sam Altman sympathizes with mathematicians, but says OpenAI’s math onslaught won’t stop
articles.summary: OpenAI chief executive officer Sam Altman stated that humanity deserves fundamental knowledge, defending the release of AI-generated mathematical results despite researcher criticism over poor communication and inadequate verification. Speaking on the Cheeky Pint podcast, Altman admitted spending hundreds of millions on math problems and hinted at holding further undiscovered breakthroughs. Mathematicians have criticized the company for inadequate attribution and gatekeeping scientific research.
articles.description: After months of bombarding mathematicians with a relentless stream of AI-generated results, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman says he sympathizes with researchers struggling to make sense of it all. But he has no intention of stopping - and hints there could be much more to come from the company's stockpile of discoveries. "I think, on net, […]

articles.headline: Jharkhand Chief Minister Hemant Soren and Congress leaders leave for Delhi INDIA bloc rally
articles.title: Jharkhand: CM, Congress leaders leave for Delhi to take part in INDIA bloc rally on November 1
articles.summary: Jharkhand Chief Minister Hemant Soren and state Congress leaders departed for New Delhi to join the INDIA bloc rally on November 1, 2026. Jharkhand Congress chief Keshav Mahto Kamlesh stated that participants will demand the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged voter list irregularities and vote theft. Thousands of party workers are expected to attend the opposition protest in the national capital.
articles.description: The rally on Sunday is expected to bring together opposition leaders and workers from across the country

articles.headline: Sudan RSF commander defects from Hemedti’s forces
articles.title: Sudan RSF commander defects from Hemedti’s forces
articles.description: Senior Rapid Support Forces commander Siddiq Ander says he has defected, in an exclusive video obtained by Al Jazeera.

articles.headline: District Collector urges coordinated action to prevent elephant electrocutions in Chittoor
articles.title: Electrocution behind 32 of 49 elephant deaths in Andhra’s Chittoor since 2015
articles.summary: District Collector Sumit Kumar directed the Forest Department and the Andhra Pradesh Southern Power Distribution Company Limited to address vulnerable electrical infrastructure on October 30, 2026. Officials revealed that electrocution caused 32 of 49 elephant deaths in the Chittoor region between 2015 and 2026, prompting authorities to commit to fixing 150 critical locations within a month.
articles.description: Chittoor Collector Sumit Kumar orders 150 critical spots with low-hanging power lines to be fixed within a month

articles.headline: Climate academic Andreas Malm barred from entering the UK
articles.title: Swedish academic says he has been barred from UK over event with Palestine Action founder
articles.summary: Andreas Malm, a senior lecturer at Lund University in Sweden, stated he received a Home Office letter denying him entry because his presence was deemed not conducive to the public good. The academic believes the decision stems from a scheduled London panel with a co-founder of Palestine Action, though the Home Office does not comment on individual cases.
articles.description: Andreas Malm was due to appear on a panel alongside a co-founder of the proscribed group next week.

articles.headline: Riot police deployed in Madrid as protests erupt over deadly train crash
articles.title: Riot police deployed in Madrid as protests erupt over deadly train crash
articles.description: A deadly train crash fuelled anger in Spain as far-right demonstrators clashed with police

articles.headline: Three individuals arrested in Hyderabad for supplying mule accounts
articles.title: Three from Hyderabad held for supplying 83 mule accounts to cyber fraudsters; ₹10.05 crore siphoned off
articles.summary: Police in Hyderabad arrested a 24-year-old waiter and two others for procuring 83 mule bank accounts and selling them to cyber fraudsters for up to 25,000 rupees each. Investigators found that several accounts were linked to fourteen cyber frauds across India, with the network receiving over 10 million rupees through illegal transactions that were withdrawn immediately.
