articles.title: 'The city is alive': A brief peace in Kherson, but residents fear what comes next
articles.summary: The Ukrainian city of Kherson has experienced its first two days of quiet in years due to a temporary, US-brokered ceasefire that ends on Sunday. Facilitated by US First Lady Melania Trump to evacuate civilians from Russian-occupied Oleshky, the truce has allowed residents to walk streets and access damaged homes. However, local sources fear Russian forces are using the pause to strengthen military positions.
articles.description: A temporary ceasefire has brought rare quiet to Kherson, offering its residents a glimpse of normal life before fighting resumes.

articles.headline: French suspect admits targeting Muslims and North Africans in shooting attack
articles.title: Man targeted Muslims, Africans and North Africans, French prosecutors say
articles.summary: France's anti-terrorism prosecutor's office confirmed that a thirty-nine-year-old suspect named Kevin T has been formally charged with terrorism after admitting he deliberately targeted individuals appearing to be Muslim, African, or North African. The shooting across Trappes and La Verriere left one person, twenty-six-year-old Pengo Bossio Wangi, dead and seven injured. Police found weapons, ammunition, and extremist materials during a search of his home.
articles.description: Prosecutor Olivier Christen said suspect admitted that he chose the location because it was 'a hotbed for Islamists'.

articles.headline: NHRC issues notice to Kolkata Police over public parading of three accused
articles.title: NHRC flags human rights concerns over parading of three persons in south Kolkata
articles.summary: The National Human Rights Commission took suo motu cognisance of media reports regarding three individuals paraded semi-clad with ropes around their waists in Kolkata's Behala area. The Commission issued a notice demanding a detailed report from the Kolkata Police Commissioner within two weeks, noting the incident raises serious human rights violations. The action follows the arrest of two men who were similarly paraded by police following an assault involving a minor.
articles.description: The Commission took suo motu cognisance of the incident based on media reports and observed that the contents of the news report, if true, “raise serious issues of violation of human rights”

articles.headline: J&K Deputy CM hits back at BJP criticism over cabinet expansion
articles.title: ‘Show me one Muslim minister at Centre, BJP-ruled States’: J&K Deputy CM
articles.summary: Jammu and Kashmir Deputy Chief Minister Surinder Choudhary criticized the Bharatiya Janata Party on Thursday, stating the party lacks the right to criticize the National Conference when it has no Muslim ministers in the central government or BJP-led states. Choudhary also defended his Hindu identity following BJP criticism over cabinet representation after four new ministers joined Chief Minister Omar Abdullah's cabinet on October 27, 2026.
articles.description: J&K witnessed a Cabinet expansion on October 27, with four new faces joining the Omar Abdullah Cabinet

articles.headline: Cornell faculty begin no-confidence vote over handling of alleged sexual assault
articles.title: Cornell begins no confidence vote over handling of alleged gang rape
articles.summary: Instructors at Cornell University initiated a non-binding leadership ballot on Thursday that runs through November 6 following widespread campus outcry. The action follows an October lawsuit alleging a female student was drugged and assaulted by seven men at a fraternity in 2024. President Michael Kotlikoff faced criticism over the institution's response, while two accused students sought to remove New York Attorney General Letitia James from overseeing the renewed criminal investigation.
articles.description: Faculty vote will continue until next Friday and could send message that school's president has lost their confidence.

articles.headline: Ennore residents criticize government agencies for pollution and wetland restoration gaps
articles.title: Ennore residents’ report card for govt. flags gaps in wetland restoration, pollution control
articles.summary: Residents in Ennore evaluated twenty-four government bodies on October 30, 2026, giving poor scores for unfulfilled commitments regarding wetland restoration, industrial pollution control, and fisheries. The community highlighted issues including a recent mass fish kill, incomplete dredging, and inadequate healthcare infrastructure that continues to impact local livelihoods and public safety.
articles.description: The report assesses 24 govt. bodies, five of which score ‘zero’ for failing to initiate their assessed commitments; it flags fly-ash leaks, illegal emissions, and hot-water discharge into Ennore Creek

articles.headline: Jammu and Kashmir High Court strikes down water usage charges under 2010 Act
articles.title: J&K High Court declares imposition of water usage charges under 2010 Act in UT as ‘ultra vires’
articles.summary: The Jammu and Kashmir High Court ruled on October 29, 2026, that water usage charges imposed on hydro power projects under the 2010 Act are unconstitutional. A Division Bench held that the legislature lacked the competence to levy taxes on electricity generation under the guise of water charges, granting relief to eleven petitioning companies.
articles.description: The J&K government in 2010 passed the J&K Water Resources (Regulation and Management) Act “to generate revenue on water resources by charging for its usage from private and public units, which will include companies generating electricity in the State”

articles.headline: Google adds direct document generation and editing features inside Gemini chats
articles.title: You can generate and edit Google Docs files directly in Gemini chats now
articles.summary: Google introduced new file capabilities allowing all users to generate, preview, and edit various formats directly within Gemini chats. The update enables users to modify documents in full-screen mode and prompt the assistant for changes without leaving the application. While PDF features are available on both web and mobile, other formats currently remain limited to the web version.
articles.description: Now you can generate, preview, and edit PDFs, Google Docs, Google Sheets, slide decks, Markdown files, TXT files, and code directly within Google Gemini. The new file editing capabilities are available starting today for all Gemini users, and while PDF previews/editing works on both the web and mobile, all other file formats are only in […]

articles.headline: Texas Republican group files federal lawsuit seeking to block state election certification
articles.title: Texas Republican group seeks to block certification of state’s election
articles.summary: The Potter County Republican Party filed a lawsuit asking a federal judge to halt the certification of upcoming Texas midterm elections. The plaintiffs cited potential artificial intelligence interference and Chinese-made components in voting machines. They requested a complete hand count of paper ballots from every precinct, while state officials declined to comment on the ongoing legal challenge.
articles.description: Republicans in a Texas county have filed a lawsuit asking for ballots in the state's midterm races to be hand-counted.

articles.headline: Enforcement Directorate searches cryptocurrency platforms over alleged FEMA violations
articles.title: ED searches premises linked to Mudrex, Instadapp over alleged ₹4,600-crore FEMA violations
articles.summary: The Directorate of Enforcement conducted searches at multiple premises in Bengaluru and Madhya Pradesh on October 27, 2026, targeting cryptocurrency platforms Mudrex and Instadapp. According to the agency, the investigation involves unauthorized cross-border money transfers exceeding four thousand six hundred crore rupees utilizing stablecoins. Authorities stated that entities bypassed authorized banking channels through virtual digital assets, and the ongoing inquiry centers on alleged Foreign Exchange Management Act violations.

articles.headline: Left-arm spinner Vaishnavi Sharma secures five-wicket haul for India against Zimbabwe
articles.title: Vaishnavi — India’s new orchestrator
articles.summary: Left-arm spinner Vaishnavi Sharma claimed a sensational five-wicket haul to help India secure victory in the third one-day international against Zimbabwe at the BCA Stadium in Kotambi. The international newcomer, who previously debuted against Sri Lanka in Visakhapatnam in 2025, achieved the milestone almost a year after her first appearance.
articles.description: The left-arm spinner may not have burst onto the scene but is making a case for herself with stellar performances for the National team. Those who have followed her from close quarters believe that the 20-year-old is just getting started

articles.headline: National Investigation Agency takes over synagogue arson probe in Kerala
articles.title: NIA takes over probe into alleged arson attack at Kadavumbhagam synagogue in Keralam
articles.summary: The National Investigation Agency has assumed control of the investigation into an arson attack at the Kadavumbhagam Synagogue in Ernakulam following a directive from the Union Home Ministry. Kochi City police previously invoked the Unlawful Activities Prevention Act against the primary suspect, Ebin Paul. Investigators are examining potential international terror links, cryptocurrency transactions, and recovered communications referencing sensitive religious sites.
articles.description: Police cite suspected cryptocurrency payments, alleged reconnaissance videos and possible international terror links as grounds for a wider probe

articles.headline: Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri to visit Kathmandu for bilateral talks
articles.title: Foreign Secretary to visit Kathmandu as plans get underway for Nepal PM’s India visit
articles.summary: Indian Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri is scheduled to travel to Kathmandu on November 4, 2026, alongside ambassador Sudhakar Dalela. The visit aims to finalize preparations for Nepalese Prime Minister Balendra Shah's upcoming trip to India. Discussions will address bilateral cooperation, disaster management regarding the Bhote Koshi River floods, and the appointment process for new diplomatic envoys following recent political changes in Nepal.
articles.description: Nepal PM Balendra Shah is expected to visit Delhi by the end of the year, in what would be his first bilateral visit abroad, as he has been focused on domestic issues

articles.headline: Finnish police investigate Google over data centre environmental damage
articles.title: Finland launches criminal probe of suspected environmental damage by Google
articles.summary: Finnish authorities have initiated a criminal investigation into Tuike Finland, a local subsidiary of Alphabet’s Google, concerning suspected environmental violations at a data centre construction site near Muhos. Police are examining whether forest clearing and drainage activities breached the Water Act prior to required assessments. The probe follows a fifteen billion dollar infrastructure investment announcement, prompting local public scrutiny regarding water management and regulatory compliance.
articles.description: The US tech giant is investing $15bn in a huge new data centre project in northern Finland.

articles.headline: India defeats China in Asian Champions Trophy hockey match
articles.title: ACT: India registers hard-fought victory over a spirited China
articles.summary: The Indian men's hockey team secured a five to two victory against China at the Asian Champions Trophy on Thursday. Sukhjeet Singh and Harmanpreet Singh scored multiple goals, supported by Jugraj Singh, to overcome a structured Chinese defense. Despite a competitive challenge and penalty corner conversions from Yang Peng and Chen Chongcong, India maintained offensive momentum to claim the win under coach Craig Fulton.
articles.description: Sukhjeet and skipper Harmanpreet score a brace each for the home team

articles.headline: Albanian opposition members storm parliament and trigger smoke bombs
articles.title: Albanian opposition storms parliament, sets off flares and smoke bombs
articles.summary: Lawmakers in Albania disrupted a parliamentary session on Thursday by setting off smoke bombs and flares in Tirana. The protest was led by Sali Berisha, head of the Democratic Party of Albania, in support of demonstrators demanding the resignation of Prime Minister Edi Rama. Rama has faced months of anti-government protests triggered by economic stagnation and a luxury resort project.
articles.description: Opposition lawmakers disrupt parliament session, accusing prime minister of downplaying ongoing antigovernment protests.

articles.headline: India Meteorological Department warns of heavy rainfall in coastal Andhra Pradesh
articles.title: Coastal Andhra Pradesh may receive heavy rain from November 1 as low-pressure area brewing over Bay of Bengal
articles.summary: Following Cyclone Arnab, the India Meteorological Department announced that coastal Andhra Pradesh could experience another spell of heavy rain beginning November 1, 2026. A low-pressure area formed over the south Andaman Sea is expected to intensify into a depression and move northwest toward the coast by November 2. Officials noted that several districts remain rain-deficient from the previous storm.
articles.description: Formed over Andaman Sea, the low-pressure area may strengthen over the next three days and approach Andhra Pradesh coast, says IMD

articles.headline: Supreme Court orders NCLT and NCLAT leaders to submit proposals
articles.title: Corporate Affairs Ministry has ‘hijacked’ staff appointments in NCLT: Supreme Court
articles.summary: The Supreme Court of India directed the presidents of the National Company Law Tribunal and the National Company Law Appellate Tribunal to submit comprehensive infrastructure and staffing proposals within four weeks. The directive follows concerns over collapsing facilities at the NCLT Principal Bench and severe staffing shortages affecting daily operations.
articles.description: The court said the power to make staff appointments must remain with the NCLT president, and an employer-employee relationship must prevail between staff members and the tribunal

articles.headline: Uttar Pradesh bars violent system-change protesters from state government jobs
articles.title: No government jobs in Uttar Pradesh for protesters ‘involved in regime change through violence’
articles.summary: The Uttar Pradesh government updated its direct recruitment rules to disqualify individuals associated with organisations seeking to alter the established political system through violence. Issued by Principal Secretary M Devaraj, the revised character verification framework applies across government departments and local bodies, drawing criticism from opposition parties including the Samajwadi Party and Congress.
articles.description: The revised guidelines will apply to character verification in government departments, public sector corporations, boards and urban and rural local bodies; the government added, however, that political ideology alone cannot be grounds for disqualification

articles.headline: Samajwadi Party wins five Legislative Council seats in Uttar Pradesh polls
articles.title: U.P. MLC poll results mark a defeat of BJP’s anti-education policies: Opposition leaders
articles.summary: The opposition INDIA bloc declared the Samajwadi Party securing five of 11 Legislative Council seats in Uttar Pradesh as a rejection of Bharatiya Janata Party policies. Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav stated the outcome signals growing public discontent ahead of the 2027 assembly elections. Meanwhile, Congress officials alleged that administrative delays during vote counting favoured the ruling party.
articles.description: INDIA bloc leaders say SP victory in five of 11 Legislative Council seats provides a boost to the Opposition ahead of U.P.’s 2027 Assembly election; ‘Double defeat of the double engine,’ says SP chief

articles.headline: Pakistani court sentences human rights lawyers to ten years in prison
articles.title: Pakistan rights activist Imaan Mazari and husband jailed for 10 years
articles.summary: An antiterrorism court in Rawalpindi sentenced human rights lawyer Imaan Mazari and her husband, Hadi Ali Chattha, to ten years in prison on Thursday. Judge Tahir Abbas Sipra convicted the couple for security breaches involving England cricket team route barriers in Islamabad during October 2024. Relatives and Amnesty International criticized the trial as politically motivated and lacking due process.
articles.description: Couple say they are 'prisoners of conscience' being made an example of by Pakistan's military-backed authorities.

articles.headline: Canada and European Union leaders meet in Montreal to discuss ties
articles.title: EU chief lays out vision for new Canada partnership at Montreal summit
articles.summary: Canadian Prime Minister Carney and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen convened in Montreal for a two-day summit starting Thursday to discuss deepening bilateral cooperation. While European officials proposed a new associate membership status, nations like Germany raised concerns over the terminology. The meeting follows ongoing trade tensions between Canada and the United States under President Donald Trump.
articles.description: Ursula von der Leyen continued to use the term "associate member" for Canada despite some opposition of the bloc's members, including Germany.

articles.headline: Hotels and condiment stores raise tea and coffee prices following milk hike
articles.title: ₹8 milk price hike to push tea, coffee prices up by ₹5
articles.summary: Hotel associations and condiment stores across Karnataka announced that tea and coffee prices will increase by ₹5 per cup following a government decision to raise milk prices by ₹8 per litre starting November 1. Representatives noted that the sharp increase in input costs will also lead to higher prices for milk-based desserts, though bakeries will temporarily keep sweet prices steady due to intense market competition and declining profit margins.
articles.description: Last time, the government increased the price of milk by ₹4 per litre in April 1, 2025. Previous to this hike, in June 2024, the prices of milk were increased by ₹2 per litre in proportion to additional 50 ml per 500 ml milk packets by the State government.

articles.headline: India votes for UN General Assembly resolution to end US embargo on Cuba
articles.title: India votes in favour of UNGA resolution calling for end to US embargo on Cuba
articles.summary: The United Nations General Assembly adopted a resolution on October 28, 2026, with 130 countries voting in favour, including India, to demand the termination of the United States economic embargo against Cuba. Indian envoy Soumya Nair stated that international restrictions severely impair Cuba's economy, food production, and health services. The vote followed a tense procedural confrontation in the assembly hall involving U.S. Ambassador Mike Waltz and Cuban Foreign Minister Bruno Rodriguez Parrilla.
articles.description: The 193-member General Assembly adopted the resolution on October 28, with 130 countries voting in favour, 17 against and 25 abstaining

articles.headline: Indian pharmaceutical exports grow to sixteen billion dollars in first half
articles.title: Pharma H1 exports up 5% to $16.14-bn. as Europe offsets U.S. slowdown
articles.summary: India's pharmaceutical exports rose 4.90 percent year-on-year to $16.14 billion in the first half of fiscal year 2027, according to the Pharmaceuticals Export Promotion Council of India. Increased demand from Europe, Latin America, and ASEAN markets compensated for a 2.05 percent decline in shipments to North America. Drug formulations and biologicals comprised the largest export category at $11.91 billion.
articles.description: Market diversification strategy pays as exports to Europe, Africa, LAC and ASEAN gain momentum

articles.headline: Congress questions trial delays and trust official roles in Ram Temple donation theft case
articles.title: Congress questions delay in framing charges in Ram Temple donation theft case
articles.summary: Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh criticized authorities on October 29, 2026, over repeated delays in framing charges against eight suspects linked to alleged donation theft at the Ram Temple in Ayodhya. The opposition party questioned why former temple trust officials Champat Rai and Anil Mishra were listed as witnesses rather than defendants. Furthermore, the Congress demanded an independent investigation supervised by the Supreme Court into financial records, audit warnings, and comprehensive CCTV footage.
articles.description: Congress’s Jairam Ramesh questions delay in providing the complete CCTV footage and audio recordings, demands impartial investigation under the Supreme Court’s supervision

articles.headline: Kuki group initiates 48-hour shutdown in Manipur district over missing youths
articles.title: Shutdown begins in Manipur district over two missing Kuki youths
articles.summary: The Committee on Tribal Unity launched a 48-hour shutdown in Manipur's Kangpokpi district beginning on October 29, 2026, to protest the alleged abduction of two twenty-year-old Kuki youths. The missing individuals disappeared while travelling between Hengbung and Taphou Kuki villages, with non-Kuki extremists suspected of involvement. The organisation criticized what it termed a biased government response to kidnappings affecting the Kuki-Zomi community while exempting medical services and security forces from the closure.
articles.description: The Committee on Tribal Unity says the two 20-year-olds were kidnapped around dusk on October 28

articles.headline: Experts highlight roadblocks facing Kashmir apple industry at CII conclave
articles.title: Experts at CII meet flag roadblocks in Kashmir apple cart’s global ambition
articles.summary: Agricultural experts at the Confederation of Indian Industry meet in Srinagar on October 28 discussed major challenges confronting the Jammu and Kashmir horticulture sector, including poor cold chain transport, substandard fruit quality in southern markets, and insufficient cold storage. The sector supports roughly seven lakh farming families and contributes up to 10% of the region's Gross Domestic Product. Officials emphasized the need for modern technology, high-density plantations, and improved local plant material production to enhance global competitiveness.
articles.description: Kashmir has a small four-month window for exporting apples and the cold chain is still poor at maintaining the quality, said Dr. N.K. Krishna Kumar, ex-Deputy Director (Horticulture) Indian Council of Agricultural Research

articles.headline: Why US Sports Owners Spend Millions on Politics
articles.title: Why US Sports Owners Spend Millions on Politics
articles.description: US sports team owners include some of the wealthiest people in the world and some spend millions of dollars on politics

articles.headline: Youth groups in Itanagar protest detentions over mega dam opposition
articles.title: Anti-mega dam protest rocks Arunachal capital
articles.summary: Demonstrators gathered at Indira Gandhi Park in Itanagar on October 29 to demand the release of over thirty individuals detained following violent protests against the proposed Siang Upper Multipurpose Project in Arunachal Pradesh. Participants called for the protection of local lands and rivers, urging the government to halt pre-feasibility surveys. Meanwhile, religious and tribal forums appealed for constructive dialogue between authorities and local stakeholders to de-escalate regional tensions.
articles.description: The protestors in Itanagar want the Siang Upper Multipurpose Project plan scrapped and arrested activists released

articles.headline: Deadly rock collapse at famous Turkiye tourist site
articles.title: Deadly rock collapse at famous Turkiye tourist site
articles.description: Deadly rock collapse at famous Turkiye tourist site

articles.headline: Flash floods inundate Andhra Pradesh and Odisha border villages
articles.title: Flash floods leave AP-Odisha border villages inundated, traffic on NH-16 disrupted
articles.summary: Flash floods caused by surging waters in the Bahuda river and seasonal streams severely disrupted life across Ichchapuram and surrounding border villages on October 28 and 29. The inundation followed the release of approximately 86,000 cusecs of water from the Baghalati Dam in Odisha, cutting off traffic on National Highway 16. District authorities deployed disaster response teams and medical staff to distribute food and provide relief to affected residents.

articles.headline: Coal India reports 57 percent rise in second quarter net profit
articles.title: Coal India profit jumps 57% as higher offtake, prices weigh over costs
articles.summary: Coal India Limited posted a net profit of 6,547 crore rupees for the quarter ending September, marking a 57 percent increase driven by higher offtake and improved price realisations. The state-owned enterprise declared a second interim dividend of 10.25 rupees per equity share as overall revenue climbed 21 percent to 44,179 crore rupees. Production grew 4 percent to 151.37 million tonnes despite missing internal targets, while material costs rose 20 percent.
articles.description: Cost of input materials increased 20% during the quarter.

articles.headline: Industrial tourism grows across factory tours in China
articles.title: The rise of industrial tourism in China
articles.summary: Factory floor tours targeting high-tech manufacturing facilities, electric vehicle plants, and shipyards experienced a surge in popularity across China during the summer vacation. Booking data from the Tongcheng platform showed a 36 percent year-on-year increase, with families accounting for the majority of reservations. Promoted by the ruling Communist Party as a policy initiative, these industrial tours aim to showcase manufacturing capabilities, strengthen domestic brands, and educate young people on technology.
articles.description: Industrial tours showcase showcase innovation and manufacturing prowess to instil national pride, while presenting STEM as a sustainable career option for the youth

articles.headline: Qatar rejects Israeli accusations of election interference
articles.title: Israel’s anti-Qatar campaign bleeds into elections
articles.summary: Qatari foreign ministry spokesperson Majed al-Ansari categorically denied unsubstantiated claims by Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s party that Doha interfered in recent parliamentary elections. The official rejected the allegations as disinformation, emphasizing that Qatar respects internal Israeli matters and remains fully focused on its crucial international diplomatic and humanitarian mediation roles.
articles.description: Qatar's Foreign Ministry spokesman rejects 'disinformation' amid allegations by some Israelis of voting interference.

articles.headline: Laurus Labs reports surging quarterly revenue and profit
articles.title: Laurus Labs Q2 net profit surges on 33% rise in revenue
articles.summary: Indian pharmaceutical firm Laurus Labs announced a consolidated net profit increase to 436.74 crore rupees for the September quarter, driven by a 33 percent revenue growth. Founder and CEO Satyanarayana Chava attributed the financial performance to strong operations in contract development, manufacturing, and affordable medicines. The company also declared an interim dividend.
articles.description: Laurus is executing a transformation strategy and operationalised its first commercial scale peptide plant in Visakhapatnam to address surging demand for peptide therapeutics.

articles.headline: Spanish athlete Julieta Gallego killed in train collision
articles.title: Spanish long jumper Julieta Gallego among victims of deadly train collision
articles.summary: The Royal Spanish Athletics Federation confirmed that 24-year-old long jumper Julieta Gallego was among at least 68 people killed in a high-speed train collision in Spain’s Toledo province. The tragic crash occurred when two trains collided on the Madrid-Andalusia line, injuring approximately 80 people and prompting widespread mourning across the national sports community.
articles.description: Julieta Gallego, who competed for Madrid-based AD Sprint, among those killed in train crash in Spain.

articles.headline: Defeated presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro calls himself Brazilian leader
articles.title: Flávio Bolsonaro calls himself 'leader of Brazil' after election loss
articles.summary: Following his election defeat to Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, defeated candidate Flávio Bolsonaro declared himself the leader of Brazil in a social media letter after leaving the country for the United States. Bolsonaro alleged electoral fraud without providing evidence, having previously defied a Supreme Court order to surrender his passports amid a money laundering investigation.
articles.description: The defeated presidential candidate says he will lead the opposition from the US.

articles.headline: Pixxel launches U.S. subsidiary to serve federal defence and intelligence agencies
articles.title: Bengaluru firm Pixxel sets up Pixxel Federal to serve U.S. defence, intelligence agencies
articles.summary: Planetary infrastructure company Pixxel has established Pixxel Federal in the United States to deliver Earth observation technologies, satellite mission systems, and geospatial intelligence to civilian, defence, and intelligence agencies. The new subsidiary will operate an office in the Washington, D.C., area, drawing on a $100 million Series C funding round to expand international operations and manufacturing capabilities.

articles.headline: Private corruption complaints do not require prior approval, says judge
articles.title: Prior approval not required for private complaints against corruption, says judge
articles.summary: Private complaints can be filed against public servants without prior approval under Section 17A of the Prevention of Corruption Act based on a Supreme Court ruling, according to Principal District and Sessions Judge N.V. Vijay. Speaking at the inauguration of Vigilance Awareness Week 2026 in Dharwad, officials emphasised that integrity, stronger administrative systems, and online services are essential for public trust and service delivery.
articles.description: Such complaints can be filed against public servants without prior approval under Section 17A of the Prevention of Corruption Act

articles.headline: New York Times tests artificial intelligence recipe modification feature in cooking app
articles.title: The NYT Cooking app is testing AI recipe modifications
articles.summary: The New York Times is testing an artificial intelligence feature for its Cooking app on iOS that recommends ingredient substitutions, suggests equipment alternatives, and scales servings. While the optional tool has sparked user concerns regarding environmental impact and user experience, app editors state that the feature allows cooks to customize recipes according to their immediate needs.
articles.description: The New York Times is testing a new AI feature for its Cooking app that helps users to modify recipes, and it has sparked some drama among users. Last Friday, NYT Cooking senior editor Genevieve Ko announced the feature, which can be used to recommend substitutions for ingredients and cooking equipment, scale recipes to any […]

articles.headline: DVAC conducts searches at properties linked to former DMK MLA and industrialist
articles.title: DVAC searches places linked to former DMK MLA, industrialist Sekar Reddy in Vellore
articles.summary: Sleuths from the Directorate of Vigilance and Anti-Corruption conducted searches at properties in Katpadi linked to former Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam Member of Legislative Assembly A.P. Nandakumar and industrialist J. Sekar Reddy. According to investigators, the operations form part of an ongoing probe into 25 locations across Tamil Nadu regarding an alleged cash-for-jobs scam within the Municipal Administration and Water Supply Department.
articles.description: The searches are part of the ongoing probe at 25 locations across Tamil Nadu linked to former Minister and DMK leader K.N. Nehru in connection with an alleged ₹634-crore cash-for-jobs scam

articles.headline: Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu's bloc applies pressure on Arab parties amid inconclusive election
articles.title: Israel piles pressure on Arab parties as Netanyahu seeks government
articles.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc has pressured Arab party leaders over unproven allegations of foreign funding following an inconclusive election where neither major camp secured a majority. Supreme Court Justice Noam Sohlberg requested a security service investigation into claims that the Raam party received Qatari funds, while Arab leaders and opponents strongly rejected the accusations as a political delegitimisation campaign.
articles.description: Israeli President Isaac Herzog called for an investigation into allegations of fraud but cautioned against stigmatising the entire Arab Israeli community, who voted at unprecedented rates

articles.headline: US farmers scale back crop acreage amid rising production costs and elections
articles.title: As US midterms approach, farmers decide what to plant and how to vote
articles.summary: American agricultural producers are reducing planting areas for crops like rice and shifting to cheaper alternatives due to soaring fuel and fertiliser expenses following the war on Iran. According to university experts, these elevated input costs have strained farm budgets nationwide, compounding financial pressures during the October 2026 midterm elections.
articles.description: In Arkansas, rising costs spurred farmer Hallie Shoffner’s long-shot Senate campaign. Will farmers back her?

articles.headline: Adani Airports and IHCL partner to develop eight airport hotels
articles.title: Adani Airports, IHCL plan 8 hotels with 2,000+ rooms across four cities, expanding airport-led hospitality hubs
articles.summary: Adani Airport Holdings Ltd and Indian Hotels Company Ltd signed agreements on October 29, 2026, to construct eight hotels featuring over two thousand rooms across Mumbai, Ahmedabad, Lucknow, and Guwahati. The airport-centric hospitality hubs aim to boost regional commerce and tourism, with Adani handling development and IHCL operating the properties under brands like Taj and Ginger.
articles.description: Airport-centric developments were emerging as important commercial and hospitality hubs as India strengthened its position as one of the world’s fastest-growing aviation markets.

articles.headline: India offers counter-terrorism expertise and maritime cooperation to ASEAN nations
articles.title: India ready to share battle-tested counter-terrorism expertise with ASEAN partners: Rajnath
articles.summary: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh announced on October 29, 2026, that India is prepared to share its battle-tested counter-terrorism expertise with ASEAN partners through joint exercises and intelligence sharing. Speaking in Cebu during the thirteenth ADMM-Plus meeting, Singh also proposed a new youth bridge to strengthen institutional connectivity and highlighted ongoing maritime security efforts in the Indo-Pacific.
articles.description: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh told the 13th ADMM-Plus in Cebu that India would share its operational experience through joint exercises, capacity-building programmes and intelligence sharing, and proposed a dedicated defence ‘Youth Bridge’ with ASEAN countries

articles.headline: Bangladesh tribunal sentences absent Awami League official to death for killings
articles.title: Bangladesh's tribunal sentences Awami League leader to death
articles.summary: A special tribunal in Bangladesh sentenced Awami League leader Mahbubul Alam Hanif to death in absentia on October 29, 2026, for six murders committed during the July Uprising. Three other local party members received life sentences while absconding, drawing criticism from international rights groups regarding trial fairness following the 2024 ouster of Sheikh Hasina.
articles.description: A three-member tribunal led by Justice Nozrul Islam Chowdhury and comprising Justices Md. Manjurul Bashid and Nur Mohammad Shahriar Kabir delivered the verdict

articles.headline: Damascus and Amman dispute responsibility over deadly Jordanian airstrikes in Syria
articles.title: Damascus, Amman contradict each other on attack that killed civilians
articles.summary: Public anger has risen in Syria following Jordanian airstrikes on Deraa and Suwayda that killed several civilians, including a grandmother and her three grandchildren. While Jordan stated the raids targeted Islamic State fighters in response to a church attack, the Syrian Ministry of Foreign Affairs asserted that the military operation occurred without prior coordination.
articles.description: Analysts say accountability is needed to quell public outrage over killing of family in southern Syria.

articles.headline: Indonesians share impact of haze on their livelihoods
articles.title: Indonesians share impact of haze on their livelihoods
articles.description: Months of forest fires and toxic haze in Indonesia has severely disrupted daily life.

articles.headline: Anthropic faces massive financial commitments and intense competition detailed in S-1 filing
articles.title: Anthropic’s business plan: Build God or die trying
articles.summary: Artificial intelligence company Anthropic faces roughly one trillion dollars in long-term compute and infrastructure commitments over the next twenty years, according to financial documents. To sustain its operations and cover massive fixed costs, the firm relies on enterprise software sales and rapid revenue growth. Analysts warn that aggressive expansion is mandatory to prevent bankruptcy amidst fierce competition from industry rivals.
articles.description: The Anthropic S-1 seems to have provided the financial justification for the company to spend as much as it possibly can on compute. If you are the kind of person who wonders if Anthropic is doing its level best to build a machine god while convincing Wall Street it's in the business of selling IT […]

articles.headline: Animal experiments, what the new draft rules allow and what they mean for research | Explained
articles.title: Animal experiments, what the new draft rules allow and what they mean for research | Explained
