articles.title: The megadonors financing the US midterms to influence policy
articles.description: Who are the groups funding the US midterm campaigns and what are they hoping to influence?

articles.headline: Sensex surges 905 points as banking and FMCG shares rally on Thursday
articles.title: Stock markets rebound over 1% on Fed pause, but rupee and crude keep investors on edge
articles.summary: Indian stock markets rallied more than one percent on Thursday, driven by heavy buying in banking and Fast Moving Consumer Goods shares alongside easing global crude oil prices. The 30-share BSE Sensex jumped 905.01 points to close at 74,151.04, while the NSE Nifty settled higher at 22,936.75. Brent crude fell 1.18 percent to $113.96 per barrel, according to exchange data released on October 29, 2026.
articles.description: While Thursday’s rebound offered some relief to investors, the combination of elevated U.S. interest rates, foreign fund outflows and expensive crude oil continues to cloud the outlook for Indian markets.

articles.headline: Kerala Health Minister orders medical board probe into expired Remdesivir usage
articles.title: Expired drugs possibly given to Nipah patients, says Keralam Health Minister
articles.summary: A medical board will investigate whether expired Remdesivir antiviral drugs were administered to Nipah patients and caused fatalities in the Indian state. Health Minister K. Muraleedharan announced the inquiry in the Keralam Assembly on Thursday, following submissions from lawmakers. The board will be headed by Aravind R., the head of the Infectious Diseases department at Government Medical College Hospital in Thiruvananthapuram.
articles.description: K. Muraleedharan says medical board will probe whether use of expired Remdesivir led to deaths of Nipah patients

articles.headline: Tamil Nadu prisons director-general transferred following high-profile jailbreak
articles.title: Days after Theni jailbreak, Tamil Nadu Prisons DGP Sandeep Rai Rathore transferred
articles.summary: The Tamil Nadu government transferred Director-General of Police for Prisons Sandeep Rai Rathore on Thursday following a jailbreak in Theni district. Seventeen remand prisoners escaped on Monday night from the Thekkampatti sub-jail after overpowering guards, though all escapees were recaptured by Wednesday. K. Shankar has been appointed as the new Additional Director-General of Police for Prisons and Correctional Services following the incident.
articles.description: 17 remand prisoners who were lodged at the Thekkampatti sub-jail near Andipatti in Theni district escaped on October 26 and were later recaptured by special teams over the next two days.

articles.headline: Afghan farmers pushed to opium farming to make a living
articles.title: Afghan farmers pushed to opium farming to make a living
articles.description: Farmers in Afghanistan say they're being pushed into poppy seed cultivation to make a living despite a ban.

articles.headline: Legislative Council election results do not reflect general popular support
articles.title: What the MLC elections do and do not tell us
articles.summary: Recent Legislative Council elections across several Indian states do not accurately measure popular support for political parties. According to reports published on October 29, 2026, the electorate in these contests represents only a fraction of voters compared to general Assembly elections. Uttar Pradesh recorded 11 constituencies voting, Bihar had eight, Maharashtra saw five, and Karnataka held polls in four constituencies.
articles.description: MLC elections are held for the Legislative Council, the Upper House of a State legislature, which exists in only six of the 28 States — Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Maharashtra, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh and Telangana

articles.headline: Ethiopia acquires Russian fighter jets and air defence systems
articles.title: Why is Russia sending fighter jets and air defences to Ethiopia?
articles.summary: Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed announced the acquisition of 12 Su-35 fighter jets and four S-400 batteries during the Russia-Africa Summit. Analysts noted the agreement strengthens bilateral military cooperation amid domestic conflicts in Tigray. Russian President Vladimir Putin highlighted expanding trade figures as both nations seek to deepen strategic ties.
articles.description: Experts say Moscow is seeking arms revenue and further diplomatic influence.

articles.headline: Pope Leo visits Argentina amid clergy abuse scrutiny
articles.title: Pope Leo’s Argentina visit brings renewed scrutiny of clergy abuse scandals
articles.summary: The papal visit to Argentina brings renewed attention to sexual abuse allegations involving Catholic clergy and lay members. Survivors have demanded harsher Vatican penalties, including the removal of clerical status for convicted priests. Demonstrators and victims expressed mixed reactions regarding ongoing investigations into church officials and institutions across the country.
articles.description: Victims have expressed frustration over the Vatican’s silence on church proceedings involving priests convicted in criminal courts

articles.headline: Cyclone Arnab disrupts rail services as bridge in Andhra Pradesh is inundated
articles.title: Cyclone Arnab: Railway bridge near Andhra’s Ichchapuram inundated; trains cancelled, diverted
articles.summary: Train operations in the Visakhapatnam Division faced severe disruptions on October 29, 2026, following heavy water inundation at Bridge No. 1052 between Ichchapuram and Jhadupudi. According to South Coast Railway officials, overflowing local rivulets forced authorities to cancel, divert, or short-terminate multiple passenger and express services. Special trains and helpline desks were established at major stations to assist stranded travelers.
articles.description: A special train will run between Visakhapatnam and Palasa for stranded passengers

articles.headline: Former West Bengal minister Indranil Sen arrested over Durga Puja scam
articles.title: Former West Bengal minister Indranil Sen arrested in Durga Puja ticket scam
articles.summary: Kolkata Police arrested former West Bengal minister Indranil Sen on Wednesday evening in connection with a Durga Puja ticket scam involving the organisation MassArt. The arrest followed questioning by the Enforcement Directorate at the CGO Complex in Salt Lake. Investigators allege the accused falsely represented the organisation as sponsored by UNESCO to collect funds between 2022 and 2025.
articles.description: He faces allegations of financial irregularities and had been reportedly avoiding the police for a while

articles.headline: King Charles on Caribbean tour as calls grow for slavery reparations
articles.title: King Charles on Caribbean tour as calls grow for slavery reparations
articles.description: UK’s King Charles joined a Junkanoo street parade during a visit to the Bahamas ahead of the Commonwealth summit.

articles.headline: Court sentences three individuals to life imprisonment for cow slaughter
articles.title: Trio gets life sentence for cow slaughter in Gujarat, court cites Manusmriti on cow’s significance
articles.summary: An additional sessions judge in Gandhinagar sentenced three men to life imprisonment and imposed a fine of three lakh rupees following the seizure of 277 kilograms of beef. Gujarat Deputy Chief Minister Harsh Sanghavi praised the verdict under the state preservation act. The prosecution presented testimony from fifty-four witnesses during the trial.
articles.description: Through a 2017 amendment to the Gujarat Animal Preservation Act, 1954, the Gujarat government had enhanced punishment for those found guilty of cow slaughter to life imprisonment, making it the first State in the country to make cow slaughter punishable with such a sentence.

articles.headline: South Africa names Durban as preferred candidate to host 2036 or 2040 Olympics
articles.title: Olympic Games: South Africa bids to make Durban host city for 2036 or 2040
articles.summary: South Africa selected its third-biggest city, Durban, as the preferred candidate to host the Summer Olympics and Paralympics in 2036 or 2040, aiming to become the first African nation to stage the Games. According to the South African Sports Confederation, Olympic and Paralympic Committee on Thursday, the bid will center on the Moses Mabhida Stadium. The International Olympic Committee set an October deadline for declarations.
articles.description: South Africa names Durban as host city for its 2036 and 2040 bids to bring the Olympics to Africa for the first time.

articles.headline: Israel parliamentary election produces no clear winner as major blocs fall short
articles.title: Israel’s election rhetoric: What candidates said, and how they performed
articles.summary: Israel’s parliamentary election on Tuesday concluded without a clear winner, leaving both major political blocs short of the 61 seats required to form a government. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s bloc is on course to win 53 seats in the 120-member Knesset, while the opposition bloc led by Gadi Eisenkot is expected to secure 48 seats. Meanwhile, Arab-majority parties secured a historic high of 19 seats amid high turnout.
articles.description: From Netanyahu to Ben-Gvir, campaign boasts and attacks on Arab parties have been met with a deadlocked result.

articles.headline: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham could visit India soon, envoy says
articles.title: U.K. PM Andy Burnham’s trip to India could take place soon: British Envoy
articles.summary: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham is keen to visit India soon, according to Acting British High Commissioner to India Ben Mellor. Speaking on October 29, 2026, the diplomat expressed confidence that bilateral trade targets would be surpassed following the free trade agreement. The visit aims to strengthen economic ties and investments between the two nations.
articles.description: India and the U.K. are aiming to double bilateral trade to around $120 billion by 2030

articles.headline: Jamia Millia Islamia students continue protests demanding union elections
articles.title: Protest at India university where no students’ union vote held for 20 years
articles.summary: Students at Jamia Millia Islamia in New Delhi continued demonstrations on October 29, 2026, demanding the restoration of their elected union after twenty years of suspension. Law student Ebin Basil led a prolonged hunger strike. The university administration set a December 20 deadline for a draft constitution, but protesters rejected the timeline as vague while facing campus closures and heavy security deployments.
articles.description: Jamia Millia Islamia campus in Indian capital has seen weeks of protests, with several students holding a hunger strike.

articles.headline: Can the UK afford more help with the cost of living?
articles.title: Can the UK afford more help with the cost of living?
articles.description: Labour party aims to help households and sustain growth as inflation and debt costs limit its options.

articles.headline: Americans highlight economy and immigration as top concerns in midterm elections
articles.title: Voter voices: Which issues matter most to Americans?
articles.summary: As part of the British Broadcasting Corporation Voter Voices series, residents across the United States discussed their primary concerns ahead of the midterm elections. While polls indicate the economy remains the principal priority, citizens also emphasized law and order, healthcare, and immigration, alongside ideological fears. These interviews provide insight into the domestic issues influencing American voters this year.
articles.description: As part of our Voter Voices series, the BBC asked Americans across the country what issue will influence how they vote.

articles.headline: Mother feeding practices significantly influence children reluctance to try new foods
articles.title: Mother’s feeding practices may influence children’s reluctance to try new foods: NIN study
articles.summary: A new study by researchers at the ICMR National Institute of Nutrition examined food neophobia among children aged two to seven in Hyderabad. Findings published in the Journal of Nutritional Science revealed that seventy seven percent of children showed moderate reluctance. The research underscores the need for improved nutrition counselling by caregivers to enhance dietary variety during early childhood.
articles.description: Food neophobia among children can limit dietary variety and potentially affect nutritional health during crucial years of growth

articles.headline: Public interest litigation challenges India transgender document change regulatory regime
articles.title: Document change regime developed following NALSA ‘grossly discriminatory’ against ‘biological females’: PIL
articles.summary: The India chapter of Women Declaration International filed a public interest litigation in the Supreme Court arguing that India transgender document framework is discriminatory against biological females. A Bench led by Chief Justice Surya Kant issued notices to three Union ministries on October 28, 2026. The petition challenges parts of the Transgender Persons Act and standard operating procedures for Aadhaar cards.
articles.description: The India chapter of the UK-based trust seeks to overrule the NALSA judgment that laid down that legal recognition of gender identity was part of the Constitutional right to dignity and freedom

articles.headline: Stalin urges President Murmu to act against Chief Election Commissioner
articles.title: Stalin urges President Murmu to initiate action against Gyanesh Kumar
articles.summary: Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam president M.K. Stalin petitioned President Droupadi Murmu to initiate parliamentary action against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. He alleged that the unauthorized deletion of millions of electors from Tamil Nadu voter rolls during a 2025 revision distorted electoral outcomes, and requested the suspension of the disputed rolls for future polls.

articles.headline: NTK member Saattai Duraimurugan seeks anticipatory bail in Madras High Court
articles.title: NTK’s ‘Saattai’ Duraimurugan moves Madras High Court seeking anticipatory bail
articles.summary: Naam Tamilar Katchi office-bearer A. Duraimurugan approached the Madras High Court seeking anticipatory bail regarding a Chennai cyber crime case. The First Information Report stems from a complaint lodged on October third by Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam cadre A. Christopher over a YouTube video containing remarks against Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay. The petitioner argued the allegations are politically motivated and intended to curb freedom of speech.
articles.description: An FIR had been registered against him for his alleged derogatory YouTube video against Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay and Minister Aadhav Arjuna

articles.headline: Hong Kong housing secretary resigns following deadly fire investigation
articles.title: Hong Kong's Housing Minister resigns after fire investigation finds inadequate oversight
articles.summary: Hong Kong leader John Lee announced that Housing Secretary Winnie Ho resigned after an independent committee found regulatory oversight failures related to a deadly apartment fire last November that killed 168 people. Mr. Lee and top officials issued a public apology, while separate criminal investigations involving manslaughter charges continue against seven individuals and two companies.
articles.description: During the investigation, an independent committee found that the Housing Bureau's independent checking unit failed in its duties supervising the maintenance work

articles.headline: Tamil Nadu police recapture seventeen escaped prisoners after manhunt
articles.title: Audacious Indian jailbreak saga ends with 17 prisoners recaptured
articles.summary: Police in India's Tamil Nadu state recaptured 17 undertrial prisoners who staged an audacious jailbreak from a Theni district facility on October 26, 2026. Following a 36-hour manhunt involving drone surveillance and police forces, authorities suspended nine staff members amid concerns over severe prison overcrowding and a breach of security protocols.
articles.description: The jailbreak began with a fake seizure and ended 36 hours later with all the inmates back behind bars.

articles.headline: Brazilians split over Flavio Bolsonaro’s exit to US
articles.title: Brazilians split over Flavio Bolsonaro’s exit to US
articles.description: Brazilians are split over Flavio Bolsonaro fleeing to the US after refusing to concede the election to President Lula.

articles.headline: Report alleges North Korean forced labour recruitment network in Russia
articles.title: North Koreans being recruited into forced labour in Russia, report says
articles.summary: An international law foundation report released on October 29, 2026, revealed that a broker network operated by Russian businessman Vladimir Sokolov uses bogus student enrolments to funnel North Korean workers into forced labour in Russia. The scheme allegedly bypasses United Nations sanctions to fund Pyongyang's missile development and support Russia's military-industrial complex.
articles.description: Russian broker network recruiting North Korean labourers using student visas, Global Rights Compliance report says.

articles.headline: GameDev Outlook report highlights capital barriers for Indian developers
articles.title: GDAI launches India gaming report, highlights need for stronger funding
articles.summary: Approximately seventy-five percent of game developers in India identify capital and publishing investment as major growth barriers, according to a new report launched by the Game Developer Association of India in Chennai. Developed alongside PhonePe Appstore and The Dialogue, the study notes that while India generated over one billion dollars in revenue, monetization potential remains limited relative to the vast player base.
articles.description: The report — developed in partnership with PhonePe Appstore and research partner The Dialogue — examines the structural challenges facing Indian game developers and identifies priorities for building globally competitive studios

articles.headline: New low-pressure area forms in Andaman Sea following Cyclone Arnab
articles.title: Low pressure forms in Andaman Sea after Cyclone Arnab, may affect Andhra Pradesh
articles.summary: A fresh low-pressure system has formed over the south Andaman Sea under the influence of a cyclonic circulation just a day after Cyclone Arnab crossed the coast of Andhra Pradesh. According to the India Meteorological Department, the system is expected to move west-northwestward and intensify into a depression by October 31, potentially bringing heavy rainfall to Andhra Pradesh as local body elections approach.
articles.description: The system is likely to intensify into a depression by October 31, the IMD says

articles.headline: Kerala leaders criticize airlines for steep airfare hikes during festival seasons
articles.title: Airfare hikes: Keralam CM and Opposition Leader slam airlines for ‘fleecing’ NRKs
articles.summary: Lawmakers in the Kerala Legislative Assembly strongly condemned airlines for sharply increasing ticket prices during festival seasons, particularly on routes connecting the state to West Asia. Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan and opposition leader Pinarayi Vijayan criticized the financial burden placed on non-resident Keralites, noting that state leaders have repeatedly urged the Union government to implement fare caps.
articles.description: In Assembly, V.D. Satheesan and Pinarayi Vijayan point out that successive governments in the State have raised the matter with the Centre. Opposition stages walkout over alleged denial of NRK benefits, dissolution of Loka Kerala Sabha

articles.headline: Are Texans divided over Republican and Democrat candidates?
articles.title: Are Texans divided over Republican and Democrat candidates?
articles.description: Al Jazeera’s Emma Withrow asks Texans what matters most to them ahead of the US midterm elections.

articles.headline: VHP accuses Opposition of targeting Hindu festivals with November 1 rally
articles.title: ‘Desist from targeting Hindu festivals, economy’: VHP to Opposition over November 1 rally
articles.summary: The Vishva Hindu Parishad accused the Congress and other Opposition parties on October 27, 2026, of conspiring to damage the economy and disrupt Hindu festivals through their planned November 1 rally at Ramlila Maidan in New Delhi. National spokesperson Vinod Bansal stated that leaders rejected traders requests to postpone the event, which coincides with the Ahoi Ashtami fast, ignoring concerns over security and business disruptions.
articles.description: The remarks came a day after traders held a protest at Kashmere Gate in New Delhi, demanding that Congress defer the November 1 rally until after Diwali.

articles.headline: European Union drops associate membership term for Canada in draft statement
articles.title: European Union backtracks on Canada becoming ‘associate member’
articles.summary: The European Union removed references to associate membership for Canada in a joint draft statement ahead of the summit in Montreal hosted by Prime Minister Mark Carney on Thursday. European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen initially proposed the status in September, but pushback from German Chancellor Friedrich Merz and other leaders led negotiators to adopt phrasing calling for an ever closer association.
articles.description: Several European leaders reportedly pushed for the term to be removed from a joint draft Canada-EU statement.

articles.headline: Delhi traders seek postponement of INDIA bloc rally over festive season disruption
articles.title: Delhi traders flag potential impact on 21 markets from INDIA bloc’s November 1 rally, seek postponement
articles.summary: The Chamber of Trade and Industry warned on October 27, 2026, that the proposed Congress-led INDIA bloc rally at Ramlila Maidan on November 1 could paralyze business across 21 major markets in Delhi. The traders body urged party leaders Rahul Gandhi and Mallikarjun Kharge to postpone the event or shift it away from commercial hubs, citing potential traffic gridlock from thousands of vehicles and estimated losses of up to 10000 crore rupees.
articles.description: It projected that the November 1 rally could bring commercial activity across Old Delhi to a standstill, resulting in losses of up to ₹10,000 crore

articles.headline: Railway authorities cancel 64 train services due to approaching Cyclone Arnab
articles.title: Cyclone ‘Arnab’: 64 train services cancelled on October 27 and 28
articles.summary: Railway authorities cancelled 64 train services scheduled for October 27 and 28, 2026, as a precautionary measure against Cyclone Arnab along the Andhra Pradesh coast. The cancellations comprise 53 regional passenger routes and 11 express services connecting Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, and Odisha. Officials advised passengers to verify train operational statuses through official channels before traveling.
articles.description: Long-distance express trains connecting Telangana with coastal Andhra Pradesh and Odisha among those affected; passengers advised to check status before travel

articles.headline: Delhi Police grants no-objection for INDIA bloc rally on November 1
articles.title: INDIA bloc’s Nov. 1 rally: Delhi Police grants permission with strict conditions; denies mock impeachment request
articles.summary: The Delhi Police confirmed that a no-objection certificate was issued for the opposition INDIA bloc to hold a demonstration at Ramlila Maidan on November 1, 2026. According to Deputy Commissioner of Police Rohit Rajbir Singh, authorities imposed strict security and logistical requirements while stating that no formal application had been filed for a separate mock public impeachment event.
articles.description: Police say no separate request was received for the proposed mock impeachment on October 30 and November 1

articles.headline: Telangana electoral rolls face high rejection and deletion rates during revision
articles.title: Telangana SIR: Form-6 rejections and Form-7 deletions unusually high during pre-SIR period
articles.summary: According to the office of the Chief Electoral Officer, Telangana recorded unusually high rejection and deletion rates during the Special Intensive Revision of Electoral Rolls. Out of total applications processed across 119 constituencies, authorities rejected close to 27 percent of Form-6 applications, while millions of voter names were deleted using Form-7, creating significant exclusions in the final voter rolls.
articles.description: The number of rejections constitutes close to 27% of the total Form-6 applications processed during Pre-SIR and SIR phases, which is very high

articles.headline: Russia seeks political influence and economic ties at Africa summit
articles.title: ‘Economic incentives are limited’: What does Russia really offer Africa?
articles.summary: Delegations from forty-eight countries gathered in Moscow for the Russia-Africa Summit to discuss bilateral cooperation amid ongoing international sanctions. Analysts noted that while Moscow offers limited financial investments compared to other global powers, the diplomatic engagements provide vital political backing for military regimes in the Sahel region.
articles.description: African nations weigh political incentives as Moscow offers limited economic benefits compared with China and the West.

articles.headline: Prime Minister Narendra Modi questions Congress over MLC election results
articles.title: PM questions Congress over party’s MLC election results
articles.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi criticised the Congress party on Wednesday for failing to win any seats in Member of Legislative Council elections held using ballot papers across Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra, Bihar and Karnataka. While results in several states showed victories for the Bharatiya Janata Party and regional entities, BJP leaders claimed the outcome highlights a severe lack of public support for the opposition.
articles.description: ‘MLC elections in 28 seats across four big States — Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra, Bihar and Karnataka. Elections held using ballot papers. Guess how many seats Congress won? said Narendra Modi in a post on X

articles.headline: Congress slams Prime Minister Narendra Modi over Varanasi MLC election losses
articles.title: Stop sermonising others; introspect why BJP lost Varanasi seats in MLC polls: Congress slams PM
articles.summary: The Congress party criticized Prime Minister Narendra Modi on October 29, 2026, telling him to stop sermonizing after the Bharatiya Janata Party lost both seats in his Varanasi constituency during Legislative Council elections. Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh stated that citizens across multiple cities have delivered a clear verdict against government policies.
articles.description: Jairam Ramesh said that from Varanasi and Nagpur to Lucknow, Prayagraj, and Patna, the people have clearly passed a "no-confidence motion against" the PM's policies

articles.headline: Microsoft introduces voluntary exit offers as artificial intelligence business expands
articles.title: Job cuts, retirement plan, voluntary exits: What’s going on at Microsoft?
articles.summary: Technology corporation Microsoft launched a voluntary exit programme providing financial and career support to eligible personnel across several countries. Chief People Officer Amy Coleman indicated the measure accompanies ongoing internal reorganisations, as the enterprise increases capital expenditures toward cloud computing and artificial intelligence infrastructure.
articles.description: Microsoft’s recent workforce moves come amid strong financial growth and rising investments in AI infrastructure

articles.headline: Medical specialists highlight importance of prompt stroke treatment
articles.title: Experts in stroke medicine emphasise on timely treatment
articles.summary: Medical professionals speaking during a webinar organised by Kauvery Hospital for World Stroke Day emphasised the necessity of medical intervention within a four-and-a-half-hour window. Experts discussed rising annual incidence rates, common neurological symptoms, and the utilization of telemedicine services to transfer patients from remote areas to specialized medical facilities.
articles.description: The doctors discussed lifestyle-related risks, including poor dietary habits, physical inactivity, and inadequate sleep

articles.headline: Kerala high court prevents arrest of judge involved in car crash
articles.title: Cheranalloor luxury car crash: Kerala HC directs police not to arrest accused judge until further orders
articles.summary: The Kerala High Court on October 29, 2026, ordered police not to arrest an additional district judge whose teenage son drove a luxury car involved in a fatal accident. The judge was directed to cooperate with the investigation while the victim family joined the anticipatory bail proceedings. The crash occurred at Maraparambu on Container Road in Cheranalloor.
articles.description: Justice Kauser Edappagath orally remarks that court ‘cannot succumb to public opinion’. Court allows family members of the accident victim, Jayabalakrishnan, to be impleaded in anticipatory bail petition filed by the judicial officer

articles.headline: Jharkhand experiences heavy rainfall as cyclone Arnab impacts region
articles.title: Cyclone Arnab effect: Rain intensifies in parts of Jharkhand, to continue till October 30
articles.summary: Heavy rainfall intensified across Jharkhand on October 29, 2026, driven by the severe cyclonic storm Arnab that previously made landfall along the Andhra Pradesh coast. The Ranchi Meteorological Centre reported significant precipitation, prompting orange and yellow alerts for multiple districts through October 30. Several regional administrations had already ordered school closures on October 28 and 29.
articles.description: An ‘Orange’ alert of heavy rainfall has been issued for Garhwa, Palamu, Latehar, Lohardaga, Gumla and Simdega till 8.30 a.m. on October 30

articles.headline: North Andhra rivers swell and flood border areas following cyclone Arnab
articles.title: Rivers in spate in north Andhra after Cyclone Arnab; flood water enters Ichchapuram
articles.summary: Major rivers in north Andhra districts received heavy inflows on October 29, 2026, following cyclone Arnab, causing floods in Ichchapuram and surrounding border areas. Srikakulam and Vizianagaram recorded exceptionally high rainfall, disrupting traffic on National Highway 16 and prompting relief deployments by state authorities and the Indian Red Cross Society.
articles.description: A junior lineman dies after falling from an electric pole during repairs in Vizianagaram district

articles.headline: New studies reveal heavy research bias toward vertebrates in ecological literature
articles.title: Taxonomic ‘chauvinism’ rife in ecological literature
articles.summary: Research from the University of New South Wales analyzing over 1.3 million scientific papers found that vertebrates dominate conservation and ecology literature despite representing a tiny fraction of animal biodiversity. Scientists warn that this taxonomic chauvinism neglects invertebrates, skews funding, and potentially hampers innovations in medicine and engineering.
articles.description: For instance, even though birds and mammals comprise less than 1 per cent of animal biodiversity, they dominate both conservation and research efforts, find two studies.

articles.headline: Researchers in Keralam study potential links between gut bacteria and Parkinson's disease
articles.title: Study in Keralam sheds light on link between gut bacteria, Parkinson’s disease
articles.summary: Scientists at Cochin University of Science and Technology and the Sree Chitra Tirunal Institute for Medical Sciences and Technology published findings revealing distinct gut bacteria differences in Parkinson's disease patients. Funded by the Indian Council of Medical Research, the study analyzed stool samples from 65 patients and 65 healthy individuals using metagenomic sequencing to explore early diagnostic tests and treatments.
articles.description: Researchers from CUSAT and SCTIMST, Thiruvananthapuram, find significant differences between gut bacteria of Parkinson’s patients and those of healthy individuals

articles.headline: Israel faces political standoff following national elections without outright majority
articles.title: Israel elections: Understanding how Knesset polls work vs India’s system
articles.summary: Israel entered a political standoff following the October 27 national election after exit polls showed Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and rival Gadi Eisenkot locked in a tight race. Neither camp secured an outright majority in the 120-seat Knesset, requiring coalition negotiations. President Isaac Herzog will consult parliamentary factions to assign a lawmaker the task of forming a government.
articles.description: Israel’s political clash after the October 27 national vote pits Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu against former military chief Gadi Eisenkot in a neck-and-neck fight to form a government, as neither major bloc won a 61-seat majority in the 120-seat Knesset

articles.headline: Former US officials urge 2028 candidates to reject Biden Gaza policy
articles.title: Former US officials call on 2028 candidates to denounce Biden’s Gaza policy
articles.summary: Twelve former United States officials who resigned from the Joe Biden administration published a joint statement on Wednesday urging 2028 presidential candidates to pledge against hiring individuals responsible for enabling Israel military actions in Gaza. The signatories argued that those officials helped facilitate violations of domestic and international law during the ongoing war.
articles.description: Biden-era officials who quit over Gaza urge Democratic candidates for next presidential race to denounce the policy.

articles.headline: El Salvador deploys soldiers to Haiti as electoral timeline faces delay
articles.title: El Salvador pledges more than 2,000 soldiers as Haiti delays elections
articles.summary: El Salvador announced the deployment of over 2,000 soldiers to Haiti to combat armed gangs and search for four missing aviation technicians as Haitian electoral authorities postponed the first round of presidential and parliamentary voting to July 18, 2027. The security crisis and widespread gang violence have severely hampered voter registration and basic safety.
articles.description: El Salvador troops to support rescue mission to find four UN-backed soldiers who disappeared after ambush.

articles.headline: Two Indian nationals charged with election fraud in California
articles.title: Two Indian nationals among 28 charged with election fraud in California
articles.summary: The United States Department of Justice announced that two Indian nationals are among twenty-eight green card holders charged with election fraud in California. Amandeep Kaur and Kamlesh Shah face felony charges for fraudulently registering and voting in the November elections. Eleven defendants were arrested during raids across the state. The case involves noncitizens who unlawfully cast ballots during the general election.
articles.description: According to the Justice Department, Amandeep Kaur (30) and Kamlesh Shah (67) have been charged with fraudulently registering as voters and casting their ballots in the November 2024 U.S. elections

articles.headline: Opposition leaders urge West Bengal election commission to delay municipal polls
articles.title: Opposition leaders, activists urge SEC to delay Bengal civic polls till SSR to enrol voters is complete
articles.summary: Political figures and activists met State Election Commissioner Krishna Gupta to request a postponement of upcoming municipal elections until the Special Summary Revision finishes on January 4. The delegation highlighted that approximately 1.6 lakh Tribunal appellants are awaiting inclusion in Kolkata and Howrah, warning that holding the vote earlier would disenfranchise them.

articles.headline: Karnataka electoral rolls potentially miss over six million voters
articles.title: Karnataka SIR: 64.5 lakh voters potentially missing in rolls, majority of them young
articles.summary: Approximately sixty-four point five million electors are potentially missing from Karnataka's final electoral rolls following a Special Intensive Revision exercise released on October 27, 2026. Calculations based on the Chief Electoral Officer's data indicate that young adults aged eighteen to twenty-nine account for the majority of excluded voters. Economist Jean Dreze noted that the resulting elector-to-population ratio falls significantly below projected adult demographic estimates for the state.
articles.description: Elector-to-population ratio released officially by Karnataka CEO shows under-enrolment of about 64.5 lakh electors, of whom roughly 38.41 lakh are in the 18 to 29 age group.

articles.headline: Municipal Corporation issues water advisory for parts of Mumbai and Thane
articles.title: Boil, filter drinking water for seven days: BMC tells residents in parts of Mumbai, Thane and Bhiwandi
articles.summary: The Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation advised residents across multiple wards in Mumbai, Thane, and Bhiwandi to boil and filter drinking water for seven days. Issued on Tuesday, the precautionary directive follows water quality concerns arising from the recommissioning of a repaired reservoir at the Pise-Panjrapur supply complex, though no actual contamination has been officially confirmed by civic authorities.
articles.description: The BMC issued the warning over a possible impact on water quality following the recommissioning of a repaired reservoir at the Pise-Panjrapur water supply complex

articles.headline: Congress defeats BJP in Nagpur as opposition alliance leads Maharashtra polls
articles.title: Maharashtra MLC election: Congress trumps BJP in Nagpur, MVA leads 3-2 in State
articles.summary: The Indian National Congress defeated the Bharatiya Janata Party in Nagpur during the Maharashtra Legislative Council elections. Overall, the opposition Maha Vikas Aghadi alliance secured three of the five contested graduates and teachers constituencies, while the ruling Mahayuti alliance won two seats. Opposition leaders criticized Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis over the results and highlighted that the election was conducted using ballot papers.
articles.description: While the NCP SP called for going back to ballot papers for holding elections, the BJP called for introspection among the alliance partners

articles.headline: Artificial intelligence framework helps authenticate discovered painting resembling Rembrandt's work
articles.title: AI can help experts tell a real Rembrandt from a fake
articles.summary: A painting discovered in an attic in Maine sold for $1.41 million due to its resemblance to Rembrandt's work. An artificial intelligence framework developed by Carnegie Mellon University, combined with human expertise, determined with an 84.7 per cent confidence that the artwork was an original piece by the seventeenth-century Dutch master.
articles.description: A newly developed AI model aids art attribution, which traditionally takes a trained human eye and several tools, reports a new research paper.

articles.headline: El Salvador deploys troops to Haiti to rescue missing soldiers
articles.title: El Salvador sends 2,000 troops to Haiti to rescue four missing soldiers
articles.summary: The government of El Salvador deployed over two thousand soldiers to Haiti following the disappearance of four air force technicians. President Nayib Bukele communicated the deployment to Prime Minister Alix Didier Fils-Aime. The missing personnel belong to a United Nations-backed anti-gang organisation and were ambushed in Croix-des-Bouquets. Salvadoran authorities rejected four bodies previously handed over by Haiti because the remains did not match the missing servicemen.
articles.description: The troops are trying to recover four military personnel who went missing in an ambush on the outskirts of the Haitian capital Port-au-Prince.

articles.headline: Abhishek Banerjee demands Supreme Court restore West Bengal elected government
articles.title: Restore previous elected govt in West Bengal, says TMC’s Abhishek Banerjee after SC’s SIR observations
articles.summary: Trinamool Congress parliamentarian Abhishek Banerjee questioned West Bengal electoral legitimacy on October 29, 2026. He urged the Supreme Court to reinstate the previous administration and order fresh elections within six months. The remarks followed a bench observation stating it has not adjudicated the legality of the Election Commission voter scrutiny category.
articles.description: The Supreme Court said it has not yet adjudicated the legality of the ECI’s use of the "logical discrepancy" category to scrutinise voters' details durins SIR

articles.headline: Pakistan minister invites Punjab chief minister to attend conference
articles.title: Pakistan minister invites Punjab CM Mann
articles.summary: Ramesh Singh Arora, Pakistan Punjab Minister for Minority Affairs, has formally invited Indian Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann and all Punjab Assembly legislators to visit Pakistan. The invitation follows Mr. Mann's expressed desire to attend an international Punjabi conference in Lahore and visit Sikh shrines. The Kartarpur corridor, which connects Dera Baba Nanak to Darbar Sahib Gurdwara, has remained closed since May 2025 due to bilateral tensions.
articles.description: Punjab CM Bhagwant Mann had said that he wished to accept the invitation from the organisers of the Lahore International Punjabi Conference in Lahore from November 27 to 29 and would want to visit Sikh shrines in Pakistan

articles.headline: Kiren Rijiju labels actor Naseeruddin Shah a dangerous urban dimagi naxal
articles.title: Extremely harmful to Indian democracy: Rijiju slams Naseeruddin Shah's 'dimagi naxal' video
articles.summary: Union Minister for Minority Affairs Kiren Rijiju condemned actor Naseeruddin Shah on October 29, 2026, calling his views harmful to democracy. Shah had released a video supporting protesting Jamia Millia Islamia students, accusing the central government of destroying the education system and identifying himself as a dimagi naxal.
articles.description: In a video posted on Facebook, a visibly angry Naseeruddin Shah came out in support of Jamia Millia Islamia students, who have been protesting for the restoration of the students' union, and called himself a "dimagi naxal"

articles.headline: Potential Democratic midterm victory could create complex diplomatic challenges for Europe
articles.title: Why a Democratic win in US midterms could adversely affect Europe
articles.summary: Analysts suggest a Democratic victory in the United States midterm elections could foster complacency regarding European far-right movements and pressure Ukraine into unfavourable peace deals with Russia. Polling indicates declining trust in the United States, with only 31 percent of Europeans viewing Washington as their most trustworthy ally, down from 51 percent in 2024 under President Joe Biden.
articles.description: Complacency about rising far-right movements and renewed pressure on Ukraine could be the result.

articles.headline: Liverpool and Manchester City advance in League Cup following penalty shootouts
articles.title: Carabao Cup: Liverpool beats Chelsea on penalties, Man City survives Brighton scare
articles.summary: Liverpool defeated Chelsea in a penalty shootout to reach the League Cup quarterfinals following a 1-1 draw at Anfield on Wednesday. Holders Manchester City also advanced after drawing 2-2 with Brighton and winning on penalties at the Etihad Stadium. In other matches, Bournemouth defeated Aston Villa 3-0, and Crystal Palace secured a 1-0 victory against Fulham.
articles.description: Liverpool to face Bournemouth in quarterfinals; Man City plays Bradford City

articles.headline: Turkiye offers maritime boundary agreement to Egypt amid improving bilateral ties
articles.title: Can Turkiye’s Libya breakthrough reshape Eastern Mediterranean diplomacy?
articles.summary: Turkiye renewed an offer to sign a maritime boundary agreement with Egypt on Wednesday, according to the Turkish Ministry of National Defence. The proposal follows a decision by Libya's eastern-based parliament in Tobruk to approve a 2019 maritime accord with Ankara. While the diplomatic outreach complicates Egypt's position and tests regional alignments, Turkish and Egyptian officials continue working to strengthen bilateral cooperation.
articles.description: Ankara wins backing from former adversaries in Libya for maritime border agreement, but other diplomatic tests remain.

articles.headline: Thane Police warn protesters against highway blockades during murder investigation demonstrations
articles.title: Thane Police warn of action over highway blockades amid Purnekar murder protests, say SIT probe on track
articles.summary: Thane Police announced warnings on Wednesday regarding illegal road blockades following violent protests over the murder of Pradeep Purnekar. Joint Commissioner Panjabrao Ugle stated that a 23-member Special Investigation Team has arrested five suspects and gathered forensic evidence while handling family allegations of political interference. Authorities urged residents to refrain from demonstrations that severely disrupt public movement.
articles.description: The protests, which continued overnight, followed allegations by Purnekar’s family that police had failed to act against former Thane mayor Meenakshi Shinde and her husband Rajendra Shinde despite evidence allegedly linking them to the murder conspiracy

articles.headline: Wageningen University researchers test salt marsh resilience against large artificial waves
articles.title: How the humble salt marsh softens the ocean’s fury
articles.summary: Researchers at Wageningen University and Research transported live salt marsh samples from the Dutch Wadden Sea to a large flume facility at the Deltares Research Institute. Testing revealed that dense root networks successfully held sediments together under severe wave action despite substantial surface flora damage. The study highlights the ecological value of coastal salt marshes as natural protective buffers against storms.
articles.description: The Hindu’s weekly Science for All newsletter explains all things Science, without the jargon

articles.headline: Incredible celebrations as last patient leaves a DRC Ebola centre
articles.title: Incredible celebrations as last patient leaves a DRC Ebola centre
articles.description: Footage shows healthcare workers celebrating at an Ebola treatment centre in DR Congo after the last patient left.

articles.headline: Minnesota fraud scheme participant Salim Said receives thirty-year prison sentence
articles.title: US man gets 30-year sentence for Minnesota fraud that drew Trump backlash
articles.summary: Salim Said, a thirty-seven-year-old restaurant operator in Minneapolis, Minnesota, received a thirty-year prison sentence for his involvement in a forty-four million dollar COVID-nineteen pandemic food programme fraud scheme. US District Judge Nancy Brasel delivered the sentence on Wednesday following a case that drew national scrutiny and intense political pressure from President Donald Trump.
articles.description: Government says Salim Said hit the jackpot in a scheme claiming to feed needy children during the COVID-19 pandemic.

articles.headline: NIMHANS neurology casualty reports high stroke patient volume in Karnataka
articles.title: 40% of patients at NIMHANS neurology casualty have stroke; KMCRI in Hubbali treats 120 cases a month
articles.summary: Nearly 40 percent of patients seeking neurological care at the NIMHANS casualty in Bengaluru are stroke victims, with 705 cases reported monthly. To address this urgent demand, a hub-and-spoke collaborative model linking NIMHANS with the Karnataka Institute of Medical Sciences and Research Institute in Hubballi helps doctors manage approximately 120 monthly stroke cases in northern districts using teleconsultation.
articles.description: Hub-and-spoke model extends specialised stroke care to northern Karnataka, reducing the need for emergency transfers to Bengaluru. World Stroke Day is observed on October 29.

articles.headline: Al Jazeera speaks to El-Sayed as religion becomes flashpoint in Senate race
articles.title: Al Jazeera speaks to El-Sayed as religion becomes flashpoint in Senate race
articles.description: Democratic candidate Abdul El-Sayed is pushing back against attacks over his Muslim faith.

articles.headline: Utah files criminal charges against prediction market Kalshi and cofounders
articles.title: Kalshi, cofounders hit with criminal charges in US state of Utah
articles.summary: Utah Attorney General Derek Brown filed criminal charges against prediction market Kalshi, CEO Tarek Mansour, and COO Luana Lopes Lara on Wednesday. The Salt Lake City court complaint accuses the platform of twelve counts of online gambling promotion and facilitating undercover sports wagers, escalating a jurisdictional showdown between state authorities and the Trump administration.
articles.description: The charges come after a federal judge ruled that Utah could enforce its anti-gambling laws against prediction markets.

articles.headline: Bolsonaro in Miami: I am the ‘true president-elect’
articles.title: Bolsonaro in Miami: I am the ‘true president-elect’
articles.description: Flavio Bolsonaro claimed to be the ‘true president-elect’ of Brazil in his first statement since fleeing to the US.

articles.headline: RSS well-wishers register RSS Friends as a foreign agent in the United States
articles.title: ‘RSS Friends’ registers in U.S. to step up outreach, correct inaccuracies
articles.summary: A group named RSS Friends has officially registered with the United States Department of Justice as a foreign agent under the Foreign Agents Registration Act. The organization lists the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh in New Delhi as its principal and aims to enhance public outreach, engage with community leaders, and correct inaccurate information regarding the India-based volunteer group.
articles.description: The RSS Friends, which provided a Georgia address in the registration document, listed Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh, Keshavkunj, New Delhi as its “foreign principal”

articles.headline: Congress candidate Abhijeet Wanjari retains Nagpur division graduates constituency seat
articles.title: In setback to BJP, Congress wins Nagpur MLC seat
articles.summary: Congress candidate Abhijeet Wanjari defeated Bharatiya Janata Party rival Sudhakar Kohale by 3,271 votes in the Nagpur Division Graduates constituency election. The victory delivers a significant political blow to the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party in the hometown of Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis and Union Minister Nitin Gadkari, following a counting process that concluded on October 29, 2026.
articles.description: The Congress fielded sitting MLC Abhijeet Wanjari, who secured 67,231 votes, while the BJP fielded former MLA Sudhakar Kohale, who secured 63,960 votes

articles.headline: Digital Personal Data Protection Act does not infringe on press freedom, says Ashwini Vaishnaw
articles.title: Digital Personal Data Protection Act does not infringe on press freedom: Ashwini Vaishnaw
articles.summary: Information Technology Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw stated on October 28, 2026, that the Digital Personal Data Protection Act protects personal data without undermining journalistic independence guaranteed by the Constitution. Addressing media concerns over investigative reporting, he invited editors for dialogue and noted that the government is open to parliamentary amendments to explicitly safeguard media activities if necessary.
articles.description: IT Minister invites editors and media professionals to engage in open dialogue with government to discuss concerns surrounding the law

articles.headline: Enforcement Directorate attaches Mohammad Ali Jauhar University land and buildings
articles.title: ED attaches land, buildings of Mohammad Ali Jauhar University in Rampur in money laundering case
articles.summary: The Enforcement Directorate provisionally attached land and buildings belonging to Mohammad Ali Jauhar University in Rampur, valued at 426.46 crore rupees with a market value of approximately 1,170 crore rupees. According to an official statement on October 28, 2026, the action falls under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act regarding a case against the Maulana Mohammad Ali Jauhar Trust and former Uttar Pradesh cabinet minister Mohammad Azam Khan.
articles.description: “ED found that funds meant for public works were diverted to the University, government works were executed on its private campus, and funds from contractors who had been allotted government contracts were routed back to the Trust as donations,” the statement said

articles.headline: Israelis rally for Jewish-Arab government after election gains
articles.title: Israelis rally for Jewish-Arab government after election gains
articles.description: Israelis rallied for a Jewish-Arab gov’t after parties representing Israel’s Arab citizens made gains in the election.

articles.headline: Romanian court extends pre-trial detention of far-right politician Calin Georgescu
articles.title: Romania extends pre-trial detention of far-right politician Calin Georgescu
articles.summary: The Bucharest Court of Appeal extended the pre-trial detention of far-right politician Calin Georgescu by thirty days during an investigation into an alleged one point one million euro fraud case. Prosecutors stated that Georgescu and two associates defrauded a businessman under the pretense of securing a credit line. Georgescu denied all wrongdoing, alleging the investigation is politically motivated, while hundreds of his supporters protested outside the court building.
articles.description: The Bucharest court has extended the pre-trial detention of Calin Georgescu by 30 days, appealing a lower court ruling.

articles.headline: Instagram head Adam Mosseri says AI negativity will worsen
articles.title: Adam Mosseri says negativity around AI is ‘going to get worse’
articles.summary: Instagram head Adam Mosseri stated in a podcast interview that public frustration, anger, and anxiety regarding artificial intelligence will continue to escalate over the coming years, driven largely by a fear of job displacement and being left behind. Speaking on the Colin and Samir podcast, Mosseri also discussed content ranking challenges, the prevalence of misleading celebrity deepfakes, and new labeling requirements for artificial intelligence accounts on the platform.
articles.description: Asked about AI and the trend of college students booing tech CEOs at graduation ceremonies, Instagram head Adam Mosseri acknowledged in an interview that a lot of people really don't like AI, and it's not just young people and creatives. Appearing on the Colin and Samir podcast to talk about the launch of widescreen and […]

articles.headline: UN experts condemn excessive police force during student protests in France
articles.title: UN experts sound alarm at excessive use of force in French student protests
articles.summary: United Nations human rights experts expressed concern on Wednesday over the disproportionate use of force and mass arrests of minors during nationwide student demonstrations in France. Protests began in mid-September over high school conditions, living costs, and budget cuts under President Emmanuel Macron, drawing 410,000 participants on Saturday according to the interior ministry. The crackdown left multiple injuries, including a teenager who lost a hand in Lille.
articles.description: UN experts have condemned police crackdowns, warning they deter demonstrators from exercising their rights.

articles.headline: Costa Rica opens new maximum-security prison built with Salvadoran assistance
articles.title: Costa Rica’s mega-prison receives first inmates
articles.summary: Costa Rica's Justice Ministry announced the intake of the first 123 inmates at the newly inaugurated High-Containment Center Against Organized Crime on October 15. Built with Salvadoran assistance on the outskirts of San Jose at a cost of $35m, the 5,100-capacity facility aims to address prison overcrowding. Justice Minister Gabriel Aguilar stated the facility supports President Laura Fernandez's firm stance against rising organized crime and drug trafficking violence.
articles.description: President Laura Fernandez inaugurated the $35m mega-prison built to house up to 5,100 inmates near San Jose.

articles.headline: Indonesian students demand action on wildfires and rising costs
articles.title: Indonesian students demand action on wildfires and rising costs
articles.description: Hundreds of Indonesian students protested against the government's handling of forest fires and rising costs.

articles.headline: Upper caste candidates dominate Bihar legislative council election results
articles.title: Bihar MLC polls: Upper caste candidates dominate election results
articles.summary: Upper-caste candidates secured six out of eight seats in the Bihar State Legislative Council elections held on October 23, 2026. Bhumihar candidates won five seats, while a Rajput candidate won one, with victories split across ruling and opposition parties. Additionally, Other Backward Class and Extremely Backward Class candidates secured one seat each, while the opposition Congress party failed to win any of the contested positions.
articles.description: The Opposition Congress party which had put up its candidates on five seats has failed to win even a single seat in the elections

articles.headline: Flavio Bolsonaro arrives in Miami after presidential run-off election defeat
articles.title: What’s next for Brazil’s Flavio Bolsonaro after election defeat?
articles.summary: Far-right Senator Flavio Bolsonaro and his family arrived in Miami, Florida on Wednesday following his defeat in Brazil presidential run-off election against incumbent Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva. Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes had ordered him to surrender his passports amid a money laundering investigation. Meanwhile, US President Donald Trump claimed without evidence that the election was rigged.
articles.description: The far-right ally of US President Donald Trump has fled to Miami with his wife and children.

articles.headline: National Democratic Alliance secures four seats in Bihar Legislative Council polls
articles.title: Bihar MLC polls: NDA close to win 4 out of 8 seats
articles.summary: Election results for six out of eight seats have been declared in the Bihar Legislative Council polls held across graduate and teachers constituencies. The National Democratic Alliance is set to win four seats, while independent candidates and the Jan Suraaj Party also secured victories. Janata Dal United candidate Neeraj Kumar won his fourth consecutive term from the Patna Graduate constituency.
articles.description: All sitting MLCs of the Teachers constituency lost the election, whereas Janata Dal (United) candidate Neeraj Kumar retained his Patna Graduate Constituency

articles.headline: Jan Suraaj Party secures first victory in Bihar Legislative Council elections
articles.title: Bihar MLC polls: Jan Suraaj Party opens account, JD(U)'s Neeraj Kumar 'wins' Patna Graduates seat
articles.summary: The Jan Suraaj Party opened its account in the Bihar Legislative Council elections as candidate Suresh Prasad Rai defeated sitting Congress member Madan Mohan Jha on Wednesday. Polling took place on October twenty-third with a turnout of eighty-two percent in teachers constituencies and fifty-three percent in graduates seats. Leaders from various parties reacted to the outcomes while highlighting regional issues.
articles.description: In the Patna Graduates constituency, JD(U)'s Neeraj Kumar has defeated the RJD candidate, though official results for the seat are yet to be declared

articles.headline: SAD and AAP trade barbs over Punjab drug menace issue
articles.title: SAD-AAP trade barbs on drug menace issue in Punjab
articles.summary: Political tensions intensified in Punjab as the Aam Aadmi Party and Shiromani Akali Dal exchanged sharp accusations regarding narcotics trafficking ahead of the 2027 Assembly election. The dispute followed a supplementary chargesheet filed by the Punjab Vigilance Bureau against senior Akali Dal leader Bikram Singh Majithia, alleging he accumulated substantial wealth through illicit drug sales.
articles.description: SAD leader Bikram Singh Majithia accused Arvind Kejriwal of misleading Punjabis by giving the disproportionate assets case the label of a drug case to suppress the issue

articles.headline: Lawyers protest against judge, causing chaos at Allahabad High Court
articles.title: Furniture thrown, proceedings disrupted as lawyers’ protest against HC judge turns chaotic
articles.summary: Advocates engaged in disruptive protests inside an Allahabad High Court courtroom, throwing furniture toward the dais during a hearing conducted by Justice Arun Kumar Singh Deshwal. The demonstration erupted over allegations that a lawyer was mistreated by another judge, prompting the Bench to order a report for potential disciplinary and contempt proceedings.
articles.description: The conduct of the lawyers prompted the court to consider disciplinary and contempt proceedings against those involved

articles.headline: Mumbai police re-arrest 11 accused under MCOCA in actor firing case
articles.title: Tiger Shroff firing case: 11 accused re-arrested under MCOCA after court grants permission
articles.summary: Mumbai Crime Branch officials re-arrested eleven suspects under the stringent Maharashtra Control of Organised Crime Act following authorization from a special court. The accused are linked to an October 18 incident involving gunfire directed at actor Tiger Shroff’s car in Juhu, an attack allegedly orchestrated by associates of jailed gangster Lawrence Bishnoi.
articles.description: The accused were produced before the special MCOCA court on October 28, a day after the Mumbai Crime Branch invoked provisions of the Act against them

articles.headline: Kavitha threatens to block census operations over OBC column demands
articles.title: Kavitha threatens to block census operations over OBC column demand
articles.summary: Telangana Rakshana Sena chief Kalvakuntla Kavitha threatened to obstruct upcoming census activities in Telangana unless authorities implement a dedicated Other Backward Classes column with standardised caste coding. Speaking at an association meeting in Hyderabad, she urged the State government to pass a legislative resolution supporting comprehensive nationwide caste enumeration and proportionate representation.
articles.description: Hyderabad Declaration adopts nine resolutions on caste census, reservations

articles.headline: Boston federal jury convicts Rwandan American man of perjury and obstruction
articles.title: US jury convicts Rwandan American of lying about role in genocide
articles.summary: A federal jury in Boston convicted Eric Nshimiye of four counts of perjury and one charge of obstruction of justice regarding his involvement in the 1994 Rwandan genocide. Prosecutors stated the 55-year-old United States citizen lied during a 2019 trial and on immigration paperwork. Defence lawyers argued inconsistencies in witness testimonies. Nshimiye faces sentencing while his family sought a different outcome.
articles.description: Jurors heard competing witness testimony on where Eric Nshimiye was and what he was doing in April 1994.

articles.headline: Students on hunger strike in India demand restoration of student union
articles.title: Students on hunger strike in India demand restoration of student union
articles.description: Students at New Delhi’s Jamia Millia Islamia university are on hunger strike demanding a student union.

articles.headline: How did Flávio Bolsonaro end up in Miami?
articles.title: How did Flávio Bolsonaro end up in Miami?
articles.description: BBC Verify has pieced together defeated presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro's journey through Brazil, Argentina and Ecuador to reach Miami.

articles.headline: Microsoft ends Copilot support on LG and Samsung smart televisions
articles.title: Microsoft is ending Copilot support on smart TVs
articles.summary: Microsoft is terminating Copilot support across all smart televisions during 2026, according to an on-screen notification discovered on an LG television. The artificial intelligence assistant previously provided chat functions and content recommendations on devices made by LG and Samsung. Microsoft recently shifted the assistant toward business tools, while LG previously faced user backlash over unremovable shortcuts.
articles.description: Nearly two years after LG and Samsung announced at CES 2025 that their latest smart TVs would include access to Microsoft's Copilot, the company is ending support for the AI assistant's functionality on all TVs this year, according to a report by Windows Central. The news comes not from an official announcement from LG, Samsung, […]

articles.headline: Balad leader Sami Abu Shehadeh condemns exclusion of Arab parties in Israel
articles.title: Balad leader blasts ‘racist’ exclusion of Arab parties in Israel
articles.summary: Balad party leader Sami Abu Shehadeh has condemned Israeli political leaders for refusing to form a coalition with Arab parties despite a record performance in polls. Arab parties are projected to win 19 seats. Abu Shehadeh criticized the exclusion as racism while speaking to Al Jazeera. Meanwhile, a United Nations commission reported that Israel has continued committing genocide in Gaza.
articles.description: Elections have yielded no clear winner but opposition bloc refuses to ally with Arab parties.

articles.headline: Myanmar diplomat breaks down as he urges world to 'end our suffering'
articles.title: Myanmar diplomat breaks down as he urges world to 'end our suffering'
articles.description: Kyaw Moe Tun - Myanmar's representative to the UN - makes an emotional appeal after saying the international community had failed the country's people.

articles.headline: Border clash between Afghanistan and Pakistan kills one and injures five
articles.title: Afghan-Pakistan border clash kills one, injures five
articles.summary: A cross-border clash in the market town of Angoor Adda left one person dead and five injured on Wednesday, according to officials in Pakistan. The South Waziristan district administration blamed the incident on unprovoked mortar fire from Afghanistan, prompting Pakistani forces to respond with artillery. Pakistan and Afghanistan have experienced sporadic fighting since a truce in March following earlier conflict.
articles.description: The countries went to war earlier this year and, with no permanent resolution reached on security issues, there have been sporadic attacks since a March truce

articles.headline: MP Vikramjit Singh Sahney urges Union government to reopen Kartarpur corridor
articles.title: BJP MP seeks reopening of Kartarpur corridor, Amit Shah inaugurates exhibition to mark 25 years of Modi’s public service
articles.summary: Rajya Sabha member Vikramjit Singh Sahney urged the Union government on Wednesday to reopen the Kartarpur corridor before next month. The corridor links shrines in Punjab and Pakistan and has remained closed since the Pahalgam terror attack on April 22, 2025. Sahney raised the issue with Union Home Minister Amit Shah during an event in New Delhi marking twenty-five years of Prime Minister Narendra Modi's public service.
articles.description: Rajya Sabha member Vikramjit Singh Sahney says Prime Minister Narendra Modi deserves the Bharat Ratna for his dedication and service to nation

articles.headline: Madhya Pradesh police arrest eleventh suspect in Dewas spurious liquor case
articles.title: M.P. hooch deaths: prime accused used AI to help brew liquor at home, say police
articles.summary: Police in Dewas arrested Aman Kasliwal on October 28, 2026, for allegedly supplying chemicals used to manufacture illicit liquor linked to thirteen deaths in Chandana and Binjana villages since September 27. Officials stated that prime accused Ajay Rathore used artificial intelligence to learn mixing formulae. Meanwhile, the district excise officer was suspended for gross negligence, and top officials were transferred.
articles.description: A total of 11 people have been arrested so far, amid allegations surfacing of over 10 deaths due to spurious liquor in a month in two villages of Dewas district in Madhya Pradesh

articles.headline: Sudan war and inflation leave Khartoum families struggling to buy food
articles.title: Sudan war and inflation leave families struggling to survive in Khartoum
articles.summary: Families in Khartoum are struggling to survive amid soaring food prices and severe inflation driven by the ongoing war between the Sudanese military and the Rapid Support Forces. According to the Central Bureau of Statistics, national prices rose by twenty-eight percent in September compared to the previous year. The conflict has severely damaged infrastructure, disrupted supply chains, and forced millions from their homes.
articles.description: Soaring food prices and shrinking incomes force families in Sudan's capital to borrow money and skip meals.

articles.headline: Vedanta chairperson Anil Agarwal explores investments in West Bengal
articles.title: Vedanta chief meets Suvendu, explores investments in West Bengal
articles.summary: Vedanta Group chairperson Anil Agarwal met with Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari in Kolkata on Wednesday to explore investments worth approximately seventy thousand crore rupees in West Bengal. Agarwal stated that the company plans to invest in power generation and an aluminum smelter plant if it receives active administrative support. Adhikari noted that the proposed project in Asansol could potentially generate up to ten thousand jobs.
articles.description: Anil Agarwal says he will leave no stone unturned to invest in Bengal if the right opportunity presents itself; CM says the industrialist made a specific proposal to set up a unit in Asansol
